Gameplay, Tropico 4 doesn't delve too far from the generic mechanics of a city building simulation genre. You manage your city/nation's economy, monitor the population, provide housing, food, services and employment, and construct buildings for some of their other needs such as healthcare and spirituality.
The definitive characteristic of this one's you'll be tasked to focus on one island and only one island at a time (unlike in Anno where you can build on other nearby islands, here, other islands are almost non-existent). There's also balance on this one in terms of freedom on how you want to run your island. You have options on where to run your economy, be it Tourism or other forms of industry chains.
Another strong selling point of this game's the dialogue, the humor is strong in this one. I hope I can also befriend someone from the Middle East who promises me a camel but sends me 30,000 USD on my way instead. Something his wives found while cleaning the couch.
Visuals, score and other things, nothing really stands out here.
So, yeah. I'd give this one a commend. Buy the DLC's too, if you can. I heard they make the game a little more rounded with options.

Graphically, this game is stunning, almost flawless. Every bike is faithfully reproduced down to the last nut. Tracks are also well rendered, exhibiting most of the nuances you would expect to come across, without being completely anal. The bikes handle well, and differently according to each bike's particular characteristics - no mean feat considering you're probably sitting there with nothing more than a big plastic M in your hands.
Caveats? Well, there is an issue with framerate stuttering, which has been around for some time - running with vsync enabled does help a lot, but it is something the develpers need to address. Some also complain that the sound isn't that realistic, but that's a minor niggle. Tracks are, unfortunately, somewhat limited but not enough to induce boredom. Online doesn't seem to be great (I have only looked briefly at that, but options to race against others doesn't seem to be as supported as some YouTube channels might have you believe - though a group of friends hosting their own races might negate that.
Basically, if you're a biker, who is looking for a motorcycle game/sim, this is probably about as good as it will ever get. There's much to enjoy, little to whinge over and, all things considered, it's by far the best playing and looking motorcycle game available.

A shockingly good little motorcycle game.
I'd nibbled about on some of this developers' previous efforts but they had left me largely unimpressed. The buzz wasn't very positive for any of their previous attempts really either so it was very surprising to find myself plugging as much time into this one as I have.
A small confession: I do ride IRL and have the grace to own several motorcycles although none at competition level. But trust me when I say that when you hear the street triple fire up in the frontend of the game it IS a Triumph triple. It is that attention to the little details that sucked me in in spite of dated graphics, sometimes glitchy framerate and questionable AI and physics. When the 675r tries to ground loop on me at the 'ring in second gear, when I'm actually "out there" and not focusing on the fact that it's a game controller and I can "see" into the apexes like we do IRL and set up for the corners, that's when this game shines. The physics since I've mentioned them are surprisingly good except for some apparent AI indelicacies in the name of catching up and where they will choose to path when bunched up. Physics are always moot with games as there is NO proper way to convey anyways, even Sega's Hang On was just a plastic bike that leaned.
Another really cool aspect of this game is that the bikes are actually unique besides just the soundset and a paint job. Two strokes run flat out just like IRL and even have the characteristic fat spot in the power band . And yes, customizing them ala Gran Turismo is very similar. In fact that game is most directly "like" this game for its' portrayal of auto sports. The Devs obviously have patterned this a bit after that title and it shows. Which gives me a reason to actually play the thing I guess which probably explains why I like this one enough to make it my first review.
Now on to the Warts:
Multiplayer. Haven't gone in myself as I've heard it's abysmal but I can well imagine. I've had a couple of their previous titles and multiplayer reliability is not too hot. Then again these games don't sell to Yankees like me generally so US internet bias might be a factor, but I don't know.
Graphics. These are fairly OK. They work well up to about 1920 but the source stuff gets a bit too blocky up past that and then again let's not talk about the
FRAME RATE- Seriously,???!!! - I've got a Haswell 4790 @4.4, 32Gb matched,tested memory and a 1080GTX so you "think" I might avoid stutters. No such luck here though, once the traffic stacks up at Monza I'm in the teens and jerky. Still playing with settings though and most of the time it runs well with only an occasional hiccup. But for what amounts to PS3 gen graphics it's weak.
Controls- As I said nothing short of a full 360 degree strapped on moving platform with projection could get close so that is kind of moot. Still I suppose some folks won't be happy that you can't use anything but a 360 wireless or Steam controller but there it is. Doesn't see my Logitech wheel at all and I'm not too sure about my Thrustmaster stuff.
Now onto the good again to recap:
Variety- Even without any DLC there is a LOT of content. I at no time felt obligated to purchase something else to progress- I was able to advance quite easily with upgrades and bikes available in the base game which seems to be a rare thing nowadays.
Individual "feel" and character of the bikes- This is probably the biggest single reason I'm playing. By this I mean that obviously some time was taken to convey a good many of each bike's individual little nuances and quirks. Such as the tendency for the Daytona to ground loop easily in second, the way the power kicks in mid to 3/4s throttle on the little Honda smoker or the way the street triple sounds when stated, these details make the game.
Controls: Funny, huh? But although you are stuck with it the wireless controller works well for this. There is a report of someone getting a new PS4 controller to work via Bluetooth so as to get the tilt function to steer ala Drive Club Bikes but I don't know how myself and have little inclination as I don't steer that way even in that title.
Tracks- It comes with quite a few and should keep you busy for a while. They are pretty well represented for whatever discipline you are into and I still haven't ridden them all. There "might" be a mod that lets you import all the tracks from Valentino Rossi The Game as well if you happen to own that title. It is/was available on Racedepartment. The textures are far from the likes of Assetto Corsa or Project Cars but they convey their various locations well and aren't distractingly bad.
In short it is a fairly decent little catch-all motorcycle title with a broad base of appeal to people who might be interested in motorcycles. No Isle Of Man or TT, but a worthy title with a bunch of different types of bike all under one all-inclusive sim-light umbrella. A bit of something for most everybody if you will. The AI while not brilliant is at least challenging and manage to follow the line fairly accurately and provide some challenge to you. The bikes are many and varied from hipster bobbers to full on GP grade assault machines. The DLC isn't onerous. If you are a motorcyclist just go buy it already to drool on the bikes you will never own. Just like Gran Turismo.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown and its addons are de facto re-issue the game UFO Defence game 1993 year edition. Established Firaxis Games and published by 2K new game turned out pretty not bad. The basic details and the scenario were simply transferred from the 1993 year game: as the war with the aliens, turn-based tactics, tactical role-playing elements.
   The mission of the player is protection the planet from alien attacks, their operations on the ground and in the air. For ground operations under player control will be a special detachment. It is replenished by hiring for the money, so long as you have money and you will have recruits. But a large number of detachment on base  senselessly because the operation can only use a limited number of soldiers 5 in the original game; 6 in addon Enemy Within. After successful operations soldiers who took part in the operation may be promoted in rank then become available new options and opportunities. The game has 4 classes of soldiers, -heavy infantry, support, assault, sniper and unique class - psionic - a soldier who has psionic abilities. The soldiers of different classes differently armed and have different skills. What classes to use depends on the player and his chosen tactics. Battle goes step by step: the player and the enemy take turns. During the battle each fighter can perform two actions (move / open fire / reload weapon / etc.). To win, the player has to fulfill the mission goal (to clean the area from aliens, rescue civilians or hostage). Enemy are various forms of aliens - their number, skills and capacity increases according to the game walkthrough. To destroy alien aircraft,  XCOM need to buy aircrafts, but unlike the recruits its construction takes time.
The player has a secret base. In a bunker is a research center, engineering department, a command post, a hangar for XCOM aviation, satellite control center, barracks, etc. The player decides which conduct research, what structures build, what type of equipment use for soldiers who will took part in operation. Project XCOM financed by 16 countries. Due to aliens attack, if XCOM ignore countries request of help, country can leave project. If 8 countries leave project - player lose.
   Since the game is turn-based tactics not possible not to pay attention to the entourage of battles in XCOM. The battles with aliens take place throughout the planet and the question remains, why the location is almost indistinguishable from one another. The same cars, houses, people in Beijing, in London, in Cairo, in Lagos. This is pathetic, seems what game was created not a company with over 100 man crew, but several people who raised money on kickstarter.
   Despite some disadvantages, the game still came worthy sequel to the original game of 1993.

Get this game only if you like hardcore roguelike games that doesn't give you any slake. While I enjoyed the fact that this game seemed to be a love letter to Fallout 1/2 with it's turnstyle controls and combat, the luck factor in this game will often be against you if you are starting out. You will die a LOT in the first playthroughs, but if you retain your experiences from those playthroughs you'll be able to survive long enough to progress on the storyline.
It is a good survival game that is worth the price but my only complaints are that it feels a bit empty what with only a handful of locations to visit on a giant map. There are random encounters, but most of the time, they tend to be to your disadvantage unless you save beforehand. The major thing is that this game has permadeath ie. you lose EVERYTHING when you die...including your savefile. Unless you manage to make a backup of your savefile, you will have to start at the beginning everytime you die and that will be the breaking point for gamers interested in getting this.
Finally, my last grip is that there will be no new content added to the game by the creator. However, there is a growing Mod community for the game an the creator made the game itself to be moddable. Hell you can even play around with the xml file of the game itself to adjust the game to your liking, though you'll have to go to the game's forums to learn more on that.
All in all, if you enjoy survival turnbased games dealing with post-apocalypse and supernatural themes with good story, crafting and (more importanly) mods to extend the game , then buy this. If not, then Project Zomboid might be more your thing.

Before writing down a review, My main 3d workflows are (exclude post-processing tools like Nuke, Fusion, etc., only for modeling and texturing) use 3dsmax, Maya, Cinema 4D, Houdini, Mari, MODO and blender.
If you are new to 3D modeling include texturing, I strongly recommend use blender as your first 3D tool; There are lots of 3D creation tools on Steam, such as MODO, Maya LT, etc., those for indies. More than that Blender is free and quite easy and powerful IMO so far.
Tools don't matter to what to you create. Once you understand how the polygon worlds are working, It's still not too late to switch to other 3d programs or stay on Blender. Each tool has their pros and cons. and if Blender is not enough for you; if so, it's your choice to switch or not.
The only problem is Steam won't allow you to run multiple instances of blenders! You rather use standalone version from official blender website to use multiple instances.
tl;dr: If you want to make smth /w 3D but you don't know what to start? Use blender as your starting 3d tool to learn 3D.

Тим — абсолютный эгоцентрик, запертый в себе, неспособный на сопереживание или отождествление себя с другими, на любовь, дружбу, влечение или нежность. Он является абсолютно изолированной единицей, неспособной на взаимоотношения с кем-либо. Его реакции направлены внутрь, они не относятся к мыслительным процессам; его разум — просто инструмент для обслуживания собственных страстей и потребностей; он не способен к полету мысли, обмену идеями; он не соотносит себя ни с чем, кроме собственных физических ощущений. Он — полумертвая, ни на что не реагирующая масса, неспособная давать или получать удовольствие или счастье; соответственно, он, в лучшем случае, абсолютно скучное явление, безобидное пятно, поскольку только те, кто способны воспринимать и принимать других, обладают очарованием. Он застрял на полпути в сумеречной зоне между человеком и обезьяной, но гораздо хуже обезьян, поскольку, в отличие от них, способен испытывать множество негативных чувств — ненависть, ревность, позор, отвращение, вину, стыд, сомнение; более того, он осознает, что он такое, и чего ему недостает.
Обуреваемый чувством вины, страхами, стыдом и неуверенностью, обладая, если удается, едва заметными физическими ощущениями, Тим, тем не менее, полностью захвачен желанием ебаться; он переплывет море соплей, перейдет вброд глубокую лужу блевотины величиной в милю, если будет думать, что там его ждет любезная «киска». Он выебет женщину, которую презирает, любую беззубую ведьму, и даже заплатит за это. Почему? Снятие физического напряжения — это не ответ, поскольку для него достаточно мастурбации. Нельзя объяснить это и удовлетворением самолюбия, иначе он не ебал бы детей и трупы.
Абсолютно эгоистичный, не способный реагировать, сочувствовать, отождествлять себя с другими, наполненный до краев необъятной, всепроникающей, всепоглощающей сексуальностью, он физически пассивен. Он ненавидит свою пассивность, поэтому считает, что она свойственна женщинам, а мужчины — активны, а затем пытается доказывать, что он существует («доказывать, что он — Мужчина»). Главный его способ доказать это — ебля.

- Overcooked is a party game that anyone can pick up on the go. The controls are straight forward and the gameplay is quite intuitive.
- I like that you can play on both keyboard and controller at the same time. Or two people can share one controller/keyboard. The developers really thought about making this game more accessible to more simultaneous players.
- I really enjoyed the different levels and the different gimmicks in each one. You’re expected to have a different game plan for each kitchen and to improvise as things start to go wrong. Overcooked is challenging but not to the point of frustration.
- I found the game to be quite forgiving. When food is about to burn, you are given a warning way in advance (I think around 4 seconds?) so you have plenty of time to react. Food doesn’t spoil, even if you cook it way in advance. You can throw ingredients and plates on the floor and nothing will happen. This game is chaotic enough, so I appreciate that the developers did not overcomplicate the cooking part.
- Only local co-op. I find it such a shame when co-op centric games do not include online multiplayer.
- You don’t stand a chance if you’re playing single player. For some reason the chopping takes roughly twice as long if you’re playing alone.
-This game works on a star system. You can gain up to three stars depending on your performance on a level. I found it somewhat annoying that later levels require you to have a certain amount of stars before you can play them. However, at the same time I can understand the reasoning behind this. Levels get progressively harder (kitchen layout, gimmicks, recipes) so you are expected to reach a certain mastery level before you can progress.
- I only disliked one level. In this level you are stuck on a platform floating on top of lava and the stoves are on mini platforms rotating around your platform. Creatively designed, but not very fun to play.
- This is a small detail but all the players connected can control the bus (you drive around in a bus to select a level). This leads to some chaotic driving that can either be hilarious or frustrating. I hope the people you are playing with aren’t trolls.
It is clear that Overcooked was designed to be a co-op experience. I would not recommend buying this game if you plan on playing it alone. The levels are chaotic and coordinating with your fellow players is harder than it looks. Having said that, be prepared to have fun while making mistakes.

Well well well, what do we have here? Another Relic RTS in my reviews? Fear not, viewer, as this one will be mostly positive.
Now then, let's start things off, shall we? As far as the story goes.. well, I could care less about it. Go here, talk a bit, fight guys. Go there, talk a bit, fight guys. Go to another place, talk a bit, surprising revelation and/or plot twist, fight guys, emerge victorious. 1: The game (Like a lot of WH40k titles.) fails to realize that Space Marines are not the good guys. Nobody is. Except maybe the Eldar. 2: The voice acting is incredible. The story does have cutscenes.. but they are god awful. Let's just say I'd rather watch PS1 FMV than these "cutscenes." I will cut this game some slack, as it came out in the early 2000s, but some things, such as these cutscenes, are inexcusably terrible.
I will point out that this game actually nails strategy right on the head. Each race is well balanced and has their own special perks, strategies and weaknesses.. unless you're playing as Orks. Just.. just don't play as Orks. (Please note that this is the GoTY edition, and not any of the DLCs where balance gets thrown out the window.) While on the subject, I will point out that the different units in this game are very impressive, sporting many different infantry and vehicles from Warhammer 40,000 lore. Still on gameplay, you will notice there are two major types of units you can build: The more combat-oriented ranged units and the frontline first-to-die melee units. Ranged units are generally preferable over the latter, but melee units can also disrupt ranged infantry and force them into melee combat - not exactly a ranged unit's strong suit. Melee units are also typically more durable than their ranged counterparts, as the Space Marine Dreadnoughts have armor so thick it's like trying to punch a hole through a cereal box using nothing but packing peanuts. Some infantry and vehicles can be equipped with weaponry to make them more effective against certain targets. Take the Predator for example. It is a sturdy battle tank with side-mounted heavy bolters and a small main cannon effective against infantry. By default, it is an infantry annihilator, but it can be upgraded to rock lascannons on every firing port it has, transforming it into a vehicle obliterator. Take note that  most weapons effective against infantry will not do much against vehicles, and vice versa. Refer to my cereal box and packing peanuts metaphor.
The graphics are dated, but still acceptable nonetheless. This game came out in '04, so this is fine by me. Everything looks like how it should.
The soundtrack is pretty nice, having good battle themes and whatnot. But it's mainly the voice acting I would like to cover in this section. As I said before, the voice acting in this game is surprisingly well done. I cannot get Gabriel Angelos's voice out of my head. Every race has their own 'attitude' towards seeing you as their commander - Space Marines and Eldar have somewhat British accents (I say somewhat because a lot of Space Marine units like Dreadnoughts and Assault Marines have American accents, while Scout Marines have British ones.) and respect you and would die for you as their leader, Chaos worship you as their lord and speak in an angry and sometimes panicked tone 24/7, and Orks constantly question your leadership and will often insult you when you simply select a unit; also, the way they butcher the English language is just... beautiful to witness. Props to Relic on the voice acting front!
This game does have a fair amount of DLC, but it is quite affordable. Buying this game plus all of it's DLCs doesn't put it above 60 U.S. dollars, so the price is pretty good even with like two of the DLCs. One more thing about the DLCs I will mention in this review is that all of this game's DLCs are playable as standalone games. Yes, you heard me right. Granted, you will only have one or two races depending on which DLC you bought, but it is a really cool feature in my book.
Dawn of War runs pretty smoothly on my PC, but watch it with the multiplayer connection; it can get laggy at times.
The battles Dawn of War offers are great to spark and even greater to see. They aren't massive scale like Supreme Commander: Forged Alliance, but they aren't overly tactical like this game's sequel. The map sizes fit these battles appropriately, and everything seems like a legitimate battlefield, minus the running for cover part.
TL;DR: Dawn of War has it's flaws, but in general it is a solid RTS with great potential. I think the RTS genre is where the Warhammer 40,000 franchise would fit perfectly, and Relic has proven this. If you love strategy games or WH40k, go ahead and give this a shot.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown and its addons are de facto re-issue the game UFO Defence game 1993 year edition. Established Firaxis Games and published by 2K new game turned out pretty not bad. The basic details and the scenario were simply transferred from the 1993 year game: as the war with the aliens, turn-based tactics, tactical role-playing elements.
   The mission of the player is protection the planet from alien attacks, their operations on the ground and in the air. For ground operations under player control will be a special detachment. It is replenished by hiring for the money, so long as you have money and you will have recruits. But a large number of detachment on base  senselessly because the operation can only use a limited number of soldiers 5 in the original game; 6 in addon Enemy Within. After successful operations soldiers who took part in the operation may be promoted in rank then become available new options and opportunities. The game has 4 classes of soldiers, -heavy infantry, support, assault, sniper and unique class - psionic - a soldier who has psionic abilities. The soldiers of different classes differently armed and have different skills. What classes to use depends on the player and his chosen tactics. Battle goes step by step: the player and the enemy take turns. During the battle each fighter can perform two actions (move / open fire / reload weapon / etc.). To win, the player has to fulfill the mission goal (to clean the area from aliens, rescue civilians or hostage). Enemy are various forms of aliens - their number, skills and capacity increases according to the game walkthrough. To destroy alien aircraft,  XCOM need to buy aircrafts, but unlike the recruits its construction takes time.
The player has a secret base. In a bunker is a research center, engineering department, a command post, a hangar for XCOM aviation, satellite control center, barracks, etc. The player decides which conduct research, what structures build, what type of equipment use for soldiers who will took part in operation. Project XCOM financed by 16 countries. Due to aliens attack, if XCOM ignore countries request of help, country can leave project. If 8 countries leave project - player lose.
   Since the game is turn-based tactics not possible not to pay attention to the entourage of battles in XCOM. The battles with aliens take place throughout the planet and the question remains, why the location is almost indistinguishable from one another. The same cars, houses, people in Beijing, in London, in Cairo, in Lagos. This is pathetic, seems what game was created not a company with over 100 man crew, but several people who raised money on kickstarter.
   Despite some disadvantages, the game still came worthy sequel to the original game of 1993.
    
7/10

Open-source 3D authoring software by Blender Foundation is now available for Steam. Blender is a free and very good alternative for creation of models, compositing and general editing. Blender offers GPU accelerated rendering (use your GPU to accelerate rendering), VSE (Video Sequence Editor, a NLE editor like Sony Vegas), smoke & fire simulations, liquid simulations, complex particle simulations, physics simulations, ability to develop games (Blender Game Engine), ability to use dynamic topology for seamless sculpting, supports very high resolution texturing, ability to export many formats (with and without the addons), rigging, vertex painting, weight painting, A.O, G.I, support for many different rendering methods (Yafaray, Luxrender, Blender Render, Blender Cycles, V-Ray and many more!) and it has a plethora of builds with unique features and addons.
Blender is quite the exceptional piece of open source software. Programmed with a focus on industrial quality rendering and modeling and is a great starter point for any budding person(s) or professionals to evovle their skills in 3D authoring or CAD. Many independent artists can be found on
showcasing their grand works.
It is used in many of VALVe's games to generate skins, models and even maps with the right knowledge and scripting thus can be beneficial for those who seek to earn money from their artistic use from Blender.

If you like RTS where your weakest unit can last longer than 1 second and tough units are mean to be tough (they'll last longer than 5 seconds even when things are really intenses, and will win a 1v20 against weak units), then this game is for you.
Quite easy to start with (Game Tutorial for beginner), Dawn of War 1 is a classical "build your base, create your army and crush your opponents" game, where you can get both a high amount of units and "Nokia" units (yeah, you won't be able to take them down in less than 10 seconds unless you have enough dakka).
The skirmish setting gives you the opportunity to choose between different victory condition (ex : annihilate the enemy, kill the enemy's leader, get enough ressources, ...).
If you already played to a Blizzard RTS (Warcraft 3 or Starcraft), you'll discover a new way to get ressources : forget everything about harvesting ressources. Ressources increase automatically : build a Generator, and you'll get Energy over time (+10/sec for each generator, but you'll get 1 energy each 0.1 second). The more you build generator, the faster you'll get Energy (and they'll continue giving ressources, until you or your enemy destroy them). Thus you don't have to worry about "units harvesting ressources" or "exhausting all the map ressources" : just focus on the battle and use your ressources wisely.
This game also has memorable ambient music (look out for «Blood Ravens Approach») and nice sync kills too, especially when a heavy unit "crushes" smaller units.
Edit : Forgot to mention it, but effectiveness and ineffectiveness (between units) are really applied in this game (a sniper can easily one hit kill an infantry or deal 300 damages to a heavy infantry, but try it out on a building and you'll do less than 20 damages).

Тим — абсолютный эгоцентрик, запертый в себе, неспособный на сопереживание или отождествление себя с другими, на любовь, дружбу, влечение или нежность. Он является абсолютно изолированной единицей, неспособной на взаимоотношения с кем-либо. Его реакции направлены внутрь, они не относятся к мыслительным процессам; его разум — просто инструмент для обслуживания собственных страстей и потребностей; он не способен к полету мысли, обмену идеями; он не соотносит себя ни с чем, кроме собственных физических ощущений. Он — полумертвая, ни на что не реагирующая масса, неспособная давать или получать удовольствие или счастье; соответственно, он, в лучшем случае, абсолютно скучное явление, безобидное пятно, поскольку только те, кто способны воспринимать и принимать других, обладают очарованием. Он застрял на полпути в сумеречной зоне между человеком и обезьяной, но гораздо хуже обезьян, поскольку, в отличие от них, способен испытывать множество негативных чувств — ненависть, ревность, позор, отвращение, вину, стыд, сомнение; более того, он осознает, что он такое, и чего ему недостает.
Обуреваемый чувством вины, страхами, стыдом и неуверенностью, обладая, если удается, едва заметными физическими ощущениями, Тим, тем не менее, полностью захвачен желанием ебаться; он переплывет море соплей, перейдет вброд глубокую лужу блевотины величиной в милю, если будет думать, что там его ждет любезная «киска». Он выебет женщину, которую презирает, любую беззубую ведьму, и даже заплатит за это. Почему? Снятие физического напряжения — это не ответ, поскольку для него достаточно мастурбации. Нельзя объяснить это и удовлетворением самолюбия, иначе он не ебал бы детей и трупы.
Абсолютно эгоистичный, не способный реагировать, сочувствовать, отождествлять себя с другими, наполненный до краев необъятной, всепроникающей, всепоглощающей сексуальностью, он физически пассивен. Он ненавидит свою пассивность, поэтому считает, что она свойственна женщинам, а мужчины — активны, а затем пытается доказывать, что он существует («доказывать, что он — Мужчина»). Главный его способ доказать это — ебля.

After hours of hard work and days of in-game hard-earned survival, I was well off: a cart to carry all of my heavy items that would bog me down in combat, two compound bows stocked with arrows (enough to take down pretty much anything before it even knew what hit it), enough provisions to last until judgement day, and my trusty spear should things get a little too close for comfort. I set up camp for the night in a dense bit of brush, threw together a lean-to using a tarp I took off the corpse of some raider who thought he'd take me for all I was worth, laid out my sleeping bag, and went down for the night.
Around 2 AM I was awoken by a massive *crack* in the woods near my position. Suddenly I remembered forgetting to hide my tracks, that's how it found me: a savage creature the size of a truck with teeth and claws protruding like foot-long razors. It saw me before I saw it, and that was all it took. Its claws tore across my chest before I knew where the danger was coming from sending blood flying all over the campsite along with what focus my eyes had achieved in the 5 seconds since their rude awakening. I was able to bring up my spear before the next attack landed and sliced open the creature's powerful arm, interrupting its strike. Vision fading quickly, I lunged. The beast let loose a shriek as the spear found its mark and dove deeper, piercing the heart. I'm not sure what gave out first, my legs or the crumpled heap of what was once the hulking black monstrosity.
Somehow I dragged myself to my backpack and fished out some rags. I quickly bandaged the massive gash in my chest, ever mindful that giving in to the swirling blackness meant never waking up. I popped a couple of strong painkillers and some antibiotics to ward off the inevitable infection that comes with a reused bandage (like there was any other choice) and retreated back into the safety of my lean-to to rest and give my wounds time to heal.
I must have dozed off, I'm not sure, all I remember is the pain. The incredible pain that only follows a crowbar being slammed into your knee.
Two thugs stood over me, wearing what appeared to be the mismatched hides of dozens of small animals. I didn't even have time to cry out in pain before the the bigger of the two brought his crowbar down again, silencing me permanently.
My vision churned and faded as I fell to the ground. Lying in an ever-growing pool of my own blood, my last sight was the assailants as they picked apart the life I had fought so hard for. As my sight turned to black, I had only one final thought:
I should have stayed in that cryotube...
Like an abusive relationship with a man who hates me, I keep coming back

While Battlefront II's graphics may not have aged well, the gameplay itself is still just as fun as that one day eight years ago when I finally popped it in and gave it a shot.
PROS
+Great gameplay mechanics
+Epic maps showing some of the most famous battles from Star Wars (including Geonosis, Kashyyk, Coruscant, Hoth, and Endor)
+Space battles! (which can be won by both dogfighting and boarding actions!)
+(Non-canon) Story-driven campaign where you play as the 501st Legion.
+Generic campaign system for galactic conquest!
+Heroes, each of whom has a different playstyle (for the most part).
+Vehicles!
+Class-driven spawning system familiar to anyone who played pre-Bad Company Battlefield.
+Each faction has two unique "special" units, from Jet Troopers to Wookies to Destroyer Droids to Dark Troopers.
+Original score from the movies!
+Additional "Hero Assault" mode where everyone is a Hero, allowing for such fights as Darth Maul vs Han Solo, or Jango Fett vs. Luke Skywalker.
+You can command NPC troops, a trait gone from most modern FPSs.
+Mods!
+Doesn't have EA's name on it!
CONS:
-Graphics are showing their age.
-Some of the voice actors are bad "sounds-like"s
-Balance issues in some various matches.
-Minor complaint, but there's no options to customize teams aside from Clone Wars/Galactic Civil War. So no fighting Droids or Clones as the Empire (except for two seperate campaign missions).
-No Space Heroes.
Overall an excellent game. It deserved a sequel/reboot infinitely better than that half-serious game EA offered (2015).
EDIT: Also better than that pay-to-win ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t EA thinks would make for a reasonable game (2017).

As you can tell from the trailer, Overcooked is chaotically fun. I have only played Overcooked with 1-2 players, so I cannot say much about the 3-4 players mode. Though I would imagine that the kitchen becomes even more chaotic, and thus, less manageable with more players.
- Overcooked is a party game that anyone can pick up on the go. The controls are straight forward and the gameplay is quite intuitive.
- I like that you can play on both keyboard and controller at the same time. Or two people can share one controller/keyboard. The developers really thought about making this game more accessible to more simultaneous players.
- I really enjoyed the different levels and the different gimmicks in each one. You’re expected to have a different game plan for each kitchen and to improvise as things start to go wrong. Overcooked is challenging but not to the point of frustration.
- I found the game to be quite forgiving. When food is about to burn, you are given a warning way in advance (I think around 4 seconds?) so you have plenty of time to react. Food doesn’t spoil, even if you cook it way in advance. You can throw ingredients and plates on the floor and nothing will happen. This game is chaotic enough, so I appreciate that the developers did not overcomplicate the cooking part.
- Only local co-op. I find it such a shame when co-op centric games do not include online multiplayer.
- You don’t stand a chance if you’re playing single player. For some reason the chopping takes roughly twice as long if you’re playing alone.
-This game works on a star system. You can gain up to three stars depending on your performance on a level. I found it somewhat annoying that later levels require you to have a certain amount of stars before you can play them. However, at the same time I can understand the reasoning behind this. Levels get progressively harder (kitchen layout, gimmicks, recipes) so you are expected to reach a certain mastery level before you can progress.
- I only disliked one level. In this level you are stuck on a platform floating on top of lava and the stoves are on mini platforms rotating around your platform. Creatively designed, but not very fun to play.
- This is a small detail but all the players connected can control the bus (you drive around in a bus to select a level). This leads to some chaotic driving that can either be hilarious or frustrating. I hope the people you are playing with aren’t trolls.
It is clear that Overcooked was designed to be a co-op experience. I would not recommend buying this game if you plan on playing it alone. The levels are chaotic and coordinating with your fellow players is harder than it looks. Having said that, be prepared to have fun while making mistakes.

All in all, it is highly recommended!

After hours of hard work and days of in-game hard-earned survival, I was well off: a cart to carry all of my heavy items that would bog me down in combat, two compound bows stocked with arrows (enough to take down pretty much anything before it even knew what hit it), enough provisions to last until judgement day, and my trusty spear should things get a little too close for comfort. I set up camp for the night in a dense bit of brush, threw together a lean-to using a tarp I took off the corpse of some raider who thought he'd take me for all I was worth, laid out my sleeping bag, and went down for the night.
Around 2 AM I was awoken by a massive *crack* in the woods near my position. Suddenly I remembered forgetting to hide my tracks, that's how it found me: a savage creature the size of a truck with teeth and claws protruding like foot-long razors. It saw me before I saw it, and that was all it took. Its claws tore across my chest before I knew where the danger was coming from sending blood flying all over the campsite along with what focus my eyes had achieved in the 5 seconds since their rude awakening. I was able to bring up my spear before the next attack landed and sliced open the creature's powerful arm, interrupting its strike. Vision fading quickly, I lunged. The beast let loose a shriek as the spear found its mark and dove deeper, piercing the heart. I'm not sure what gave out first, my legs or the crumpled heap of what was once the hulking black monstrosity.
Somehow I dragged myself to my backpack and fished out some rags. I quickly bandaged the massive gash in my chest, ever mindful that giving in to the swirling blackness meant never waking up. I popped a couple of strong painkillers and some antibiotics to ward off the inevitable infection that comes with a reused bandage (like there was any other choice) and retreated back into the safety of my lean-to to rest and give my wounds time to heal.
I must have dozed off, I'm not sure, all I remember is the pain. The incredible pain that only follows a crowbar being slammed into your knee.
Two thugs stood over me, wearing what appeared to be the mismatched hides of dozens of small animals. I didn't even have time to cry out in pain before the the bigger of the two brought his crowbar down again, silencing me permanently.
My vision churned and faded as I fell to the ground. Lying in an ever-growing pool of my own blood, my last sight was the assailants as they picked apart the life I had fought so hard for. As my sight turned to black, I had only one final thought:
I should have stayed in that cryotube...
Like an abusive relationship with a man who hates me, I keep coming back

Milestone, we meet again...
Out of my three favorite companies I follow in the racing game genre, Kylotonn, Codemasters, and then Milestone.
Ride 2...
I'm blown away, I truly am.
I honestly got the game late, I'm glad I did!
The game has improved so much, finally updated the bikes physics engine(if you say thay didn't, you're new to Ride or you've only played Ducati 90th), done a lot that we've asked in terms of bikes, and just went all out for this game.
The physics engine did need a bit of tuning, you guys did it!
You're able to push bikes a lot farther and gain from it.
Engine pulls feel more accurate, riding and tucking feels smoother, if you use a different style bike for a Sports Bike event you can tell a real difference just in watching on track behaviour.
I do think that trying to modify the Supermoto physics from VR The Game however didn't work, I'd started off with the Supermoto from the start and was immediately able to tell what had been done, solid but didn't play into Ride's engine all too well. The Supermoto class for people who ride manual has a gear skipping issue, engine lag issue out of corners, and the swooping feels awkward on this game. For the whole Supermoto Improv I'm gonna toss a 6.5/10 on how well it was done. The reason I'm throwing a number there is simply due to how well it turned out being a direct port from VR.
If there's one thing I loved the most from this game I'd have to say it's the ambition for it because the team has always showed that they love to work hard for their fans.
Ever since they learned they had a presence in the US Gaming World they've tried to fill in things that everyone wants since we're all different from country to country.
From the mix up of bike classes, I'd say this was a VERY smart move letting different breeds finally meet on one track and duel to see who's the strongest.
The bikes themselves have been worked on! Unlike in Ducati 90th, & Ride 1 when you upgrade an engine to a bike you've gotta put new breaks on it, make it run wild but have an actual payoff, you're punished if you don't.
Having a bigger track list also helped out a lot in this game, because I swear if Milestone kept that small list of actual Bike Circuits, & Scenic Circuits I'd have lost my mind in this review. Thankfully there's enough to call this a true expansion in the way of tracks.
Some have even been improved! This blew my mind away!
Here's my take on some of the tracks.
-Sierra Nevada finally got its final corners fixed, and I'd even go as far as saying that a few of the corners felt lifted a bit to give you a good chase down of the rider ahead of you if you get a good run.
-Hellenic Towers is probably one of the better looking tracks in this game, also good for hot laps. This track has pretty much already become abused online, everyone loves to set it up for the super street bikes.
-Imola feels very slippery compared to the Imola in Ride 1. I feel like even when I run a good setup the bikes always get hung in some corners, the detail to the track is better and represents how it should, though I like the fact that it's not too realistic.
There are more, also I hate to say it but I think since the tracks were pushed to be updated I think some things got missed which let down a lot of the tracks.
My overall opinion falls along this game being one of the best Ride games to date.
Milestone, please keep it only SLIGHTLY realistic, otherwise it takes away from what Ride is.
I'm happy I got this at $25 or I wouldn't have got it. If you can get this game for cheap I fully recommend playing it if you're a Milestone fan.

Very fun game. Honestly, there isn't really much I would recommend that the developers change, they were very thorough in making this game. Certainly nothing game-breaking (so far). Bugs are non-existant as far as I can tell.* Lot's of fun for the file size. It has a sense of brutality without relying on gore to get the message across.
I recommend when you play this game that you do *not* look anything up first. The game is intuitive, and a great deal  of fun can be had by messing up. This is a great game for just getting on and having fun.
If I had to think of a downside, it would be difficult but I would say there are two. The first would be that it is simple, and those that want fancy 3d graphics or a complex game should look to a different genre altogether. Second would be replayability. It has a good story, but there is something disappointing about each part of the story fleshed out: that's one fewer mystery for later. Of course, you can say that about any story-oriented game.
Again, I would say that the keyword here is intuitive. Easy to pick up the mechanics, more difficult to use them effectively, but overally the difficulty is anywhere from mild to moderate. This isn't an 'easy' game per-se, but it certainly isn't hard. It is a game where risk and reward are both quite high in most encounters. A small slip up can cost you dearly, a well timed strike can earn you incredibly useful loot, so long as you have the space to carry it all. By far the most scarce resource in the game is space. You can't carry everything you find in the beginning, so deciding what is most valuable can be a very tough decision.
All of the above serve to make it the ideal rogue-like game IMO.
*EDIT: About the bugs, I should mention that there is a minor graphics bug where items will appear partly off-screen, and cannot be selected from boxes. This is uncommon, however, and easily fixed by switching between fullscreen and minimized (you can end in whatever screen you prefer). Probably not worth mentioning except that I had said "Bugs are non-existant as far as I can tell."
EDIT 2: One other critisism: This game does not offer difficulty settings at this time. Initially, it seems difficult. After a few hours, it does seem slightly easy. Hopefully that will change in time, but with a sense of ease often comes recklessness (at least in my case), counteracting any potential for this game to become boring. It still remains a very fun game, and I look forward to updates.

Early Access Watcher Public Service Announcement
Game: The Silence Outside
Version: v0.9
Gameplay Footage:
Disclosure: This game copy was bought by the reviewer.
I have no issue with a developer using store bought assets as place marks. I really don’t The moment they decide to put their game up for sale, however, the leniency degrades and my palm slowly ascends towards my forehead. The frequency of the asset usage in Early Access is getting to high and I am tired of seeing poor programming accompanying it. The current amount of playable content includes two stealth missions that can be completed in under thirty seconds (with no clearing scoring method or failure state) and five run through portal missions that range from 30 to 60seconds depending on the walking or dash speed. I would say six, but the level seems to be broken and only has a CD_NAV prompt in the name. A story mode and other challenges are slated for a later date.
Visually the game is what you expect from the Unreal 4 engine with sound design being standard door opening and footsteps. The two tracks I could hear in the game were okay, but with how quickly levels complete, I couldn’t hear them to tell how long the track length was. The underlying problem is with how dark the game is in almost every section. One zone in a spiral corridor was fine, but the engineering areas and public zone were too dark. I have a guess why this might be, but I don’t like to assume anything. As for the environments, I recognize the two stealth levels being made with the Modular SciFi: Engineer Hallways and some items being a part of the Sci Fi Industrial Crates pack.
Technical issues are wide and varied, including load screen issues (can move behind the screen), mouse functionality issues (loses the ability to scan by moving the mouse/requires holding down mouse button to scan), complete character lock up (causes character to not respond as seen in video with locked walking) and unexpected stuttering. This is not the complete list, but more of the serious issues. Missing textures make it possible to fall out of the level with a view of the skybox, enemy AI fails to detect you from two feet away in certain cases and the number of times code prompts flash up in the top left corner is unacceptable. I understand things like the story mode and combat challenges are missing, but you can make it so the response prompts are not visible or explain that the feature is not available. One glaring issue is with the equipment system that wouldn’t respond properly in the Test mode, carrying over to the main menu. It adds another layer of frustration to the list requiring a restart of the program to fix.
I just can’t recommend it in this state and hope that the developers do manage to fix most of these issues within their first couple of patches. This game was released too early for the its’ own good.
This has been a EAW PSA.

Tropico 4 is - hands down - the most fun city builder-style game that I know! The difficulty level in the campaign is pretty low, so people who want to relax and build pretty cities (like me) will have their fun.
Increasing the political difficulty level in sandbox games makes the game more interesting for those who want a challenge, especially if you also increase the economic difficulty level and can't afford everything the people want. You can decide which factions of the population to please, and which to ignore.
There's some kind of a roleplay element in the way you can customize el presidente for every single mission: Social origin, the way how he/she attained power, and three character traits all give you certain strengths and weaknesses. Every time you win a mission, the three character traits will rise up a level to a maximum of five and get stronger.
With this, you can later try out more specialized and extreme kinds of government. I had tons of fun with my communist autocracy, with my pinochet-like neoliberal autocracy (where I put tons of unemployed into prison for forced labor), or my religious theocracy (This guy has less than 50% respect for el presidente? Mark him as heretic and start the inquisition edict!)
In short, I suggest that everyone who is at least slightly interested in city builder games should absolutely try this game out!

Look. People are saying this game is just a copy and paste job of Ark. This is a lie. I would give the game a try for yourself or wait until it is a little more done. I expect in a few months less and less people will compare this game to Ark and Dark and light will be a game that stands on its own. Even if the UI looks a little simiular.

The culmination of a childhood fantasy of being the Starship Captain here. The game ROCKS, now why couldn't someone make a Star Trek game like this?
The premise is pretty standard sci-fi stuff; you're alone and far behind enemy lines, the Federation is doomed unless you can save the day and a whole bunch of baddies are between you and victory. Pretty dull right? But the execution is just so spot on perfect that the plot actually becomes secondary. It's a huge thrill to be in charge of that rustbucket spaceship and having a crew doing everything they can to simply get from point A to B.
Character interaction is pretty limited but it seems that doesn't even matter. By the second or third sector (chapters) you'll be so  invested in your crew that you will be doing everything you can to keep them alive. Amazing how Subset managed to pull that off.
Additionally, while overall a serious game, it does have its lighthearted moments of humour, usually delivered with a single sardonic eyebrow skeptically raised at some pop-culture sci-fi trope. Supporting the overall feel is the soundtrack which is incredibly appropriate.
The biggest quibble is that it is REALLY DAMN DIFFICULT, every FTL Jump could be your last. It's a feature of the rogue-like of course, but when you couple it with the amount of caring that you put into your ragged band of misfits it's damn near heartbreaking.
However, if you ever wanted to Captain a starship, you need to buy this game! Your inner James Tiberius Kirk will thank you. Although he might be disappointed with the lack of green space babes...

All in all CoH2 is an awesome game.
It takes quite some time to get into it and really score well in PvP, but otherwise it wouldn't be that interesting.
Note that this game is quite resource intensive, though its a strategy game. Due to the fact that you can destroy nearly everything, explosions create crates and so on, its requirements are quite high.
IIRC the game also doesn't support Crossfire/SLI. You should definitely make sure that you AT LEAST score ABOVE the minimum requirements. And even then it might lag. I personally run a quite good machine and haven't had any non connection related lags, so I cant tell much about that.
You get a more or less historically accurate campaign, which has been criticized for its presentation of the soviet war efforts and/or moral. But, besides you should make a note of the fact, that there are historically difficult parts in it, its pretty fun.
For Skirmish games you can either play Solo or Co-Op missions. These mostly objective based missions are the so called ToW missions, only available if you own the CoH2 base-game AND the corresponding DLC
In Multi-player you can set up custom games versus AIs, from Easy to Expert, where Easy should be possible for any player, and Expert should only be done with a good team of veteran players.
Also you can just search and join a PvE game lobby manually or via an auto-matching.
And for sure there is PvP.
Game modes for Multi-player are "Victory Point" and "Annihilation". In VP-Matches you reduce your opponents points by holding the majority of the Victory points, reducing your enemy to zero points grants you Victory. In Annihilation you 'just' fight until one side is destroyed.
For game-play mechanics I can just say that I love them for their level of detail (ignoring some rare, but not less annoying bugs like dead enemies still throwing grenades)

With the release of TWFA (Western Front Armies) Relic changed their much criticized DLC policy of having to BUY half Commanders. (Though you were able to do quite well without them)
Now Commanders and War Spoils (previously known as Bulletins) drop randomly for playing. This is quite a nice feature, but the system is a bit unbalanced at the moment. (Aka you get things doubled but cant use them for the doubled effect, or you get stuff you cant use, since you don't have the appropriate commanders)
Still, now you have to BUY every FACTION you want to play. You want to play as Soviets? Go buy the base game. You want to play as U.S. Forces? Go BUY either the whole TWFA or only U.S. Forces.
That's a bit strange, but not that bad. 20€ for the whole TWFA stand alone is quite  a good price. No single player then though.
All in all CoH2 is an awesome game with an pretty active community. It can be fun either solo or in Multi-player.

So, imagine if the first Company of Heroes featured the American Soldiers executing captured enemies, executing traitors, burning civillian houses, and all that fun stuff. Well, it didn't -- it was a bowlderized version of history, but that was necessary to make the game fun, and not preachy or offensive to veterans. Company of Heroes 2 is both insensitive and crude, bludgeoning its' way through subject matter, and downright painting World War II era Soviets as sadists and murderers. As someone with relatives who fought in World War II, I'm very offended by the way this game handled the era, downright portraying events that never happened (scorching homes with civillians still inside being a big one -- something that NEVER happened as a result of a specific Russian law against it), or flat-out violating historical precedent to paint the Russians as the bad guys. (Execute a heroic soldier because he deserted his post to save an Officer? No precedent, and soldiers like this were often decorated for heroism.) The gameplay is solid, sure, but this is the most racist thing I think I've played in years. ♥♥♥♥ Relic, ♥♥♥♥ CoH 2.

In terms of overall "feel", Titan Quest + Diablo 2. It reminds me of Path of Exile in that you need to give it 1-2 hours to get used to it if you aren't a huge ARPG connoisseur. PoE's camera angle and character size/movement compared to other ARPGs was the hurdle for me there (and the ugly♥♥♥♥♥gear). Something about the ability usage and graphics in Grim Dawn feels a little bit disconnected or flimsy compared to, say, Diablo 3, which is a result of Titan Quest's licensed engine as I felt the same when first starting up that title.
Endgame is doing 'runs' of existing content like D2/TQ, as well as working on your reputation with various factions to unlock extra enemies and vendor rewards. There is, however, endgame mapping via mods that can scratch the same itch as D3 rifts, PoE maps, or Torchlight mapworks. Their crucible content is a scaling arena deathmatch against waves of monsters used for a change of pace and - mostly for rerolls - a faster leveling path. Based on the success of the current expansion, which is being well-received, they will hopefully continue to make official content, but the game will also continue to get treated to user-created content, just like there were eventually many highly enjoyable full-blown top-to-bottom guttings and recreations for Diablo 2.
If you've enjoyed ANY ARPG, do yourself a favor and get this. Tons of builds to experiment with, and each time they add a new class, it adds more possible combinations than the last time.

As a major Half-Life fan, I was thoroughly dissapointed at what the sequel became. It's basically a Michael Bay movie now. If you want more details, scroll down & read more of this review; otherwise, the summary is don't buy it if you want a good Half-Life game, but buy it if you never played a Half-Life game before and are from the more "modern" generation of COD clones.
SPOLERS AHEAD! DO NOT READ IF YOU DON'T WANT THE STORY SPOILED FOR YOU
The first problem is the difficulty. It's very inconsistent. 9/10 enemies are very easy to defeat even on the hardest difficulty, yet some enemies are simply overpowed like strider, which can usually be taken out with 10-13 rockets, which is simply to much. Nearly all your ammo and some more is used just for one thing. Another thing to noite is how bad the AI is. The original game's AI was very detailed and intelligent, even by today's standards. However, the AI apparently wasn't transfered well to the source engine. And what did come out was a lackluster AI.
The second problem is the story. Many elements from the original game were completely thrown out, such as the alien homeplanet of Xen. Instead of using that as a way of getting around, they just closed it off and said "we no longer need Xen to get around". It wastes what was a cool, weird interdimensional world and throw it straight into the trash can. Also, many slight elements are only meant to sound cool, such as the infamous "Seven Hour War" where the combine defeated every military in the world in just 7 hours.
The third problem is how much it wants to be the original; except they failed at it. Often times the characters may make joking references back to the original, like Barney saying "You forgot this back in Black Mesa" except that doesn't make sense. Gordon had 2 crowbars in the original. One from the beginning, where he lost it when he got captured by the HECU, and then got a second, replacement crowbar when he escaped military (HECU) capture. The weapon system was taken straight from the original, but worse, along with its progression. Why have an SMG with grande launcher? Cause its from the original. By the way, there's actually 2 weapons with grenade launchers. The SMG/GL and the Rifle/GL. Once you pick the Rifle/Grenade Launcher combo, there's no point in using the SMG except when you run out of ammo for everything except that. Other iconic weapons such as the Tau Cannon are now shadows of their former selves.
The fourth problem is the soundtrack. It's not bad, yet it all sounds very similiar. Some tracks are pulled straight from the original, just the quality was put up a little bit.
The fifth problem is the ending. It's the same as the original "canon" ending from the first game, where the G-Man  puts you into stasis, and roll credits. Thankfully Valve got a little bit of backlash for it, and made  HL2 Episodes 1 & 2, which are supposed to be the "true" endings/events that happened after the original. A similiar thing happened with Bethesda's Fallout 3, where the ending was so hated they made a DLC/expansion and said the ending to that one was the "canon" ending.
The final problem is the level design. Phenominal at times, but others are atrocious. The 4th chapter, or level, in the game for first timers would normally take 2-3 hours to complete, for a segment that was only supposed to take you 35 minutes. There are other segments where they take a good idea and make it boring and repetitive such as the chapter in a prison named "Nova Prospekt" where you throw things to make aliens called "Antilions" attack your enemy's. Cool idea, poorly executed.
Another minor problem is the characters voice acting/expressions. Instead of just talking realistically,  they talk, then do a split-second mug shot & pause for effect so they can allow the player to do a quick answer remark, even Gordon is a SILENT protagonist. Gordon can't talk, and will probably never. All this does is make the characters look dumber than they are. Also some charcters, such as Alyx Vance, your "sidekick" are just annoying.
One more complaint: Gordon's identity is slandered in this game. He was only special in the first because he was the only one tough enough to survive for extended period of time. Now he's special because when he arrives, it's the second coming of Christ, where EVERYONE has been waiting for him, even if he's been gone for some 20 or so years. This game brings in more qustions then answers.
So overall, Half-Life 2, for me, was EXTREMELY dissapointing. If your a big Half-Life fan, and want an actually good half-life game, just play the original game and it's expansions. HOWEVER, if you aren't a big Half-Life fan, and are from the more "modern" generation of COD and such, then give this one a go. You might have a better time with it then I did.

August 23, 2017 -- So the game has been out a litte more than a whole month. Let's take a moment to reflect upon the game's lifespan until now. I'll start with the cons, because everyone likes to know beforehand if they are going to step into a pile of dogs**t. Mostly because they don't want to step in said pile of dogs**t.
CONS:
- Regardless of the frequent patches that are being rolled out, none of them seem to really be for fixing relevant issues. Most of them were to cater to PVP servers and then it flipflopped to cater to PVE players crying about getting rekt in PVP on PVP servers.
- Actual gamebreaking bugs fixed by patching e.g. falling through mountainous terrain: Minimal.
- Actual helpful implementations to the game in any way e.g. UI/HUD updates, better Tools: Minimal.
- Server Administration is something for people who either professionally do it IRL or have spent a lot of time doing it trial & error until it just "worked." Launching your own server is a hassle, the ingame launcher tool is a waste of time as it occupies your Steam account and prevents you from playing from the same machine. You need to write a .BAT yourself to avoid the account occupation and even then the functionality is questionable. Changing the settings of running servers in realtime? Nope. Easy to use intuitive interface for Admins that have less experience with commandline i.e. writing commands on the fly in text to control game elements? Nope. The server admin GUI is currently in a very poor state, clunky to use, and not very effective so you might as well get used to writing everything out. Also, server restarts with their lack of announcement often come with massive rollbacks in one neat little aggrivating package because force saving the game world to disk and THEN restarting is something mythical that no productive server environment should ever do. /endsarcasm. Be warned if you intend on running your own server for yourself and your friends, it will be a pain in your hind end.
- Optimization: Minimal. You still need a pretty powerful computer and even then the game will probably run bad.
- PVP doesn't currently have much of a "point." The only reward one has to gain from PVP is perhaps territorial claim and what little one can scavenge from the ruins of a defeated enemy's base, which tends to just be garbage you can easily farm yourself within less time it took to kill the enemy. While barbarically butchering both foreign factions and players belonging to your own faction can be fun and this may suffice for most players, I personally feel it is lacking substance and a solid point.
PROS:
- The amount of pure potential for this game is still really nuts. The randomness of the animal AI at times, combined by crap-your-pants scare moments in the dark of night, the beautifully designed biomes and landscapes, and even the human element itself in the world, all of it ultimately leads to a good gaming experience even with all the cons I mentioned before.
- Given the PC can handle it, this game still can have compelling visuals for those of us who are graphics junkies.
- With a little revision and replanning, the game's crafting system could become quite entertaining, even allowing for players to develop characters into artisans and master craftsmen focused on special areas of knowledge, giving players a reason to fulfil a certain role and benefit from fulfilling said role. At the moment its sort of a "grind to level everything" situation where players hardly have to interact in trade, but some people like isolationism. It just doesn't make the starting towns with assorted vendors very relevant.
- Animals and creatures being tameable was cool enough as is, but many of them can even play specific roles or have special features the player can use to his benefit. Capturing a Water Elemental and having her water your crops in a location where you normally have to rely on rain is pretty spiffy thinking.
There's really a lot more to discuss but these are the things I find important. I am not quite ready to revoke my Recommendation for D&L just yet, but Devs if you are reading this, you might want to get to work fixing the problems that matter or you're going to kill this game.
July 21, 2017 -- TL;DR: If you can't cope with bugs and issues this is not for you because you'll rage, fast. If you don't have an above average PC (at least a SATA III SSD for the installation and good GPU like GTX700 card or better with 3GB RAM) then you'll have terrible performance issues. If you don't care about many things being broken and want to help fund the game then do get it, it looks like they're taking it in the right direction.
This game is basically what you get when you mix Ark with Conan. Some say there are elements of Elder Scrolls there too but I don't count a little magic as being overly Elder Scrolls. The UI is essentially exactly like Ark and Conan, even down to the wording. Most of the gameplay is exactly like those games too.
The good: It's familiar. It's definitely a good start in the right direction. There's quite a bit of potential. A platform for building something magnificent. If the developers really stay focused on the things that really count then it's going to do just as well if not even better than the titles before it. It could end up being the best blend of action MMO with survival and base building available. If they don't screw it up. Just don't expect too much from this handful of primal goo and you're golden. Enjoy it slowly.
The bad: You have to expect these things when dealing with Early Access. Bad performance. Bugs. Incomplete content. Progress wipes. Cheaters/Exploiters/Hackers. Griefers/Trolls. This game is according to the devs in Early Access but some parts feel like it's still Pre-Alpha. Either way, it's currently VERY unpolished. Many people have complained about very long loading times (my initial load with a SSD is 22 seconds which I have to say does feel like kind of a lot) Some of the starting quests flat out don't even work. So yeah, expect broken stuff.
Essentially, you're going to gamble your money. Let's get that into the open. If the devs make too many mistakes this title is going to be absolute garbage. If they don't then its going to be very much worth the current price tag. It's up to you to decide if you want to risk the investment -- but if you do and you end up disappointed, then don't say you weren't warned if you read this message beforehand. But we're talking about what 30 bucks, hell you can't even really fill up your car's gas tank with that much money. The loss is minimal.

Outside of scripted mission narratives, it's rare that any faction goes to 0% respect except the environmentalists, and they never seem to rebel.
It can be a little awkward to play. Remember the Human Element - everyone has to walk to work, or to a farm, or to a garage if you build them (
), they go to work, they go home, they eat, they sleep, they go to work.
It can be frustrating for the first dozen hours if you fail to realise this and can't work out why your construction workers think there's no projects to work on when you've slapped down half a million new buildings!!
The tutorial feels very "baby's first computer game", and
unbearably slow, but play all four missions and you get a couple neat tips on the game mechanics once it's stopped telling you what a mouse is and what a mouse wheel is for.
Very fun though. The humourous, satirical veneer is great, and the caricatures are funny to try and work out who they're meant to be. Halfway through the campaign, and it's a pretty interestingly structured campaign.
Sadly, have gotten to a point in the campaign where maps are starting to get reused. Almost identical levels of reused, down to the resources.
But the scenarios and starting buildings are different, so once you forget about it, it's great.

Company of heroes 2 takes much of the tried and tested vCOH, COH:Online & Dawn of War II mechanics  and ups the anti several notches. Improvements start with more dynamic battlefields with infantry vaulting, blizzards and a fog of war system intended to replicate human vision. You'll probably forget about the campaign because the multiplayer is where its at:
Customisable armies and unique doctrines can mean that game flow is very different from one match to another as each player has a potentially different bag of tricks from seemingly identical armies which keeps games fresh and exciting. New USA and West German forces have very different playstyles to their Ostheer and Red army contemporaries and provided your willing to invest the time to understand the functions of the various units and factions you will doubtlessly find an army that suits your playstyle.
Combat is fast, brutal and escalates organically from early infantry skirmishes to combined arms manoeuvres to full scale tank battles provided you manage to maintain control of the map. Initiating, preventing, predicting and retreating from combat is 99% of the game with flanking, cover, suppression and overwhelming firepower being key tools to maintain your advantage. Make no mistake this is not a game about economics or hotkeys for stimpacks. Company of Heroes 2 is all about making use of infantry/calvary tactics to beat you opponent. And its great fun!

Faster than Light did something that I think we'd all kind of been waiting for. It took some of the really fun elements of roguelikes, space ship sims, and squad-based tactical games, and combined them into one simple unit. You have a lot of randomization, and enough content that you won't see it all in one run, which creates high replayability. You have ship upgrading, with swappable parts, paired with a classic energy management system which will be familiar to watchers of Star Trek and players of FreeSpace. Units are controlled by assigning where they go, and they do tasks as required, while you target weapons and try to take down enemy ships. It's really quite a fantastic combination.

A great introduction to the Warhammer 40k universe. If you're like me you stumbled upon this by friends that either played the tabletop game, were into the lore or played this. As an RTS it is quite an entertaining one to play as you have your campagin of course which is really good as you play as a Space Marine chapter known as the Blood Ravens. It's even got a decent story to go with it since it takes place on a slowly chaotic planet filled with Orks, Eldar and Chaos Space Marines. I sort of wished the campaign was a little more varied in how you only play as Space Marines but it's still a rather competent campaign at that.
The game has lots of units to play as and often the game is territorial based meaning that you you have to keep moving and taking over relics and strategic points to get the resources you need to win the battle. It's a pretty good incentive instead of the usual building a huge army and steamrolling everything (not that steamrolling is fun but) it's refreshing to see a change in the RTS formula. When you're done with your campaign you have your skirmish modes where you play  against the AI with four factions to choose from (Space Marines, Chaos Space Marines, Eldar and Orks) and online mode where you play with friends and randoms which is quite nice and fun to play. Lastly you have your army painter which let's you customize your faction's armor and logo colour. It's cool but a little limited though not a lot of RTS games lets you do that.
Good campaign, fun skirmishes and online play makes Dawn of War a worthy RTS to have in your collection. It's over 10 years old and as a recent newbie to the series it is still rather fun to pick up and play. I give it an 8/10.

First line TL;DR: If your machine has the recommended system requirements and you enjoy games like ARK and RUST but have wanted more flexibility and magic in what you're doing, this is a no-brainer and a ton of fun. If you're on the fence, go watch someone play the game on Twitch and keep an open mind, i.e. don't be swayed by mob think in chat. Look at what the game actually is, not what people are complaining or praising, and decide if it's something you want to try. There are some minor issues but I'm not worried that they're going to get fixed, they already updated the servers yesterday.
I'm shocked at the number of negative reviews. I played 14.5 hours on official server yesterday with my tribe and 1.5 hours on host/local just to see how the game performed without network lag.
Trolls in chat all day complained about the game being an ARK ripoff. They're absolutely not wrong - Snail Studios USA purchased Wildcard Studios, the company that made ARK, in 2015 - the same year ARK was released. They literally own the assets to ARK and have re-used a few here. To say this is just another ARK is short-sighted and unimaginative trolling.
First, the cities add an entirely different dimension. I've played a lot of ARK on Host/local because I get tired of the trolls and try-hards. There are ARK mods out there that try to add in NPCs and currency systems, Dark and Light has them built in. The cities are well-done and perform much better than any of the custom RP ARK maps I've played (pro studio vs hobby modders, no surprise there). The currency system can be a little frustrating up front but people who enjoy exploring these games and figuring things out will pick it up pretty quickly. The other side of that is that playing on host/local is a LOT easier than in ARK. The cities make you feel like you're playing online while in host/local mode, and you don't have to fiddle with your Game.ini settings to adjust engram points just so you can afford to build housing and have saddles and weapons.
Second, the skill progression system is amazing and closer to Black Desert Online or Skyrim than ARK. You level up what you want, there are no engrams. The "you must be x level to advance to tier y in skill z" is a little annoying, but it does help the balance of the game a lot. There are no level 10 characters making top building tier. Leveling things up does require a little bit of brain work but not much. Do you want to level up light magic? Craft light magic runes or defeat light magic creatures to understand them better. Do you want to level up ranged weapons? Start by gathering crafting materials and then craft the basics once you get them until you hit the top tier you can do for your level. You're going to throw out a lot of produced goods in this game, which feels wasteful, but remember that when your character dies - and you will die - even if you lose your gear, you keep your experience and the ability to make the higher-tier items. Your experience and the abilities to produce goods is way more valuable than the goods themselves.
The melee system feels pretty good. Ranged system for bows is a little different from ARK or Conan, it's a lot more arcade-like but also feels pretty decent. Magic is a lot of fun and doesn't feel OP, at least to me. If anything, ranged weapons are currently the OP tier. I can kill a level 25 goblin with three arrows to the head, where it takes me multiple shots with Fireball I or Frostbolt I to take one down.
Dark and Light does take a while to load. Most sandbox survival games do. Please check the system requirements before purchase. I have a decent gaming rig that I built in 2015 - 8 core AMD CPU, GTX 970, 32 GB RAM, and installed game to the SSD - and had zero issues with performance other than network lag. Again, running on host/local was flawless and a lot of fun, but I have a group of friends I play with and we all went in on this game and have had a ton of fun on official servers despite the lag.
There are bugs. It's early access. Early access allows studios that don't have AAA money up front to produce AAA games. There are pros and cons to early access, yes. Protip: sleeping bags can be picked up and put back down if you can't sleep in yours more than once. The tutorials are also pretty clear on what is needed for sleep, but all day yesterday I saw people who didn't pay attention and had to turn to global chat on the server for help.
If the price is too high for you to take a risk, I understand. Don't purchase the game. If you're at all interested in survival games with a lot of freedom and depth in character builds, please join those of us who stuck with Dark & Light longer than an hour to see how good this gem really is.

Faster than Light did something that I think we'd all kind of been waiting for. It took some of the really fun elements of roguelikes, space ship sims, and squad-based tactical games, and combined them into one simple unit. You have a lot of randomization, and enough content that you won't see it all in one run, which creates high replayability.
