It is a bad sign when the demo is more fun than the main game.
NEO Scavenger has, as everyone has said, a TON of potential.  There is just so much they could do here.  Combat feels granular and staisfying, while at the same time being crazy-lethal if you're not careful.  The loot you find feels like you're struggling to survive, and the crafting system is elegant.  Character creation is simple, but offers meaningful choices.  It's got a LOT of good stuff in it.
But the main game also wants to have a story.  And that main quest line feels kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ when it's next to what would make a fantastic open-world survival game.  Since death is frequent, and often from kinda unfair places, having to redo the same quests over and over is unsatisfying, to say the least.  And I'm not a hundred percent sure if the game has magic in it or not, because it sure seems like it sometimes, and that clashes with the flavor of a sci-fi wrecked earth.
Oh, the deaths.  Man.  I have died a dozen times at least from starting a game, and freezing to death before I can find shoes.  I have died because I can't find clean water, or anything to boil water in to sterilize it.  I have died from a single lucky gunshot.  I like how lethal the game can be, but I do not enjoy at all how arbitrary it feels at times.
Also, the demo thing.  The demo shows off a scavenging system where each city tile has multiple things to search.  Do you check the storage shed, which may have nothing but is pretty safe, or do you go for the high rise, where you might get jumped, but could have a lot more left over?  The main game has one thing to search per tile.  Choice : eliminated.  Just right out the window.  I cannot, in good faith, recommend a game where the main game takes AWAY choices.

I'm really enjoying this game, except for a couple of details.
- Picking [Strong] [Melee] [Tough] is overpowered. If anything. ANYTHING comes within melee range and you're carrying a branch, they can kill their♥♥♥♥♥goodbye.
Got a rifle? Nevermind the bullets, just use the gun's butt and turn them into a greasy paste.
- If you get a disease, that's pretty much the end of the game. I was in an extremely profitable run, but caught dysenteria, then bloated, then the symptoms subsided. It came back not long after, then I reached "the lights" and I traded almost everything for a medikit, which couldn't do anything to save my life.
- There's an enemy that will call for reinforcements in the middle of a fight. While this is an interesting and welcome mechanic, IT DOESN'T MEAN THEY ARE CALLING MONSTERS FROM NEARBY HEXES. THEY ARE GENERATING MORE OF THEM. I got into a fight with one of them, I was hiding and using a slingshot and by the time I managed to kill the first, 4 more had shown up. By the time I killed the next, 3 more had appeared. I kept picking them off, but more kept being summoned.
Had it not been for the lack of ammo, I wonder if they would've kept spawning infinitely?
- It's turn based, but sometimes my actions are limited. Sometimes I get 5 actions per turn, sometimes, I just get 1, and I get no explanation as to why.
Like any good roguelike, it relies in random chance.
It has a very interesting crafting system that uses the skills you picked and an array of "substitute materials" in which it specifies what *kind* of item you need to craft.
"Waterproof, fireproof container" may refer to a pan or a glass bottle, "sharp edge" may be a piece of glass, a shiv, or a knife...
It's a very interesting game, which is a bit frustrating at times. If you get out of a bad fight alive, you're likely to die anyway.
Combat is turn-based with options for actions, which will vary depending on what you picked for skills. For example, picking [Tough] will allow you to headbutt an oponent sometimes, and the [Trapping] skill will let you lure an enemy into a makeshift trap.
Crafting is relatively easy. Drop the right items and skills into a grid, click the "craft" button, presto. You got yourself a new bow.
In the end, yes, it's still early access, but it's still fun, complex and interesting. I had a smile on my face when I fought a big, furry monster barehanded, took no damage, and got a "video recording of you beating the crap out of a wolf-man barehanded".

I had this game in my library for ages before I played it.  Comparing it to similar games like Torchlight, Torchlight 2 and Diablo 3 I can say these other games feel more polished. This does not mean Grim Dawn is the lesser game. As a whole, Grim Dawn is probably the more interesting / engaging from the lot.
Regarding character builds, Diablo 3 has the most variation. This is followed by Grim Dawn, and then Torchlight 2 and Torchlight.
Difficulty is also roughly in that order. It should be noted that, in the beginning, you can only select Normal or Veteran difficulty in Grim Dawn. Unless you're asleep at the wheel, even Veteran difficulty should be pretty easy. After finishing the game for the first time you can also choose the Elite difficulty. And a second run though unlocks Ultimate difficulty. Ultimate difficulty will give you a really serious challenge.
Running through Grim Dawn on Normal or Veteran difficulty the first time is neither too long or too short. Actually, it's a nice introduction to the game, story and your build. During my first game I used a cookie-cutter build, but the second time around I had a lot of fun with my own experimental build.
I would really like to see a LOT more content for Grim Dawn. I have yet to purchase the first DLC, so I don't know how much has been added to the game.
A thing I'm missing in Grim Dawn is gear transmogrifying. There's no way to change the looks of the equipment you're wearing.
Would I recommend Grim Dawn? Hell yes!

Pro:
* Good Graphics
* Decent Combat System
* Good Character Customization, but surprisingly limited the more you delve into it.
Meh:
* PVP unlocks at level 50, you can be pked when leaving any safe zones, the game gives you an option to stay at level 49 until you complete the quest that unlocks level 50. By staying at level 49, you would miss out on extra skills and combat mechanics.
*You can Dye most clothing in this game but Dyes can only be obtained from the cash shop (1+ dollar for 1 single use dye, the Dye comes randomly but the randomness can be lessened by buying specific dye packs that are more costly)
Con:
*Life-Simulator (Crafting, Gathering, Fishing) is simply AFK and tedious
*Voice Acting for cutscenes and NPCs ranges on barely-okay to atrocious, with a heavy leaning on atrocious
* Quests are simply kill 20 of this, talk to that npc, or gather this item for that Npc
* Community is full of "dank memers" that spam chat with talks of traps, alienware, hentai, pedophilia, out of date memes and overall trollish behaviors.
* Poor Pacing in leveling (Grinding from 1 to 50 starts out okay, but 50 and beyond is staying true to the Korean Grinder Tradition). It's gotten so bad that spam bots in the chats are offering Power-Leveling Services more than Gold Selling Services.
* Equipment for each classes are incredibly limited in terms of Aesthetics (ex. For the Valkyrie Class, you have around 17 sets of armor, 7 of them have the same look, 3 of the other set has the same look, 4 for the other sets. etc. (only 6 types of looks for the whole 17 sets of armor) (really only 4 if you don't count 2 armor sets that are universal)
* 30+ bucks for 1 character outfit (Technically, Just barely Technically, can be obtained in an Auction House for In-Game Money, But very-rarely in stock)
* Pricing in the Cash-shop is exorbitant, 10+ bucks for a pet (Auto Loot, that's all it's good for.)
* Banks in the game only keeps your in-game cash in it's territory and it's not universal, meaning you'd have to back-track to a town and go through a tedious currency exchange to turn your in-game money into a single stack, as money has weight in this game.
* If you would like to avoid this tedium, then buy a maid from the cash shop (10+ bucks).
*Wanna level up faster? Buy special undergarments that gives a permanent exp percentage boost in the cash shop 7+ bucks
*The Equipment end-game system is based heavily on RNG it's enhancement process, the material that is used for refining the equipment is a rare drop from mobs, it can also be obtained from the Auction house for pretty steep amount of in-game money when you look at the total amount of material needed.

消逝的光芒（Dying Light） 绰号：蜘蛛侠的光芒
作为波兰开发商Techland呈现给世界的2015开年大作，消逝的光芒有着优良的画面，各种元素的杂糅，跑酷+打怪的生存机制，真实的黑夜与日夜模拟系统，但因为放在年初发布，当时2015的硬件升级潮流还未开始，其较高的配置要求让诸多玩家望尘莫及。
涉及了很多元素，动作，射击，生存，潜入，逃亡，开锁...就射击方面，也只有那么几把枪，而这样一个丧尸密布还有不少“跑酷型”甚至无尽的黑夜中的“夜魔”的世界，肆意放枪令人感觉很不科学，手感一般，一般是打BOSS和跑跑跑收拾残怪时用，平时还是喜欢刀刀剑剑斩首断骨，潜入方面...基本上感觉没有，赖斯的手下很容易发现自己，一般是蹲行对小僵尸使用背后扭头的技能，
生存方面，初期真心是确实惊心动魄，血少刀烂，还跑得慢！至今记得到那个第一次邂逅夜魔的夜晚....配合全黑的画面，确实是充满逃亡的紧张感，不过到后期，游戏就越来越容易了，开锁王随随便便就是一把1000的单手剑，蹲一小洞里，三下五下就是一只夜魔，而在初期，当初跟吧友联机，那真的是18般武艺全上完了，三个人猥琐在管道里杀一只夜魔杀到天亮.....
开锁....挺考耐心的，有简单到困难的难度分级，越困难的箱子获得宝物越好，当然，获得武器的等级是随着自己等级而改变的，就像巫师3：拾荒一样，
单纯来讲，Dyinglight是一款丧尸题材的作品，相较于前辈《死亡岛》来说，添加了很多东西，不逊色于镜之边缘的跑酷元素是首当其冲的。FPS一向容易导致3D眩晕，尤其是动作幅度较大，画面摆动较大，甚至出现视觉颠倒的情况（典型就是孤岛危机1Core失重关卡），很多"体质"不行的玩家在上手他们馋嘴却又望而生畏的第一人称游戏之前，都还得吃两颗晕车药，而就是因为3D眩晕的问题，造成将于2016年发布的第一人称动作游戏，镜之边缘：催化剂的跑动头部晃动较09年的镜之边缘大幅缩水，不得不说这是一个妥协的产物，
再扯回来，虽然在赞其跑酷元素，但消光也仅有翻越，攀爬，减压滚等基础动作，没有Free-running，即自由奔跑的那传统观念里对跑酷的印象——花哨的体操性动作，当然由于是沙盒开放式的地图，拥有充满棚楼与地中海风格建筑的“贫民窟”和“老城”两大区域，相较于镜之边缘更为自由，奔跑更为舒畅，游戏中的垃圾堆和汽车顶可以无视距离趴地缓冲，每次都能听到那“啊哇~~"的一声，反科学娱乐感十足，游戏也带有升级系统，分为"生存”，“敏捷”与“战斗”三大技能
玩家初期三大技能树都贫瘠的时候，很辣鸡，渣渣的武器，攻击力低，打两下就生锈；体力差，超慢的上墙速度，跑两步就喘气，打两下就眼花，
要靠玩家剧情的不断深入与玩耍时间的增加，获取更多的技能点来提升，
但是达到满级时，又会突然发现，简直就是克傲天（玩家操纵的主角叫克莱恩，Crane）
有击打系统，可以拳击（即空手没武器时），可以脚踢（默认E键踢，我改成F），以及摔角里常见的Missile Dropkick（导弹式重脚踢）
很反科学，这游戏反正哪里都是不科学。不过用起来挺爽的，还能改文件力量踢上云霄
武器的特技有跳锤，还有360°回旋锤，以及高处落下击爆僵尸或人类的脑（刺客的光芒）等
消逝的光芒游戏自带拾荒探测技能，画面的显示给人一种外星人扫描的感觉一样，反观今年的各大作，都有拾荒与配件合成系统，确实是符合资源节约型社会发展潮流，
画面方面，赞一个，建筑与自然景观，地中海Style，不过那个远景确实是耗资源大户，1080P似乎要970才能全开，
游戏画面最大的两点就是"真实"的黑暗模拟，众所周知，“黑暗”在游戏里一向是被暧昧地渲染出来的，即“黑”得不“黑”，像比如使命召唤的各种需要带夜视镜的场景，其实不戴夜视镜也还是看得清，不是那种黑的伸手不见五指的情况，下水道画面阴暗出众，但是对于黑暗，也并非完全还原，为什么？因为黑成一片了，还玩毛啊？
但消光的开发商就是要大声地对世界说：“No”，在游戏中，进入黑夜，差不多晚上10点到2点的这时间，如果不照灯，那走在路上真的是黑成一片，真的是伸手不见五指，
而且黑暗中还埋伏着众多的丧尸，以及晚间日常Boss——夜魔，就是那些赤身裸体浑身烂肉红白相间怕紫外线的跑酷大师，100%的黑暗，算是业界一流水平吧，不愧是消逝着的光芒，黑得彻底，黑得让广州的歪果仁都心服口服。
由此，这游戏不但对硬件要求大，对显示屏要求也大，面板黑场越真实越好，一般的IPS一到晚上关了手电筒，那露点光，泛蓝，泛灰，真的是毁氛围。
游戏背景设置在一个叫“哈兰”的临海城市，对于该地区究竟在哪里玩家间曾有过热烈讨论，我认为差不多就是地中海那疙瘩的.
游戏剧情，可以说是最辣鸡的了，稀里糊涂空降到一个地区，稀里糊涂给一个不知名的叫什么GRE的卖命，自己的好兄弟和MMA女神相继死去，悲怆，然后那个一直以来的反派大BOSS赖斯，不知道跟你邂逅并打算杀死你有好多次了，但都没把你杀死，典型的烂片人物，那种宁愿装逼到死都不愿意一颗子弹正中靶心还废话老多的感觉，当然，最后猪脚与赖斯殊死搏斗，终于将其杀死，
总体就是，砍砍砍，跑跑跑，
主角的话挺多的，这点值得表扬，不像某些FPS，操纵的完全是哑巴，而且情感丰富，在好兄弟与女神快要死去的场景，都有实力配音的表现，这对于丰富人物形象有重要作用，更加生动逼真，有代入感，可是，主角克莱恩再丰富的内心活动，本质上也就是如孤岛惊魂4的阿杰盖勒那样的一个杀杀杀，任务任务任务的形象，个人观点。
呼。。。一本正经地打了这么多字，当初的那一段时间的上手感受确实记忆犹新，弥足珍贵，仍记得到2月跟吧友重开存档，联机联到午夜3点，四周也是黑黑的，好有气氛，屏幕前单机还是太孤独了老想捕捉一丝共同冒险的兄弟情。
自由度高，爬墙时能转动头部，这点比镜之边缘灵活，游戏元素与文化内涵丰富，画面不赖，还有业界最真实的黑夜模拟，只不过各种东拼西凑后，还真找不到主题了，剧情一级的水，但某些场面是做得挺好，比如那个主角产生的杰德妹子的幻象，总体来说挺不错的游戏，
波兰人在世界游戏界分量今年子一下子加重了好多好多
而我们的单机游戏.....市场情况，真的就要像国产造相机一样吗？

Tropico by nature isn't supposed to be a city builder, it's supposed to be a Political game, in other words it's a game where you literally make your own nation.  T4 gives you much more control and fine tuning to do these things.
Sure, T5 looks better, and it's easier to place buildings in perfect placement,  but it fails at it's core concept.
I don't explicitly reccomend either game, but if I had to reccomend one, it'd be T4.  It's cheaper, it's more true to the core concept of the series, and it doesn't have an astronomical amount of terrible nickle and diming DLC tacked onto it like T5 does.

I'm only just starting my Blender learning.  I initially chose Blender because it came highly recommended by those in the Unity development community.... and because it's free.  My ultimate goal is to be able to create game assets for some of the games I want to develop.  Being a solo developer at this point, even though it's complicated, I can't argue with the "free" part.  The fact that something like this is on Steam is also a bonus because it makes keeping up to date a breeze.
For those that are in a similar spot, considering Blender for a project but so far have been initially overwhelmed with its size and complexity, there is an excellent free online tutorial series by Neal Hirsig that starts from the absolute beginning, breaks things down, and starts from the basics to build up your Blender knowledge.  I highly recommend this tutorial series if you are considering learning Blender.
Speaking of tutorials and such, that's another reason why Blender is such a great program, despite having a huge learning curve.... the community!  There's hundreds, even thousands of people out there that have posted resources to demonstrate and help with an extremely wide variety of Blender functions.  You don't have far to look if you get stuck.
At any rate, even though I'm still new to it, I highly recommend Blender.
EDIT 7/22/15:  I think I'm just gonna stop trying to build models until AFTER I have finished all of the tutorials!  I finish one tutorial and figure "Hey that's neat!  I'm gonna try that!" and then a few tutorials later, I find out a completely super cool other method to do just what I wanted that requires 75% less work... and the end result looks a whole lot better no less!  The more material I cover, the more amazed I'm getting with Blender!  Even more of a thumbs up from me now!
EDIT 6/18/16:  Just thought I'd add another note stating that after a few months away from Blender, I decided to resume my learning on it and based on glowing reviews for CGCookie's Blender tutorial series, I decided to pay for a subscription.  So far it is quite excellent and even based on the limited amount I've progressed into it, I would highly recommend it as well as the previous video tutorial series by Neal Hirsig.
EDIT 7/5/16:  I know the purpose here is for me to provide a review of Blender and not provide reviews on the various tutorials out there, but I did run into a small snag with the CGCookie tutorial series and decided to try yet another tutorial course over at Udemy.  It is the one entitled "Learn 3D Modelling - The Complete Blender Creator Course".  It is absolutely excellent and fills in some of the holes left when working through the CGCookie course.  Be warned though, it is a paid course, though it is a one time fee and, in my opinion, completely worth it.
EDIT 1/18/17:  I took a bit of a hiatus from learning Blender, but have recently come back to it and I'm still with the Udemy course.  In fact, I'm only a third of the way through the course and already it's delving into even more powerful and wonderful features of Blender that I hadn't touched on in earlier tutorials.  This program never ceases to amaze me at what you can accomplish.... and for free!  That's the part that continues to utterly blow my mind!
So I guess here's the part where I actually expand on my review of Blender:  I have made it far enough into the tutorials I'm working through that I am thoroughly amazed with the power of Blender.  It is true that Blender has a rather steep learning curve, but I think a lot of the initial fear comes from the intimidating UI and, also in my case, the inability to understand the workflow of the 3D modelling process.  Well, after only a short while following through tutorials (most of which I am no more than a quarter of the way through so far), I can say that I am now able to navigate through and, most importantly, actually feel like I know what I'm doing to produce actual models.
TL;DR:  Follow a tutorial to help you learn Blender.  It seems hard at first appearance, but as your understanding grows, things get easier.

Saints Row IV is more insane,looney, and absurd than its last installment from the weapons, super powers,vertical exploration and story. The Saints are the only ones left of the human race to stop their species from being completely annihilated. Being divided and separated as prisoners of multiple alien ships you as the leader are tasked on bringing them back together for the final confrontation.
+Multiple parts to a quest (better integration with narrative)
+Switch between real life and simulation missions
-Main missions can get repetitive
There is multiple times where you will wake up from the simulation in order to do main missions that are important in order to confront the alien leader. The missions somewhat repeat since you are ultimately saving crew members over and over, but they tend to change up the narrative and the weapons available when doing so.
Quests can have multiple parts to them, depending on how the scenario develops, which flows better with the narrative. Making quests integrated better with the narrative was one of the main goals of the company since the third saints row game.

+Great variety of rewards (weapons)
The side missions offer a great variety of rewards from beating the objectives. Generally to get the rewards you will have to talk to your crew once you complete the list of quests they have for you. Not all rewards need to be claimed through the crew in order to obtain them especially the ones you get through stimulated instructions and customization quests.
The variety of gameplay is still strong here and very much like the last saints row, except a bit more geared towards superpowers in this installment. Each power has its own challenges you can find throughout the city whether its racing super fast paced checkpoints or using your telekinesis to throw people,cars, and objects through flashy points in a race against the clock.

+Vertical Exploration
-Same steelport as Saints Row 3
Locating them is the hard part - the simulation which is the main component of the game and where the free roam is at. It’s basically the map of steelport with some aesthetic changes, if you were looking forward to a brand new environment then you will be sorely disappointed. The only thing really added to steelport was more vertical exploration (aka) the actual beacon towers you can climb up and activate.

+Super powers make exploration feel fresh
-Vehicles and their customization becomes pointless
Free roam feels different in this game due to the super powers you gain. The super speed and ability to jump high really make traveling feel completely different and somewhat fun. This however ruins the point of traveling with vehicles and makes them nothing but background decoration and weapons to use in confrontations with their occasional use in side missions. Unfortunately making the vehicle customization pointless to even bother with besides gaining respect that’s not really worth the time investment into it.

+Powers offer new ways to combat enemies
+Elements are ways to change outcome of powers
The superpowers take a bit of exploration in order to really build up power in them since you are required to get the data packets scattered around the city. Don’t worry though by no means are they hard to find you can even do a mission that gives you the location of all of them on the mini-map. The superpowers have a decent amount of customization you can do to each power.
The elements change the outcome of powers, which results in 16 possible combinations of different abilities. For example adding explosion element to stomp will allow you to make huge area of effect chain explosions occur. Putting mind manipulation on your powers will also you to bend enemies to your will.
The weapons like the previous game have a great variety and come in all sorts of looney fun. Especially the weapons in the special category that are around 12 of those. The weapons have two ammo types, being cooldown and reload. This is especially good for players who normally deplete alot of their ammo since they can switch to a cooldown weapon that they don’t have ammo capacity for, or they can simply upgrade the capacity for weapons they do hold it.
+Vehicle Customization
+Homie Customization
Vehicles can still be customized from increasing durability, turning, and speed attributes to the paint job with body rigging. The cars are saved in your garage once you are done with your customization job, though it would be nice to be able to re-organize the list of vehicles in your garage. You can get rid of vehicles from the garage and keep solely the ones you want but there is no seeming way to actually change the order.
+Good variety (Drug Package, Money Pallet, Sex Doll, Photo Op)
There are 80 collectibles scattered throughout the city, in which appear as random events you can participate in or collect. They are a great way to earn some cash in-between missions while you are free roaming. Though the only reward collecting them all is the 10% increase in game completion for the save.
+Ability to call backup (vehicles,homies)
+Collecting money simplified
The ability to call backup is very helpful when you are in dangerous situations. Especially useful since it pauses the game essentially for you to start the call, not dieing when navigating menus is always a nice thing afterall. You can recruit up to 3 homies to help you at once, but once you hit the max it will not allow you to attempt to recruit anymore at the time. You also need to run to your homie to revive him so he can continue to help the homies.
Collecting money has been simplified to the point where you just need to open your phone and click on the icon to retrieve your earnings from all the places you tookover. Not having to go to a business or crib to collect money is a real welcome change.
Saints Row IV is a pretty good game despite its flaws and drawbacks as a result for reusing not only the same city but introducing super powers that undercut the fun of customizing vehicles and trying to steal awesome looking sports cars from pedestrians.

Braid is a beautiful art game which I believe often has its true beauty overlooked. Braid is fun and challenging, using time itself as a tool to overcome obstacles and solve puzzles. You start out able only to pause and rewind time to correct mistakes or "see the future" so to speak. As you progress, new mechanics are introduced as are bestowed upon you new techniques and tools. You could take only what I've mentioned so far and leave thinking that Braid was "pretty good."
Below that though, is a whole separate experience. Perhaps to the game's detriment though, you have to seek it. The most apparent theme of Braid is "fixing mistakes." There is no dying in Braid; any time you hit an enemy or fail into a pit, you simply rewind time and try again. Further than that though, you can find this same theme present throughout the story of a man's complicated relationship with his princess.
The final layer though, what really blew my mind in a way no video game ever has, occurs when you reach 100 percent completion of the game. In order to understand the full scale and beauty of Braid, you must get to this point. Use walkthroughs if you must; I did. It will turn everything you thought you knew inside-out.

I used to have a much more negative review, but the patches are consistent and this has become one of my favorite games. Great updates from the developer.
Now, although my review is much more positive and this is probably one of my top indie games, I still retain my old complaints from before:
You are referred to as "Player" which kindof kills the immersion. No way toname your character, no "Phillip Kindred" or "Phillip". Just "Player".
The forced permadeath (as opposed to optional) and flaws of RNG (instances where a NPC will appear with a gun 4 feet away at Round 1, and shoot you instantly killing you, or stepping out of the Cryo Center beginning and encountering a dogman.) are also a bit stupid at times.
When will developers learn that permadeath should always be optional? This is yet another developer who forces their playerbase to play the game the way the developer himself wants- not the way that is most fun. In this way, the bad design and RNG can instantly kill you, forcing you to lose hours of work!
So for the fundamentalist "force your playstyle down their throats" mentality so many roguelike devs have, I do not recommend this game. If you don't mind this playstyle, even when it is not fun, then I definitely recommend.
Also, the game is a bit easy once you learn the way to do things or read a guide. Once you learn that Spear + always 3 feet away = Easy Win in all Combat (unless they have a gun, in which you die instantly), some of the fun is taken away. Also, trapping turns the game into EZ mode.

The first of a stellar series of Metal Box Simulators. This one sees the hilariously ineffectual Chaos Warlord Bale ruin the good name of the Alpha Legion everywhere by being one of the most absurdly unsubtle oafs in the galaxy, as he tries to use the demonic Maledictum to transform himself into the Grandest Metal Box in the galaxy.
Naturally the Imperial Refuse Cleanup Division cannot allow such a scale of littering to occur and so the stage is set for the grandest of clashes and a rip roaring adventure as the Metal Box clad Blood Ravens get into other, larger and more swiftly moving Metal Boxes in order to thwart the evil of Chaos, who do much the same only with more spikes on their Metal Boxes. The Orks just wish they knew what a box was and the Eldar are too aloof to admit that boxes are a good idea, even as the Imperium repeatedly use Metal Boxes of all shapes and sizes to smash their silly floating hovercraft.
Also there's Sindri, a Chaos Sorcerer who almost makes up for Bale's stupidity, by being the most ridiculously moustache-twiddling villain you could picture, who's sole purpose in life seems to be to simply troll everyone he ever meets. In addition, Captain Angelos is one of the manliest men in gaming and Mordecai Toth and Carus Brom are pretty cool too. Even if their names are utterly absurd. Speaking of, there is an early boss called Orkamungus who calls Bale and his cronies "smelly boyz" and if that's not worth a five star review then I don't know what is.
In short, if you like Metal Boxes, a sublimely ridiculous story and more Metal Boxes then this is a game that you will love.

I want to like this game for the concept, but I simply can't and here's why: this entire game is built around randomness.
You can play for half an hour, only to run into a ship that is WAY more powerful than you could hope to be and die. That will happen a lot. It comprises probably half of my time with this game.
If you don't get lucky and encounter a merchant that sells a cloaking device or you just happen to not have enough scrap to purchase one because you haven't had many profitable encounters, enjoy losing the final fight when the boss's third stage uses an otherwise unavoidable and extremely high-damage superweapon. This is also true of many of the most useful weapons in the game.
Even the biggest reason to continue playing -- the chance to unlock new ships (of which there are many) -- is highly random. Steam says I've played 3.4 hours of this game, but I've really played closer to 8 or 9, and I've only unlocked 1 ship and I've never beaten the boss because something always shows up and completely screws me -- either I become trapped in a fight with a ship I could never hope to beat, or the scrap I earn is pathetically low due to lack of encounters or what-have-you, or I can't find tech I absolutely NEED to beat the boss. I might be able to get past this if I was able to consistently unlock new ship designs to try out to spice things up and give me a greater semblance of control over my playthrough, but even that is predicated on locations and events based on RNG.
If you're a masochist, you might like this game, but if you value your time, patience, and sanity you will not.

There are several reasons why this game is worth the money.
1. The game as a whole is sufficiently distinct for me to call it creative and new. I have never personally played anything like it before. If this type of game is not actually unique, then disregard this point.
2. The soundtrack is soothing and immersive.
3. The gameplay is fun and intelligent.
4. The game is appealing in that it allows you to captain (more like control) a starship in a science fiction setting.
Beyond these points, the game really just is an idea upon which should be expanded. It is very linear, and rightfully so. The game is challenging (at least for me it is) and merits multiple play-throughs. But I would be much more satisfied if I could return to this game and not have to race against the rebel fleet. I have played some of the mods for this game that allow this, but I would definitely play this game much more than I do if it permitted more freedom (although, admittedly, this might take away from the simplicity of the gameplay). Overall, worth playing.

It feels like gold to break enemy's shields and then cut their hull with laser! FTL got different unique races, augmentations, unlockable ships... Advanced Edition which came out in April of 2014 added to the gameplay a lot - new features, races, updated hud. Hard to believe it was free too. Game is an absolute must-own for sci-fi fans. Everyone else, buy it too!

10 Years Later, And It Keeps On Giving!
Ive always been a massive fan of the Wh40K Universe, and my love for Games Workshop and all things related, started 10 years ago with this game! I remember my brother pre-ordering  it, and he introduced me into the Universe, and I spent many years watching him play DoW. A few years later, I managed to get my hands on the great title, having been handed down a little beast of a PC ( or had been at the time anyway), and it was my first chance to unleash the power of the Space Marines unto those nasty orks, and the heretic forces of chaos. It was a 3 disk installation, and about a 3 hour wait ; before the game was properly onto the PC. It was well worth it, and the expansions that came out along the years added to the mayhem, it was all part of the experience. I stopped playing DoW as I got rid of my computer, as it was well outdated, and then I suppose it got forgotten in time.
Now back in present day, I became a part of the Steam community, and thought id dig around the room for some games I could add to steam. I found this little gem on my top shelf, so I thought I would give it a go and enter the cd key into steam, I was awfully excited! Put it onto my little laptop, 30 minute installation and I was away, ( so much for those 3 hours installs eh). It all came back to me when I started playing it once again, the music, the classic call of the space marines charging into battle. Me chanting “Burn The Heretic!”, while my Space Marines shoot the hell out of a squad of Chaos marines. Yes, all those requirements of a great RTS game, with hours and hours of enjoyment. You cannot go wrong with good old Dawn Of War, or rather i cannot anyway. The graphics may be quite outdated, and the multiplayer doesn’t hold much of a feature in the game nowadays,  however that certainly does not hinder any enjoyment at all.  Fan of the Wh40k Universe? Used to own the game, but not sure whether to return to serve the emperor? I recommend purchasing this game, and having a whole lot of fun playing it! I personally have a great deal of more of hours to enjoy on this game, reliving the moments of destruction and chaos.
In terms of gameplay elements, Dawn Of War still does not fail to be a very fun, and a practically great game. 10 Years Later And It Sure As Hell Keeps On Giving!
Overall:
+ Everything a classic RTS needs
+ Clever resource system
+ Immersive campaign to sink many hours into
+ Must buy for Warhammer 40k fans
+ Still great at 10 years of age
- Multiplayer servers not great
- Outdated Graphics
- Minor bugs
Solid 9/10
That goes it for my short Dawn of War Steam Review.

Braid is a beautiful art game which I believe often has its true beauty overlooked. Braid is fun and challenging, using time itself as a tool to overcome obstacles and solve puzzles. You start out able only to pause and rewind time to correct mistakes or "see the future" so to speak. As you progress, new mechanics are introduced as are bestowed upon you new techniques and tools. You could take only what I've mentioned so far and leave thinking that Braid was "pretty good."
Below that though, is a whole separate experience. Perhaps to the game's detriment though, you have to seek it. The most apparent theme of Braid is "fixing mistakes." There is no dying in Braid; any time you hit an enemy or fail into a pit, you simply rewind time and try again. Further than that though, you can find this same theme present throughout the story of a man's complicated relationship with his princess.
The final layer though, what really blew my mind in a way no video game ever has, occurs when you reach 100 percent completion of the game. In order to understand the full scale and beauty of Braid, you must get to this point. Use walkthroughs if you must; I did. It will turn everything you thought you knew inside-out.

is another Artifex Mundi game – one of their early productions, working with a young developer team: Tap It Games. It is a decent HOG to keep you busy for 2-3 hours straight with a subtle taste for noire. It is not exceptional compared to the rest of Artifex Mundi collections, but it is refreshingly well-done for the HOG genre itself anyway.
Our character, a lady private eye comes to the little town of Serpent Creek to investigate the disappearance of her journalist friend, Helen during Serpent Creek's famous Serpent Festival. We are quick to notice that there is an obscene amount of serpentine references going about the town; alongside mysterious disappearances, earthquakes and zombie-like citizens. The story gets more and more complicated between a moody hotel manager, a veteran sheriff, a suspicious British guest and a disturbingly oblivious mayor... What to do?
While the character modelling is appealing in animation, the psychological portrayal and demeanor designs of characters especially take the cake on this one. They are definitely interesting and elegant enough to keep you interested with the story revelation. People look and act similar to cover arts for classical Nancy Drew books with an extra dose of eerie and suspicion about them. You keep second guessing about characters, tying them to any kind of dreadful business the moment you see them. I won't lie, the outcome is not extraordinary, yet the display is certainly worth your time. The background artwork is also pretty and comes strong on establishing atmospheres.
The game contains some of the more imaginative puzzles that I've encountered within genre, alongside some entertaining lock picking puzzles. What I especially liked was investigation scenes where we are expected to pick up some clues around to deduce the recent happenings within the room. Hidden object scenes were ordinary if not a bit too easy. The usage of the map, action indicators and its teleportation feature are all present to bring you a relief for achievement hunting.
All in all, the game is worth the money for a HOG gamer, or anyone looking for a time kill with both noire and mystical atmosphere. If it is on sale, even better.

In 9 Clues: The Secret of Serpent Creek you play as a detective that drove to a town called Serpent Creek in order to help Helen, a friend who is also a reporter. During the story you are going to witness odd things that you can’t really explain while also meet strange characters who speak in an odd way or just show a strange behavior.
In order to advance in the story you will have to get certain items weather to unlock doors, cut fences or disable some switches. To get these objects you must play a classic hidden object mini-game every now and then or you may have to solve puzzles who may test your intellect but in the end you won’t have to struggle much to understand them. It is possible to choose the difficulty setting to your liking so that you can go through the game without worrying about penalties if you click on the wrong object for instance. Contrary to what the creator states in the “Features” page of the game, the game really gives you a big clue of who is the bad guy and who’s not so don’t mind the “Breathtaking plot full of unexpected twists” because the plot is really easy to follow and it’s really obvious about the main villain.
If you want some light-gaming experience and you like to solve mysteries, with some side puzzles, the game can offer you around 2-3 hours if you play at a normal rate. There’s no replay value unless you missed some clues and want to go back and start again in order to find them all.

I don't have a lot of experince with hidden object games but i've been curious about them and this happend to be my first and all and all not a bad experince.
You play some kind of detective searching for her lost friend in a creppy town with a thing for snakes.  You search the area, solve simple but fun puzzles and go through several hidden object segmeants and end up getting caught up in a lovecraftian mystery, albeit Yig instead of Cuthulu.
The art in the game is colorful (despite the whole thing taking place at night) and everything is well drawn.  The voice acting is nothing to write home about but its not terrible.  Overall its presented very well.
As far as adventure games go this one was pretty easy but still enjoyable. part of what makes most point and click games hard is trying to figure out what items and in what order your suppose to use them in.  Its pretty obvious what your supposed to do with most objects in this game but i find that rather refreshing given how mind bogglingly stupid some of the puzzles in other adventure games can be.
The game is aimed at more casual players.  If your ever lost you can look at your map to show you where theres a puzzle you need to solve and if your still stuck there is a recharging hint system.  That being said the game is pretty easy and can be beaten in about 3 hours without hints.  Also several puzzles are used mulitipule times and each hidden object location is used twice just with a new list of items.
The story is decent.  theres a small cast of colorful characters to interact with and the plot throws some twists and turns here and there but don't expect anything amazing.  Without spoiling anything you'll usally be able to tell who the bad guys are just by looking at them.  so the story feels kinda like a scooby doo mystery.  fun but nothing ground breaking.
Again i don't play many hidden object games so i can't really tell how it stacks up to others but judging it just as an adventure game i had fun.  Its got just enough challenge to give your brain a stretch without ever feeling like a pain.  give it a play if your looking for a lite adventure game.  though i don't know if i'd chose this as a launching point to test the waters of hidden object games.

Grim Dawn feels like a slightly less polished, much deeper Diablo 3.
The character models and voice acting aren't the greatest, but these are minor elements to an ARPG like this. Where this game excels is in the character building - you build your character from a pair of classes, allowing you to combine different elements of each to complement each other. Your build is also reinforced with a number of devotions, constellations which can be unlocked to provide additional stats, skills, and bonuses. The depth can be a little overwhelming at first, but the game is generous and keeps the cost of respeccing very low; the only permanent choices you cannot undo are the two classes you choose.
The skills and abilities are varied, interesting, and, importantly, fun. Each class is fun and different to play, and multiple builds available for each pairing (although admittedly some pairings are more difficult to excel with than others).
The loot drop-rate is generous enough to keep you interested, and it rarely feels like a chore to farm.
I've put in 450+ hours and have so many other builds I want to try and Grim Dawn just keeps pulling me back in. Highly recommended.

Ah, Battlefront 2. Such a classic. This game was one of my favorites back in the day when I had it on my Ps2, and for good reason. If you're wondering about picking up this classic on sale and if it still holds up to old memories, let me tell you that it does.
Sure, people compare SWBF2 to the modern Battlefront, but really they are completely different games just that just share the same name. SWBF2 stands on its own as one of the best games from the Ps2 era, and I think it's a bit unfair to compare those two games. I digress though, but SWBF2 is an incredible game nonetheless.
At its core, it's a first or third person shooter that involves the 4 major factions in the Star Wars universe. The campaign is the story of the 501st Clone Legion and how they rose from the Clone Wars all the way through to the fall of the Empire. The campaign itself isn't exactly deep or super revolutionary in terms of storytelling, but it does take you through just about every single map in the game and through some different objectives. The story itself is interesting, but once again, not exactly the deepest story around either.
Galactic conquest plays sort of like a board game where you pick one of the 4 factions, and the AI plays as the opposing faction. You each command a fleet to start off with as well as half the planets in the galaxy under your control. You take turns moving your fleets to other planets to engage in a battle in which the winner gains control of the planet as well as a large amount of credits than can be spent on training new unit types, bonus power-ups, or additional fleets. This game mode is a lot of fun, but not exactly the most challenging once you get a grasp for the game's mechanics.
Instant Action is exactly what the title implies. You are presented with a choice of game mode, faction, and map that you can play just for fun. It's great, quick, and easy to drop into a battle and enjoy yourself.
There isn't much to say that's bad about the game except for the AI being pretty stupid, but that's to be expected of a game of this age.
Bottom line is this game still kicks major♥♥♥♥♥ and is a definite great time to be had by all.

Note: This review is for Enemy Unknown. Enemy Within may have improved things. I may update this later.
I want to like this game a lot. The concept is cool, the visuals look good, the sound is atmospheric, and the soundtrack is amazing. It scores well with production value, and you are well immersed in that world. Unfortunately, it falls flat in gameplay.
I understand that thematically this is meant to be a challenging game. After all, it’s puny human weaponry versus the vastly superior alien technology. It’s supposed to be war, and war is hell. But the game design kind of takes this to absurd levels when the AI has to deliberately cheat in order to create this challenging world.
You’ve likely read testimonies about it already with all the reviews testifying to the fact that combat rolls are illogical and, at times, unreasonable. Examples of 99% close up shots routinely missing tell part of the story (trust me, you WILL miss shots that are seemingly unmissable). The evidence of the problems with combat rolling get exponentially more revealing when save scuming. This game doesn’t use a true RNG system to determine combat results. Results seem predetermined based on where characters are moved and whether the game wants hits or misses from the outcome. Every move will play the same way (with the same results) each time you play it, no matter how many times you play the same move. This creates a scenario of having to guess what the computer thinks is the right move rather than tactical planning and execution. It becomes rather stale and boring after a while (not to mention frustrating), and is a cheap why to simulate an artificial challenge that just feels frustrating an unfair most of the time.
To top off the lack of real RNG combat rolls, the player deals with a myriad of other issues, such as:
-Bugs and glitches.
-Illogical and inconsistent line of sight
-Teleporting enemies
-Abilities not triggering properly (usually to the AI’s benefit)
-Clunky UI and controls (especially a problem with multileveled areas)
-Auto save feature that conveniently forgets to save when the player successfully hits with overwatch.
-And other rule breaking garbage that conveniently helps the AI at the detriment of the player.
Make no mistake; this game does not play fair. It outright cheats and often breaks its own rules to screw the player over. If that isn’t enough, the game will outright mock the player while it’s happening. You’ll often hear your soldiers say things like, “I can’t believe that just happened”, “That’s Bull”, “Can’t kill it if you can’t hit it”. If that’s not proof that the designers intentionally used cheap design to simulate an artificially challenging game, I don’t know what is.
Another annoying problem is a puzzling one. You can customize many aspects about your characters. You can determine race, appearance, the color of their suits, their voices, and the gear they’re equipped with, but you can’t choose which class they are. That makes no sense at all. It can only be perceived as an attempt to keep players from stacking classes. Other than the fact that this makes little sense in a single player game, this is evidence of something else: the design team lacked the confidence that they balanced the classes correctly. With the cheap tricks from above, it’s evident that the design team wasn’t confident in its ability to create a balanced and challenging game either.
I can say that the base building aspects are the best part of the gameplay, and that aspect of the game is fairly basic. The theme of the game is cool and the story is decent for a strategy game. The voice acting is done well. The game had a lot going for it. It just fell flat with gameplay balance in battles, which is the meat of the game.
I can handle challenging games. I do so all the time. But it should be within reason. Artificial challenge and cheap tricks only make the experience feel unfair and frustrating. It’s a sign that the team lacked the talent to create a balanced game that could make the player feel like they lost due to merit rather than the game being fixed.
Frankly, I’m amazed that this game has gotten so much praise. But even a lot of the recommends tell about the serious flaws that will frustrate a lot of players. I guess there are just that many people who love brutal punishment. I’m not one of them. I want to love this game, but I hate it. This game is overrated.
I can only cautiously recommend if you’re a pain loving masochist that loves being unfairly punished. Otherwise, don’t waste your time.

One of Steam's best hidden gems.
The game feels like a cross between Fallout, DayZ, and even a little Project Zomboid sprinkled in. The game is really difficult yet it manages to make the experience fun. And when I say difficult I mean difficult, it's not a question of if you will die, it's more of a question WHEN will you die.
You start in a cryo facility completely nude, save for a hospital gown. This is a problem because un-like other survival games the temperature is a very important part of the game. If you're not wearing multiple layers of shirts as well as pants and shoes you will freeze to death minutes after you start.
The health system is really neat. It requires you to bandage each individual cut you receive. There are also injuries like broken bones that are severely crippling because of how little room you are given to carry things. The inventory system gives you a couple options: Carry it in your hands or if you have a backpack you can put it in there. Aside from that you can put things in your pants. However not even the largest backpack gives you a ton of room so every limb needs to be functioning for you to survive. There is also a range of illness that you can catch. They can be related to the cold, an infection from a cut, drinking/eating tainted water and food (respectively), and a whole host of other diseases that I've yet to experience.
TL;DR The health system is pretty intricate and requires dilligantly repairing yourself if you're going to live as well as being sanitary.
There are bandits and other monsters that prevent you from getting to comfortable. The combat in Neo Scavenger is also pretty realistic. If you fall over or get stunned it could be it for you. Or maybe not. Not everyone in this game is a blackbelt and the majority of people, including you will often stumble in combat or miss their attacks. In-fact even just charging at your enemy is a risky move becuse you could trip and open yourself up to being stomped. Guns in this game are well done and you won't become invincible if you can get one. They are decently common, however, ammo is not. You may be lucky to find maybe 6 rounds that fit into your gun. But guns are not completely uselss, though. A single bullet can end a fight. Being shot in the torso is enough to make you fall over and possibly passout, destined to either be looted and wake up naked and bleeding with your guts strewn about or to get stomped once your opponent has reached you. Bullets will also cripple/break bones so being shot in the leg or arm might not be directly fatal but the resulting infection/unability to carry things could be.
TL;DR Combat is also really realistic and fair (except for when the Bad Muthas are ganging up on you).
Crafting is also, unsurprisingly decently realistic. There isn't tons of stuff you can craft but what you can craft is realistic. For instance if you want to butcher the bandit you just killed, cook him up, and finally eat him there are several ways to do so. Unlike some games where you must have a certain tool this game allows you to use all sorts of simmilar tools to do the same thing. When you're butchering the dead bandit you can use nearly every sharp object in the game to complete this task. Crafting also will occasionally require that you have specific traits that are set up at the beggining of the game. There are a few vehicles that can be made/found and can be used to pull some of the crap you're carrying at a penalty to speed.
TL;DR There isn't much to say. Crafting is realistic but there isn't tons to make.

Basicallly, If you liked the orignial Company of Heroes then you should enjoy this game. It brings the focus to the eastern front and (if you havn't bought the Western Front Armies) you are given two main factions, the Whermacht and the Red army. Each plays indvidually and while it does share many similarties with the original CoH, it brings a new element by giving you mutliple options  for commanders who operate similarliy to the commanders from CoH. It also utilises a new sight system, the abilitlie to climb walls and things like Blizzards which can your troops from hypothermia or deep snow/mud which slow down all units considerably. The graphics are also considerably improved.
Sadly, this game is plagued by microtransactions, Some very OP commanders can only be bought as well as countless other asethetic things. However, they have tried to fix this problem with the war spoils system, although this still doesn't really fix this due to the rareness of the drops. I personally did not like the campaign and the theater or war missions are either too boring, too hard or too expensive. There is also a constant majority of German players, however if played correctly, either faction can be very strong. With the arrival of the DLC, there is many changes to the base game like new UI and customization system, but the new factions don't feel ... new, they just feel similar. Also, the common Commanders of the Americans are flat out rubbish compared to the oberkommando, in fact, I really wanted to see to more variety in commanders for all the factions rather than a small set with each with lots of really cool, fun looking commanders sitting in the store page.
Overall, I do enjoy this game, but I honestly still prefer the original CoH, I have sunk many frustrating hours into this game, but with the preogressions sytem now rendered useless, and many fun commanders (like the Kv-2 one) sitting beyond my wallets reach, I am not sure for how much longer I can keep playing. Be careful when purchasing this, for 29.99 (as of the release of this review) you'd be better off buying the DLC wich still lets you play the game with more intresting factions. Out of 10, I disapointdley must rate it at no higher than a 7/10. But, I must empahsise, I do enjoy playing it!

If you don't get lucky and encounter a merchant that sells a cloaking device or you just happen to not have enough scrap to purchase one because you haven't had many profitable encounters, enjoy losing the final fight when the boss's third stage uses an otherwise unavoidable and extremely high-damage superweapon. This is also true of many of the most useful weapons in the game.
Even the biggest reason to continue playing -- the chance to unlock new ships (of which there are many) -- is highly random. Steam says I've played 3.4 hours of this game, but I've really played closer to 8 or 9, and I've only unlocked 1 ship and I've never beaten the boss because something always shows up and completely screws me -- either I become trapped in a fight with a ship I could never hope to beat, or the scrap I earn is pathetically low due to lack of encounters or what-have-you, or I can't find tech I absolutely NEED to beat the boss. I might be able to get past this if I was able to consistently unlock new ship designs to try out to spice things up and give me a greater semblance of control over my playthrough, but even that is predicated on locations and events based on RNG.
If you're a masochist, you might like this game, but if you value your time, patience, and sanity you will not.

So I'm not giving this a thumbs down because of the "Ark ripoff" everyone seems to be claiming. Honestly, I've never really played Ark, maybe once or twice for a few minutes, but never got into it.
Now, I don't *want* to give this a negative review, as this game seems to hold a lot of potential. I saw a glimpse of this game during E3 and thought it looked really cool, and I've been waiting for it ever since. But at the current time of its release, I feel it's more of a "hold off until future updates" review. The game looks nice, and basic controls and UI system, from what I could gather, aren't that bad. Honestly, I don't mind the idea of a "Fantasy themed Ark" game, even though I've practically never played Ark. Either way, this game should be reviewed on its own accord, not what it might be based off of.
But, from the bit I've played (yes, I realize I only have 0.3 hours on record atm), it seems unpolished and unoptimized. I have a pretty good computer (GTX 1070, along with 6 core 3.2ghz gpu and 16gb RAM), and even on medium settings, I have low frame-rate, to the point to where everything feels very stuttery and awkward. Unfortunately, this has prevented me from actually getting into the game to see everything it has to offer, considering I feel like I can't really control my character to begin with. it's also definitely not worth the current price of $30 (or even the $25 sale it's currently on).
Menu's seem fine, world looks expansive and could look gorgeous if I could play on higher settings, and the skill system even looks interesting. Again, this game *looks* good, but it doesn't play well. So, ultimately, I suggest holding off til future updates to see if they fix these issues. If you have an absolute beast of a computer that can handle anything, then go for it. You can always refund the game if you experience similar issues.

Lets split this review into good, bad an neutral. Then for those who want a more in depth review I'll add a little blurb at the bottom.
Good:
-Very well done combat. Honestly every class feels unique and there are so many abilities that its unreal. PVP is engaging and has a good dynamic. It plays like an mmo fighting game.
-Graphics: Out of most mmos ive played, the graphics are pretty top notch and it doesnt run half bad. With my r9-390 OC'd a tad, i can play at 60fps in all the places it really matters.
-Afk grind: As a full time student studying in a pretty hard program i still havent felt far behind ever in BDO. Due the the afk nature of the game you can set up builders and workers and make a node empire to rake in millions overnight along with things like afk fishing and cooking. Sadly you must leave your comp running 24/7 for this (which is why me and many others have so many hours).
-character creation: Me and my friends have started referring to the game as waifu simulator online. A game where you make a waifu and level them up to destroy other peoples waifus. Its really well done and the posibilities are crazy.
Neutral:
-Progression: The gear grind is pretty fun, and ehancment isnt too bad until you start getting to TRI/TET (+18/+19) levels of gear. Here it becomes heavily rng dependent which can be off putting. Personally for someone like myself whos played other grindy games like runescape and TERA, it really isnt hard getting to TRI which would put you well above the average player.
-Story/Questing: These are pretty generic quests, dont really expect a story here. The nice part is not a single quest is required (other than maybe the ones to snag some extra inventory space) meaning you wont have the runescape issue of needing to claw your eyes out to get a certain ability.
-Skilling: Not my favourite part of the game but its a big aspect of it. If you want a game where you can just be a farmer, or a fisherman and sail the seas catching fish and selling them, then you can do that. The problem is that these parts of the game arent meant to be a full game themselves so each skill feels kind of shallow, and some skills like hunting I have not touched once since owning the game and havent even been given an introduction to them. However skipping these isnt missing much.
The bad:
-First of allthe game isnt a $10 game as it would have you believe. This game is basically a f2p game that gives you (IMO) more than $10 worth of goodies up front if you play for the whole beginner attendence awards. If you want to grind mobs for cash youll need at least 5 t1 pets which will run you $10 each. Additionally there is a quasi-subscription called a value pack which can give players a tax break at the marketplace. These little things all add up in a way where the game isnt pay to win, but it skirts the line of what people would find acceptable. For $10 up front though this makes sense and you dont NEED to buy into it more, you just need to work around it. On top of that many of these purchases are character bound NOT family bound, so besides pets, think really hard what your main character will be.
-Customization: Sadly there isnt many ways to customize your waifus clothes. Your given a free soldier outfit during a quest in the main story, but besides that you cant change how you look without spending cash on either a value pack for the free dye pallatte that comes with it. or on a costume which costs about $20.
-class balance: certain classes like musa at the time of writing are straight garbage. Witch and Wizard after years of time are still top tier in grinding and node wars with no indication that will change.
Overall: I'd give the game a 8.4/10. However if you arent a fan of korean MMO's or the grind, and dont want to open your wallet a tad to get into it, then the game isnt for you. Regardless if you can get it on sale, or need a game to tie you over till your favourite games new dlc comes out, its definitly worth it.

Note: This review is for Enemy Unknown. Enemy Within may have improved things. I may update this later.
I want to like this game a lot. The concept is cool, the visuals look good, the sound is atmospheric, and the soundtrack is amazing. It scores well with production value, and you are well immersed in that world. Unfortunately, it falls flat in gameplay.
I understand that thematically this is meant to be a challenging game. After all, it’s puny human weaponry versus the vastly superior alien technology. It’s supposed to be war, and war is hell. But the game design kind of takes this to absurd levels when the AI has to deliberately cheat in order to create this challenging world.
You’ve likely read testimonies about it already with all the reviews testifying to the fact that combat rolls are illogical and, at times, unreasonable. Examples of 99% close up shots routinely missing tell part of the story (trust me, you WILL miss shots that are seemingly unmissable). The evidence of the problems with combat rolling get exponentially more revealing when save scuming. This game doesn’t use a true RNG system to determine combat results. Results seem predetermined based on where characters are moved and whether the game wants hits or misses from the outcome. Every move will play the same way (with the same results) each time you play it, no matter how many times you play the same move. This creates a scenario of having to guess what the computer thinks is the right move rather than tactical planning and execution. It becomes rather stale and boring after a while (not to mention frustrating), and is a cheap why to simulate an artificial challenge that just feels frustrating an unfair most of the time.
To top off the lack of real RNG combat rolls, the player deals with a myriad of other issues, such as:
-Bugs and glitches.
-Illogical and inconsistent line of sight
-Teleporting enemies
-Abilities not triggering properly (usually to the AI’s benefit)
-Clunky UI and controls (especially a problem with multileveled areas)
-Auto save feature that conveniently forgets to save when the player successfully hits with overwatch.
-And other rule breaking garbage that conveniently helps the AI at the detriment of the player.
Make no mistake; this game does not play fair. It outright cheats and often breaks its own rules to screw the player over. If that isn’t enough, the game will outright mock the player while it’s happening. You’ll often hear your soldiers say things like, “I can’t believe that just happened”, “That’s Bull”, “Can’t kill it if you can’t hit it”. If that’s not proof that the designers intentionally used cheap design to simulate an artificially challenging game, I don’t know what is.
Another annoying problem is a puzzling one. You can customize many aspects about your characters. You can determine race, appearance, the color of their suits, their voices, and the gear they’re equipped with, but you can’t choose which class they are. That makes no sense at all. It can only be perceived as an attempt to keep players from stacking classes. Other than the fact that this makes little sense in a single player game, this is evidence of something else: the design team lacked the confidence that they balanced the classes correctly. With the cheap tricks from above, it’s evident that the design team wasn’t confident in its ability to create a balanced and challenging game either.
I can say that the base building aspects are the best part of the gameplay, and that aspect of the game is fairly basic. The theme of the game is cool and the story is decent for a strategy game. The voice acting is done well. The game had a lot going for it. It just fell flat with gameplay balance in battles, which is the meat of the game.
I can handle challenging games. I do so all the time. But it should be within reason. Artificial challenge and cheap tricks only make the experience feel unfair and frustrating. It’s a sign that the team lacked the talent to create a balanced game that could make the player feel like they lost due to merit rather than the game being fixed.
Frankly, I’m amazed that this game has gotten so much praise. But even a lot of the recommends tell about the serious flaws that will frustrate a lot of players. I guess there are just that many people who love brutal punishment. I’m not one of them. I want to love this game, but I hate it. This game is overrated.
I can only cautiously recommend if you’re a pain loving masochist that loves being unfairly punished. Otherwise, don’t waste your time.

Ok so this game is ... addictive.
A nice post apocalyptic setup with one of the most detailed crafting systems I've ever seen. Also the game makes real use of the character skills, just like in old school RPG's - ain't got melee skill? Well, ain't gonna craft the best melee weapons, for example.
As it is some kind of rouge like, there's no saving to be safe, it's just go for it and hope that you won't mess up, which leads to some pretty frustrating moments but also is part of the addictive character of the game. Closed the game more then one time during my 15 ingame hours but came back every time to start a new character.
The combat system is kind of strange in the first few tries but as soon as you get the hang of it, it is really fun. It works turn based and you choose your actions as the enemies choose theirs, after that the outcome is shown in a textfield with lots of pretty brutal stuff, from arrows to the knee to wolffangs to your face.
The graphic is not up to date, instead it is real outdated but this game is not about graphics, it's about imagination. Many encounters contain lots and lots of written text (remember Fallout 1/2 or Baldurs Gate conversations? - you won't find those conversations but massive ambient text).
Features:
- nice ambient text
- great crafting system, starting from making glas shards out of bottles over crafting armor from hides and furs to upgrade weapons with scopes for example
- huge bunch of neat items with degeneration
- deep skillsystem with skills giving options on encounters (but skills are chosen on character creation and can't be trained)
- big range of enemies starting from cannibal gangs over strange mutants up to paramilitary townguards (if you decide to attack them)
- extensive character needs, from hunger and thirst over induced pain to warmth (yes, you can freeze and expect to do so often in the beginning)
-rouge like: saving only by leaving the game, a dead character stays dead but a nice little statistic when died shows some of the players accomplishments
- one of the most stable early access games I've ever played with a range of features and stuff that outruns some released games by far
- big, randomly created (open) world with some points of interest
- devs active on steam forum
If you like challenging games which are more about ambient then shiny graphics, show those devs some love and give it a try (there's also a demo which I highly recommend to play to be sure this kind of game suites you).

Dying Light is a first-person zombie apocalypse-themed game set in an open world. Players traverse an expansive urban environment overrun by a vicious epidemic, scavenging the world for supplies and crafting weapons to defend against the growing infected population with a heavy focus on parkour mechanics, allowing players to perform actions such as climbing ledges, leaping off from edges, sliding, jumping from roofs to roofs and zip-lining. Parkour mechanics also applied on combat. Players can perform action such as drop-kicking when engaging combat with enemies. A grappling hook is also featured in the game, allowing players to climb up buildings and travel between places quickly.
The game is mostly melee-based with the majority of fighting using melee weapons. There are more than 100 weapons that can be used and more than 1000 weapon possibilities when players begin crafting new weapons. The melee-weapons have a limited lifespan and will be degraded and eventually broken if the player uses them for combat for a long time. Players can repair a weapon a limited number of times. Crafting weapons require crafting ingredients such as gauze and metal parts and a blueprint, which can be scavenged or purchased from a shop. Guns are also featured in the game, but players will only gain access to it in the later half of the game. However, ammo is often very scarce. The variety of guns consists of two types of assault rifles and a variety of small firearms and shotguns. Gun customization is very limited but guns don't break or become unusable after an extended amount of use.
Dying Light contains a dynamic day and night cycle. During the day, the player has to go out and scavenge for supplies to send back to the safe zones. They can set up traps, save random survivors, and make their way to airdrops. The infected are slow, apathetic, and easily visible, allowing the player to simply make their way past them, but their danger grows in numbers. Players can also use environmental traps, such as spikes and electrified fences to kill the infected. Lead game designer Maciej Binkowski stated that day time will last for approximately 64 minutes, while night time will last for approximately 7 minutes. The game also features a physics-based lighting system and a dynamic weather system, which includes a variety of conditions such as fog, rain, and wind. I highly recommend Dying Light it is the best open world zombie survival i have ever played!

If there's a kind of game that I can't stand, those are the Rogue-like games. They're, most of the time, luck-based, and you need to brain, skills, and sometimes you don't even need hands to play them. Faster Than Light is one of those exceptions that put the others to shame. While I hate the others, I just can't bring myself to hate FTL, it shines were others fail miserably. Is it perfect, though? No. As usual, I'll start taking the bad stuff out of the way first:
The biggest problem beyond the others, is that it's still luck-based. Not AS luck-based as the others, I might add, but being lucky is required in a lot of situations. Let me explain: During the game, you can choose what to upgrade or install. That's great, giving the player freedom. What's not cool, is some of those expansions being kind of needed during the final battle, and not having them meaning the difference between a last-minute Game Over, and achieving Victory. One of those being the Cloak. Being invisible and getting insane Evasion for a few seconds is NEEEDED during the Final Battle, but in one of my playthroughs, I ran to shop to shop (were, if they sell Expansions, only 3 will be available), AND I DIDN'T FIND IT, IN NOONE OF THE 13 SHOPS I RAN INTO. YES, I COUNTED THEM, THAT'S HOW MUCH IT♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ME OFF. WHY!? BECAUSE THAT'S ALL I NEEDED TO BEAT THE GAME! It was a perfect oportunity, had the best Load-out, and only needed the Cloak. Well, f#ck you too, Luck-based gameplay!
The other main issue here, is the lenght of the game. Yes, you can replay the game a sh#t-load of times and it won't get old that soon, but that doesn't make it easier to understand why they made it so short. You can beat it in an hour, less if you're lucky. But hey, you won't make it there without luck, so expect to start from scratch over, and over, and over.
The last issue is a minor one, really. Everything is randomly generated, as I said, but because of that, you often end up in hilarious battles that make no sense, and you can beat them by just staring at the screen. An example, would be the Auto-Scout ships with no shields in Asteroid fields. Those ships will only stand a few hits, but without shields, the asteroids will hit it non-stop, and the battle will last arround 5 to 10 seconds. Other times, enemies try to board your ship, even though you're using a Lanius ship, and that there's NO OXYGEN ON YOUR SHIP, so they pretty much instantly choke to death inside in some pathetic attempt of stealing your sh#t.
Now, let's go to the good stuff. The gameplay is extremely well done, and without counting the IA and the Random generator doing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crap, you'll have some serious fun being the tactical ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you desire to be.
Will you load your ship with missiles and just blow your way out of there? Will you mount it with more and bigger lasers than the Death Star? Will you use robots to do your dirty job while you other more interesting stuff? Will you just board them, kill them, and steal their crap? Or will you just ignore them all and run away? It's up to you, and there's room for strategy to be made, specially with the Expansions you can install. Some of them turn your ship invisible for a few seconds, making it impossible to hit, others let you mind-control one of them for a few seconds and turn it against them, others let you hack their ship's stuff, you get the idea.
Another big point in favor of the game, is the music. It has been done to perfection. It seriously fits the action, and it also changes really smoothly from ambient music to combat music. The sounds are also okay, but don't expect to hear any voices, since the game is done in a more "Old-school" and "minimalistic" style. There's also A TON of references to films, series and games, related to space or not...But a ton of them are from Star Wars. See if you get them when you see them.
Something that you should take into account are the mods. This game already has a sh#t-load of mods out there, and some of them seriously make it even better (like the Captain's Edition). I remember one, for example, that lets you keep ongoing forever, making playthroughs last as much as you want them. That's a fine example of  what the game needed, and thanks to the PC Master Race's best asset, the modding comunity, we got that fixed.

This game is a small jewel.
Short, but challenging - for the mind, not the fingers - with a wonderful storyline, but most of all it truly achieves something that many other videogames (and art works in general) fail to reach: true connectedness between its constitutive elements, gameplay and storyline.
Where most games are made of a) gameplay and b) story, as two separate elements, here the nature of time and therefore the puzzles to be solved would not make sense without the narrative, and actually make the narrative "concrete".
Braid is a post-modern work of art, if only for the explicit tribute to Super Mario, whose elements are used in new ways and assume different (and deeper) significance; and the marvellously moving final act, when the same action shifts in meaning when represented backwards.
The story is told in short fragments, each introducing a world with different time-rules, but it is compelling from the start, and will claim a place in your heart before you even notice

This is a generic, by-the-numbers scrolling shooter that someone might create by following the instructions on how to make your first flash game.  It has everything you'd expect in a generic scrolling shooter, but absolutely nothing to recommend it; the weapons are poorly-balanced and awarded at random, the enemies are repetitive and uninteresting, and the graphics (the only remotely original thing about the game) are ugly.
The difficulty is all over the map; bosses tend to be extremely easy, while a few levels are difficult just because they throw a large amount of stuff at you.  Nothing in the game feels new or interesting, though, and even the bosses are frequently repeated.  The plot in the game description is present nowhere in the game; there's not even a bit of scrolling text in the intro or when you beat the game (which can be done within an hour.)  The game feels like it could be an asset flip, although I'm not inclined to research any further to see if that's really the case.
Unless you're playing bad games just to see the depths of what Steam has to offer, I suggest you skip this one.

Oh boy. Where to start.
I had great hopes for this game since its initial announcement, ten years ago. Been following its development forever. When it changed from an MMORPG to a survival game, I persisted. When initial screenshots and gameplay videos came out, I rejoiced - the graphics looked awesome, great fantasy elements: exactly what I wanted.
Then came day one. The game is badly optimized - on a GTX 1050, with everything set to low, I was getting an fps of 35. Sounds doable, no? It is until you realize how utterly crap the graphics look at that setting. Setting everything to max, I got 15 fps. Yet, the graphics still looked nothing like the ones shown to me in the previews. The graphics were a letdown. I was distraught.
Secondly, this seems like an ARK: Survival Evolved clone - sure, it has more fantastical elements to it, but the core mechanics remained the same. Why play this when you can play another better, more finished, game? The game is currently only 30% finished - I suppose it is becoming a recurring theme in early access titles, fleshing out barely-finished games to garner some additional capital for development, but for the player, there is absolutely nothing to gain by playing it now. In less than an hour, server populations decreased to an absolute minimum - many quickly became tired and bored of the game at its current state. There are few mechanics within the game that incorporate creative, fantastical elements, like the fairies and magic - but the overall feel I receive may simply be summed up in two words - unpolished and rushed.
Thirdly, server size. The game boasted about factional wars. It began with 500, Then 200, Then 100. Finally, today, it was 70. I suppose, given how badly optimized it is, there was no choice but to limit server populations to such a small number. Factional wars are doable, but they're just not at the scales I, and many others, expected them to be.
In conclusion, I see no reason to purchase the game in its current state except for supporting the developers, who have worked on this title for over 10 years. However, be cautious - as this game will likely sit in your library, untouched after an initial exploration, for many years to come before the developers get their stuff together. Overall, I am disappointed with this EA release.
