In
, you play as unnamed detective who receives an urgent phone call from long-time friend Helen asking for you to save her.  As soon as you make it to Serpent Creek, you are met with the strange and supernatural when a serpentine creature smashes into the windshield of your car.  This sets the tone for the rest of the story as you journey from location to location searching for clues regarding Helen’s disappearance and the strange behavior of the locals.
There are three difficulty settings.  On easy, the hidden object puzzles and detective puzzles are pointed out to you with particle effects, while on hard, you receive very little information from your mouse cursor.  The description also says there is a penalty for misclicks on hard difficulty, but even when I spam clicked during the puzzles, I did not see a penalty of any form, so I can’t really attest to what that means.  Lastly, there is a clock on the user interface (UI) that allows you to skip puzzles or receive hints.  Supposedly this takes a very long time to recharge on hard mode, but it did not have a noticeable impact on gameplay, and I did not think the game was difficult enough to even warrant using it.
The user interface is simple, easily controlled, and excellently laid out in the help/tutorial menu.  The only complaint is that it can seem a bit large, cramping the screen (and I play on a large monitor).  However, it is not an issue that I thought was pervasive enough to be a hindrance in any form.  Also, many of the conversations and cuts scenes are skippable, so that is a plus (especially on your second or third playthrough).
This game has limited replayability.  On all three difficulty levels, the storyline and puzzle progression is exactly the same.  Therefore, replaying the game is not very useful, save to get the accomplishments you did not get on the first play through.  The hardest accomplishment is the 9 hidden clue icons you collect throughout the game, and a replay is almost a necessity as some clues are in areas you can only enter once.
This game retails for $10 USD.  I played through the game in one sitting for what was probably about four to five hours (first play through on hard difficulty, if on easy, probably would have been a bit shorter).  This tells me the game was about $2 / Hr., which is a decent value.
However, I am very miserly in my video game purchases waiting for really good deals before I decide to purchase a game.  If I came across this game for $10, I probably wouldn’t purchase it regardless of the reviews.  I simply cannot justify to myself $10 for something I will play once and then forget about.  So how did I come about this game?  There is currently an Artifex Mundi bundle from
for roughly $2.50.  For this price, the game is definitely worth its cost.
9 Clues: The Secret of Serpent Creek is a short but fun point and click adventure with an atmospheric vibe.  It is not scary, or unsettling (unless you are ophidiophobic of course), but it is not campy either.  It doesn’t try to be the game of the year, but it is solid.  The story is thought out, the controls are very to use, the graphics are pleasing (the hand brush painted type of graphics where there’s not so much animation, but rather layering images on top of each other in sequence), and most importantly, there are very few to no glitches (I heard someone say something about one in Linux, but I’m Win7).  This was a fun break from other types of games and gave me an enjoyable morning.
I recommend this game if you can find a deal on it, or if $10 is not an issue for you.  Again, this is not because there is anything wrong with the game, just that it is short and has limited replay value.

Now, this review may be slightly bias, due to the days worth of playtime under my belt from when I was a kid.
For starters, this is easily one of my top 5 Star Wars games of all time, if not the top. The PC version has slightly different menus than the PS2 version I remember, but other than that, everything else is there.
Frankly, I don't know why LucasArts thought they should make an entirely new battlefront, in my opinion, they could have easily copied BF2, touched up the graphics a lot, added some more modes, planets, heroes, more campaigns and maybe some other things nobody asked for, and it would pass as a successful game. Let's be honest, Battlefront 2 is better than Battlefront 2015, and if you use the excuse of 'Yeah but the 2015 graphics are better', my friend, PC modding has already taken care of that. HD textures.
Now, onto Multiplayer.
Not gonna lie, haven't actually played it yet. Granted, GameSpy brought down the servers early 2014, but dedicated fans out there have created mods that can still allow like-minded players to contrinue playing this great game with others, so it won't be long before I give it a shot.
Campaign? Inventive, interesting, and I feel is rather a high point of the game. Follows a specific company of clone troopers throughout the galaxy, showing everything from the first battle of Geonosis, to the excecution of order 66 and the clone's transition to the empire. Added with the fact that these missions aren't just 'Do what you normally do in regular gameplay but don't lose', they actually have really enjoyable mini-quests. Though sometimes, the missions can get a bit hard. Felucia for example. Acklays, man.
In my opinion, the game's only flaws are in its classes, and balancing. There are some issues with some specific things in the game being overpowered. For example, Bothan Spies. The disintegration gun is far too powerful in my opinion, and added with their ability to turn invisible, it can really screw you over. Second issue is with the Gamorrean guards in Jabba's Palace. Granted, they're not a playable class, but still, they get in your way, and are hostile to everyone, not to mention the fact that there is no way to make them stop spawning. You may be asking what my issue is with them. Oh I dunno, maybe the fact that they can ONE HIT KILL ANYTHING. Boba Fett for example.
As an honourable mention, I think that Space Battles are definitely one of the best parts of the game. Its just a shame that it took until Rogue Squadron on the PSP to allow for ground AND space battles in one (Correct me if I'm wrong but I believe RS was the first BF game to actually allow that). But then again, that's just me being picky.
Overall, this game is a huge hit in my books, and is easily better than some of the stuff A-List publishers roll out today. No DLCs, no extra content, no pay-to-win, just the base game, in all its glory. And what a lot of glory it has.
My Laptop is absolute bantha fodder, and it can run this game on lowest graphics with complete ease, rarely goes below 50fps, and when it does, its most likely due to the fact that I'm playing XL on Hoth, or just when there's an absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of AI on the screen at once.
Definitely give this game a go, if you can look past the graphics; which aren't even that bad considering when it was made, then this game is a real gem, and I'd encourage anyone to pick up a copy and get stuck in.
EDIT: New computer plays fine, just has issues with the whole audio jack thing. How to combat: just stick a wire into the audio jack if it crashes upon loading the map.

A great turn-based strategy game with RPG elements. There are many aspects I like about this game, including the combat mechanics; although the game can occasionally seem unfair (how could I miss with 80% hit chance?), it is actually a well-thought out system that works very well for the most part. I like how there are two different play modes - one is the on ground combat, and the other is managing your base. Think of the management aspect like a simplified Civ game. You are responsible for hiring scientists and engineers, building specific rooms, managing finances, hiring soldiers, deciding which soldiers to genetically modify, to name but a few. I also like the way each solider type (heavy, assault, support, and sniper) have their own tech trees. They are slightly limited, but enough to keep it interesting. The expansion adds plenty of content, such as new missions, weapons, and enemies.
Negatives are fairly minor. I feel there could have been more environment types (they get very stale after a while). Animations are sometimes a bit off, not enough to ruin the flow of the game, but they are noticeable. There is one enemy where their turn takes way too long, and can be irritating to wait for it to finish, especially when you are looking to load to a previous save.
Overall, a fantastic turn-based strategy game. Certainly one of my favourite stratey games. If you are late to the game like I was and enjoying good strategy, I recommend buying this ASAP.

After 75 hours, I believe I can make an honest review on this game.
Pros
------
* Free to play. Downloaded for free, played it, don't like it? Unistall. Not a dime spent.
* You can build defenses for your base, alongside your team. And then the mayhem begins!
*You gain exp and gold as you play matches and level up, which can be used to buy and upgrade perks, and heroes.
* Daily missions = more gold
*Perks have an upside, and a downside. So technically speaking, Default is best, but perks are an extra bit of help
* Map editor allows you to create maps of your own, which you can publish and edit whenever you want.
* Free Hero Rotations allow for learning who you like to play.
*This game is very easy to learn, a few steam user guides and you'll be a pro.
*As you level Heroes you will game skins for your blocks, as well as gold and some badges.
Cons
------
*Long queue times. (I usually run from 2-4 minutes in the day, 4-6 minutes at night.[This can be lowered by checking the shorthanded games button])
*Cosmetics for your characters can only be bought with platinum (pay to get currency). So most skins can't be bought for free.
* only 1 or 2 devs work on this game. Updates are pretty slow. (I imagine if the game becomes popular, move devs may want to work on it)
* A lot of Noobs vs. Pros games will happen on casual play
* You need to play a lot for enough gold to get a higher tier Hero.
Money
--------
Money will only NEED to be spent on skins, other items can be bought with gold. But, with that note, the highest price for any skin is around less than $6 (USD). And that is just for the high tier skins.
------------
Conclusion
------------
Great game, although it has flaws. But no game is perfect. If you have had any thoughts of playing it, go ahead, download it. It's free, so if you don't care for it, no money lost. Don't resist playing the game just because of negative reviews, try it out. I have fun with it.

JellyNoid is a simple game in which you have to destroy groups of jellies at the top of the screen, using a ball.
You control a log (at the bottom of the screen) to bounce the ball, guiding it towards the jellies.
The ball can also bounce off the sides of the screen.
If the ball misses the log, and goes under, then you lose the game.
Sometimes a plane will appear overhead, dropping hearts (if caught, they give extra lives for the log) and brown lumps (if one hits the log, you lose a life). The bouncing ball can destroy the plane, but if the plane then crashes into your log, you lose.
In later stages, some of the jellies will drop circular blades - each one that hits your log will make your log lose a life (those later stages can be much more challenging than the earlier ones).
If your log runs out of lives, you lose.
Sometimes the physics can seem a bit off, but that's bearable. For example, quite a few times I have seen the ball hit the side, from which it should bounce across the screen, but instead it goes straight down.
It's quite a basic game, which should be fine for children, or for adults who want a bit of a time-waster.
JellyNoid is not the greatest game out there, but nor is it meant to be.
If you buy it as a bit of cheap entertainment, then you should get your money's worth out of it.

I really like Neo Scavenger. That's why there will be a long, LONG review on it. To Start, in even a short time of five hours, this game has left a great impression on me, from death to art style to dialogues... It's brilliant to begin with.
Gameplay: You wake up in the middle of Michigan in some sort of year, in which humanity is back to the dark ages. Heal yourself, fight, scavenge, explore, talk, DAMN. And more. Every choice is better then Mass Effect's Endings and choices. DAAAAMN. 10/10
Story/Quests: Survive in the apocalypse, find out who you are, DUN DUN DUN! Kinda cliche, but I will give the quests and random encounters credit. 7/10
Dialogues: Pretty long, and most of the lore is delivered through it, which was somewhat of a let-down. However, the dialogue was good. I'll shame it for it's lack of a Dialogue Tree thus far. 7/10
AI: The AI was great. Enemies were either cowards or knew how to fight, and their AI reflected that. With the combat system, it sets up a difficulty of COMPLEXITY, and that's either really good or bad game design. Here, it's done great. 8/10
World Design: Semi-Dynamic, beautifully designed, randomly generated. It's luck, but damn good luck. 9/10
Graphics: The game is set up in a 32-bit art style (I believe?), and the graphics look promising. Some shots of the world are detailed, even with 32 pixels. This game would have great graphics back in the 32-bit era, and good indie graphics. 8/10
Sound: Haha. None. 0/10
Music: There is a death track, thus far. Nothing special. 4/10
The verdict for NEO Scavenger is an 8.75/10. It delivers well, and it's promising, even for late Early Access. Some small tweaks, and this could easily go over a 9.
DayZ Review Gimmick: "Slept in an office, robbed and left with my plastic bag. 8.75/10, would sleep again."

I'd never played a Hidden Object Game before, but saw this in a bundle of similar games by the same studio and thought I'd give it a try. I enjoyed it a lot more than I expected!
9 Clues: The Secret of Serpent Creek is basically a fairly simple and linear adventure game (get items, use them on things, solve puzzles, advance a story) interspersed with occasional scenes where you have to click on specific objects in a pile of random junk. It's very well paced, and not at all frustrating or tedious like many adventure games. The story is basically an episode of Scooby-Doo, but that's okay.
I only really have one problem with this game. Sometimes you have to do a hidden object puzzle more than once to get all the items you need from it. This is really unintuitive, because the puzzle isn't available to try again until after the game decides you need the second item from the puzzle.
There are other minor annoyances, like solutions to puzzles being a little eyeroll-inducing, but that's characteristic of the genre. Overall, this is a pretty decent adventure game and a great way to spend a few hours.

I'm a big fan of the show, so I was honestly pleased to find this game was pretty fun! It has a similar complex story feel to the show, and it's interesting to see the perspectives of other Houses like the Forresters. There are a few issues, but they're minor. For example, I initially set the game to fullscreen but the game wouldn't work then for some reason. I ended up having to return to windowed mode and adjust the resolution. Easy enough fix, but it's not an issue that should be in a game. Textures were also a minor issue, sometimes they'd look very pixelated or edges would be rough. It also sometimes feels like the choices you make don't have as big of an effect on the story as you'd think, more than once I did feel like my choice didn't matter and that the same thing would happen regardless. I also wish we had more time to make decisions with our response choices. Or just had unlimited time, like in similar choose-your-own-adventure games like this.
That being said, still a fun game! The voice acting is solid, with all the characters from the show still being voiced by their actual actors, which is a HUGE plus to me because VAs being changed just because it's a different medium to film is a pet peeve of mine. The combat system felt a little clunky sometimes, but it was still enjoyable. It really feels like you're in the pace of the battle.
Honestly, if you enjoy Game of Thrones on TV, you'll probably find this game entertaining to add further complexity to the story!

And that's just scratching the surface of all this game has to offer.

I love BDO for its versatility -- I'm a non-competitive player who prefers PvE, lifeskills, and co-op with IRL friends who also play. The game is absolutely gorgeous and allows for some pretty great character customization, your skillsets are customizable, and the game has a multitude of options regardless of whether you prefer PvE focus or PvP/end game focus. It's easy to play solo or with friends, or a massive guild if you're serious business. And since there's no monthly charge I feel comfortable dropping cash here and there in the pearl shop for cute clothes, pets, and horse gear.
It's challenging and definitely does not hold your hand, but it's still friendly towards players who are new to MMOs, because there are a ton of online resources (node maps, recipes) now that the game has been out long enough and thanks to all of the hard work of the players who took on the incredibly difficult challenge of figuring it all out at launch.
There's a massive amount of content here, especially if you're interested in gaining knowledge. Every character seems to have an indepth backstory, even if you just see the tip of the iceberg when you gain information on them. It's great for someone like me who likes to "collect" -- titles for grinding and finishing certain quests and catching enough of each type of fish -- and there are a ton of long term goals worth working towards, like getting a T9 Dream Horse or building that Epheria Sailboat with all of the Epheria accessories, because I'm vain and stubborn and like pretty mounts.
So yeah, whatever your playing style is you should be able to find plenty of content to spend your time on. I definitely have.

Now, this review may be slightly bias, due to the days worth of playtime under my belt from when I was a kid.
For starters, this is easily one of my top 5 Star Wars games of all time, if not the top. The PC version has slightly different menus than the PS2 version I remember, but other than that, everything else is there.
Frankly, I don't know why LucasArts thought they should make an entirely new battlefront, in my opinion, they could have easily copied BF2, touched up the graphics a lot, added some more modes, planets, heroes, more campaigns and maybe some other things nobody asked for, and it would pass as a successful game. Let's be honest, Battlefront 2 is better than Battlefront 2015, and if you use the excuse of 'Yeah but the 2015 graphics are better', my friend, PC modding has already taken care of that. HD textures.
Now, onto Multiplayer.
Not gonna lie, haven't actually played it yet. Granted, GameSpy brought down the servers early 2014, but dedicated fans out there have created mods that can still allow like-minded players to contrinue playing this great game with others, so it won't be long before I give it a shot.
Campaign? Inventive, interesting, and I feel is rather a high point of the game. Follows a specific company of clone troopers throughout the galaxy, showing everything from the first battle of Geonosis, to the excecution of order 66 and the clone's transition to the empire. Added with the fact that these missions aren't just 'Do what you normally do in regular gameplay but don't lose', they actually have really enjoyable mini-quests. Though sometimes, the missions can get a bit hard. Felucia for example. Acklays, man.
In my opinion, the game's only flaws are in its classes, and balancing. There are some issues with some specific things in the game being overpowered. For example, Bothan Spies. The disintegration gun is far too powerful in my opinion, and added with their ability to turn invisible, it can really screw you over. Second issue is with the Gamorrean guards in Jabba's Palace. Granted, they're not a playable class, but still, they get in your way, and are hostile to everyone, not to mention the fact that there is no way to make them stop spawning. You may be asking what my issue is with them. Oh I dunno, maybe the fact that they can ONE HIT KILL ANYTHING. Boba Fett for example.
As an honourable mention, I think that Space Battles are definitely one of the best parts of the game. Its just a shame that it took until Rogue Squadron on the PSP to allow for ground AND space battles in one (Correct me if I'm wrong but I believe RS was the first BF game to actually allow that). But then again, that's just me being picky.
Overall, this game is a huge hit in my books, and is easily better than some of the stuff A-List publishers roll out today. No DLCs, no extra content, no pay-to-win, just the base game, in all its glory. And what a lot of glory it has.
My Laptop is absolute bantha fodder, and it can run this game on lowest graphics with complete ease, rarely goes below 50fps, and when it does, its most likely due to the fact that I'm playing XL on Hoth, or just when there's an absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of AI on the screen at once.
Definitely give this game a go, if you can look past the graphics; which aren't even that bad considering when it was made, then this game is a real gem, and I'd encourage anyone to pick up a copy and get stuck in.
EDIT: New computer plays fine, just has issues with the whole audio jack thing. How to combat: just stick a wire into the audio jack if it crashes upon loading the map.

9/10 Amazing, Insanely fun! Worth Every Penny
Note: I haven't played any of the other saints row games, this is my first.
This is without a doubt one of the most fun, entertaining , exciting, hilarious games i have ever in my life. It takes GTA style(or saints row) gameplay, completely turns it upside down and introduces insane super powers such as running 200 miles per hour, jumping a 1000 feet, sprinting up buildings, gliding like a flying squirrel, telekenesis, throwing fireballs that can explode entire city intersections, and tons more. This type of gameplay is really a no brainer , and made me wonder why this type isn't present in more games. It's just too fun to describe. Not only is this  game fun beyond belief, but the characters, story, and dialogue  are all top notch. Saints Row IV is rich with satire , referencing numerous films and videogames, and it does so in a way that the game doesn't outright explain it's references, it insteads presents it in a way that if you've seen it/ or watched it, then you'll "get it".
I've read some people say that exploring the sandbox environment is boring. It's true that the city is kind of boring and nothing really stands out, but that is so besides the point for me. The fun was in the fact that i could run down the street going 200 miles per hour, knocking over any thing in my path, while listening to the radio(something that is lacking in GTA games, cause you need to be in a car for music), sprinting and jumping over giant buildings, then flying like a mad man. The mechanics of the game never got old for me. Sometimes i found myself just running around doing whatever just for the fun of it, No super hero game to date has been able to capture this kind of freedom.
I normally list pros and cons, but the pros of this game are so many that ill just stick with the cons and try to explain it a bit.
- Side activities outside the main/side questlines can become repetitive. BUT, they are totally optional, the game doesn't force you to do these things, and i had no problem experiencing the game/super powers/story to the fullest by only dabbing in a few side activities.
- anything to do with cars is pointless, wether its buying, upgrading, anything. BUT again, its totally optional. I've read peopel complaining about the fact that the game gives you your super powers early on. I for one have no problem with this. The cars are available if you want to do stuff with them, but why would you, when you have super powers? Again its something that is totally pointless to complain about. It goes to show you that people will complain about anything. Im sure if the devs gave you the powers later in the game then some gamers would just complain that it should have been available sooner in the game.
_ I wish more radio stations were available, I still love the fact that you could get out of your car and still listen to music though
- Finding clusters to upgrade your powers felt like grinding after awhile. This is prolly my only legit complaint. But even so it doesn't take long to get the amount you need to get the desired upgrades, and it was still kind of fun obtaining them.
I Love this game. It was a hell of an experience that i won't forget anytime soon. I could rant/rave about Saints Row IV all day long, but ill end it here. Do i Recommend this game? You bet your♥♥♥♥♥I do

Remember when you were a kid, flipping around channels late at night and landing on some weird 80s horror movie with terrible everything? Well, this is that movie, just with clicking on lots of items. Serpent Creek is a pulpy adventure to find your reporter friend in a weird little seaside town where everyone acts like a creepy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. In stark contrast with Haunted Past, this game is heavy on stingers and jumpscares but they're so goofy they become endearing. There's plenty of hilarious adventure game logic too, like needing an axe to chop up a little branch you could step over, using a knife to open a can of soda so you don't ruin your nails (pictured), and the classic "use gun on man" puzzle solution more than once. I really can't overstate the charm on display here, and the puzzles and item searches are mostly easy enough to keep the game rolling. The only times I got stuck were specifically because I chose the hardest difficulty where it does not highlight hidden object scenes for you, which is a problem because for some reason this game makes you do every scene twice at different points in the story. A strange annoyance, but not enough to hurt my opinion of the game.
There are investigation scenes as well where you click on 9 pieces of evidence and then listen to your character narrate an absolutely ridiculous series of events. There's voice-acting set to the Flash-level animation and it is just as goofy and terrible as it needs to be. The puzzles are pretty standard adventure game fare, minus really obnoxious ones like sliding blocks. The map is helpful, and the graphics are crisp enough to make out everything you need. I enjoyed this one quite a bit, and it even clocked in over the usual 2-hour mark.

in the name of the game.
The rest of the plot basically plays out on automatic as well. The people that look shifty turn out to be the villains, the ones that look friendly or attractive are helping you in the end.
It flaunts its new "Detective Mode" which is little more than a mini-game a few times throughout the story that has you piece together what happened in a location. It's neat enough, but far from ground breaking.
So what's left? A decent hidden object game. Nothing spectacular, nothing out of the ordinary, but well executed with high production values like those you've come to expect from Artifex Mundi.
If you've exhausted their other games I would recommend it, but it's not their best game by a long shot.

One of the best couch co-op games I've ever played.
Overcooked is an example of a simple idea, brilliantly executed. It takes the familiar concept of a time management game, turns it into a challenging co-op experience, and adds tons of creative twists on the formula.
Each level feels like a frantic impossible task at first, then comes together in a satisfying way once you and your friends figure out the best strategy. Better yet, none of the "gimmicks" in the levels outstay their welcome, and each of the games several dozen levels introduces something new to deal with.
The game isn't without a few hiccups, though. The controls can be a little finicky at times, resulting in (thankfully rare) moments of frustration when you burn something because you can't drop the thing in your hands, or can't get something to land on the right section of a counter. I also had a few issuses specifically on the first and last level of the game with FPS drops (game ran otherwise fine on my semi-old gaming laptop) and audio normalization (I know that meatball's supposed to be loud, but geeze!)
But, all in all, Overcooked is amazing. I'm hoping I can leave it on the shelf long enough to forget how to play all the levels, so I can play it again with other friends and enjoy honing my onion choping skills all over again!

Check out myself and TB playing through this game on our YouTube channel. Last Boss Gaming:
Overcooked is a game intended for local co-op. If you don't have a buddy or three to sit down with and play through a game, I'd pass by Overcooked. If you do, though, this game is one of the best you can get. Each level places you in a kitchen with its own bizarre layout and rules. They are easy to understand but tough to master. You and your buddies will have to figure out the best way to cook up the requested meals, serve them, and wash the dishes to get the highest score possible on each level.
The gameplay gets chaotic very quickly but levels are bite-sized, usually only lasting 3 minutes, so it never feels TOO stressful. While you are unlikely to ever fail levels completely (you have to basically never complete anything to fail), the game uses a three star system to encourage repeat playthroughs. To unlock new levels, you have to have enough stars on the previous levels. If your goal is just to blaze through the game as fast as possible, this may get annoying at times, particularly near the end when you need quite a few stars to progress, but mastering levels never took too long for us and was always a blast.
The whole thing is wrapped up in an amazingly crazy story about an onion king training you to save the world from a giant meatball monster who wants to eat everything, and that's just the first few minutes of the game! Overall, if you have some friends who you can get together to play this, I highly recommend it. If not or if short, stressful bursts of gameplay aren't your thing, maybe join TB and I in our channel for our playthrough!

Black Desert Online is an Online Sandbox MMORPG created by Pearl Abyss and Kakao Games. The vast open world is yours to explore at your own leisure.
Black Desert Online is a visually beautiful game. Everything in the game is very detailed and nice on the eyes, and the character creation menu is very extensive. The world is large but isn't filled with huge open voids, but instead is populated by a vast amounts of forests, towns, caves and more for you to explore. The only downside to the graphics in Black Desert Online is the cluttered UI. If it weren't for my friends who have much more experience playing the game, I wouldn't have figured out how to clean up the UI. Seriously, it's horrendous. You get spammed every few seconds with notifications that have no meaning to new players and the amount of windows you can have open is nauseating.
The audio department of Black Desert Online was, for the most part, pretty well done. The music in Black Desert Online is orchestral and is very well done. The main menu music always gets me pumped up for my next grind session (more on that later). The soundtrack is very relaxing and fits very well with the gameplay style of Black Desert Online (more on that later as well). The sound effects are decently well done, but there are always downsides. The ambient sound effects are pretty well done and help set the mood in the various areas you come across, but the noises your characters make are so damn weird.  Your characters often scream/moan/??? whenever you perform a new action and it's hard to describe the emotions I go through whenever I hear them. Seriously dude, you're riding a horse. You don't gotta scream. Get a grip.
Black Desert Online isn't for everyone. Do you enjoy RuneScape/Old School RuneScape and other such grind-fest related games? Then perhaps BDO is for you. Do you absolutely hate grind-fest games? I'd probably stay away. I for one quite enjoy playing Old School RuneScape, and grinding isn't too off-putting for me. I enjoy putting in the effort and watching my stats climb, and that's exactly what you do in BDO. Want to become an expert at fishing? Be my guest. Want to craft stuff? Go right ahead. Want to go kill stuff? Hop on my wagon, lets go. Everything in BDO revolves around the constant grind. The combat in BDO is quite fluent as well, and there are dozens of different skills that are unique to whichever class you're playing, although memorizing each skill can be pretty difficult (to be honest I just mainly use one skill). Plus, Pearl Abyss is constantly updating the game, with another class (Mystic) set to release soon (as of release of this review). Don't like actively crafting or fishing or riding your horse to level it? You can minimize the game into your tray and leave it on for a few hours while you automatically fish or craft or whatever it was you were doing, which is a pretty neat thing to do if you don't mind leaving the game open and artificially inflating your hours.
The community is also an important part of Black Desert Online. One great (or awful feature, depending on how you look at it) is the lack of direct peer-to-peer trading. Everything goes through the in game market, and therefore Real World Trading and other illegitimate transactions are not possible (except for account sharing). You can play with friends by queuing up in a party and levelling together, or you can create your own guild, enter wars with enemy factions, and even control parts of the world (which is a pretty damn cool feature if you ask me!). If you take a stroll through any major city in the game, you will find tons of fellow players just chillin' in town hotspots, having a grand old time. It's a refreshing thing to see and can motivate you to grind more or encourage you to socialize and make new friends.
Micro transactions. DUN DUN DUN! it's hard to talk about an MMORPG and not talk about the micro transactions. In fact, its kind of necessary. Oh boy, here we go.
The micro transactions in BDO aren't as bad as some other games (ahem, pride of sense and accomplishment, anyone?) but that isn't to say that there are none. One thing that gives you a direct advantage over other players are pets that help you pick items up at an extremely fast rate. More items = more silver. More silver = better items. Did I mention you can have 4 pets at the same time? Wait, there's more! You can buy items off the Pearl Shop (the game's version of a cash shop). Thats not surprising, right? You can then sell the items for in game cash. Uh, what? Yeah, you can directly influence your in game wealth with a credit card. However, Pearl Abyss does frequently host events and gives out free character slots whenever there is a new class being released, so spending money on the game after the initial $10 investment is not necessary.
To be completely honest, the story didn't catch my attention at all. Character dialogue is long and boring, and I quickly skimmed through it. The parts that I did make out though were stale, and most of the community seems to agree. The Black Spirit is still my homie though, that won't change. Questing isn't a big part of the story however, and you can go on just fine without knowing the back story to the game. If BDO was singleplayer, then perhaps the story would matter a lot more.
Black Desert Online is not for everyone. Chances are a lot of the people who have tried the game didn't enjoy it, and that's fine. Grinding your way to victory isn't for everyone, and although I do enjoy the game quite a bit, I don't think I could ever put in the time to be in even the top 10% of the community, and that's fine as well. BDO is a sandbox game. You play it at your own leisure, and that's how it is meant to be played.

Really well put together city builder, with a political twist. I've sunk a ton of hours into playing just the first campaign of this.
Loads of ways to play it too. You can try to create a utopia or you can just be as harsh as you like. On top of that, you can choose to properly fund your island using industry and tourism (and you can really mix that up however you like) or you can just devalue your currency and ignore the rest of the world. Your avater/leader also has a choice of three traits which act as modifiers (you increase the effectiveness of any given modifier by using it multiple times), which again, really changes up the way you choose to create your island.
My only real gripe with this is that the game can be a bit samey. While the story is funny and kept me interested, the maps and scenarios which back it up are lacking. The campaign especially suffers from this. In sandbox, you can randomly generate an island, but that isn't possible in campaign. You get given one of a fairly small number of islands for each scenario, which means you have to play on most of them multiple times.
Admittedly, the tasks you have to carry out to beat the level vary, but it does feel a little bit strange to have this continuous narrative in the campaign and then the island you previously created a huge city on is empty again.
That sort of niggle aside though, a really enjoyable game to take it easy with and enjoy some silly political satire.

One of the better ARPGs on the market and improved with the expansion (raised level cap, more content, two new classes (necromancer and inquisitor), new devotion specs, and many new items etc). If you are a fan of Titan Quest, the Diablo series or Path of Exile, you should look at buying this game.
What might catch players of Diablo 3 unawares is that once you choose your classes in Grim Dawn (yes, two classes make up each character you create), they cannot be respecialised to a different class. You CAN however respec to a different build in a given class, however it will cost you bits (coin). For example, if you're playing a Necromancer/Occultist (combined they become a Cabalist) and instead you would prefer to play something that uses a sword/board combination (say the Soldier class), then you would have to create a new character and start the game from the beginning. A lot of classes really don't become fun (and powerful) until later in leveling as well so I think this is the only drawback to the game for a new player.
The game runs well on even older PCs (I'd recommend forcing DX9 mode however), and you will not experience any lag or disconnects as the game is completely offline.
I've put 200+ hours into Grim Dawn at the time of writing this review and I would recommend it to anyone looking to sink a lot of time into an ARPG that differs from the Diablo-series (let's not talk about the abomination that is Diablo 3) or Path of Exile (great ARPG, made by an outstanding developer, however suffers from lag, and online-only is a bit of a turn off in certain situations.

Dying Light is a hugely underrated game. If you ask me, it's the best open world FPS since STALKER. The game mechanics are solidn, the game feel is pretty fantastic. IMO they do have the best moves in any FPS. The balance can be frustrating, but in its way it's pretty polished. It do some interesting with key point in the game where gameplay drastically evolves (grappling hook, camouflage) yet remain surprisingly balanced. Actually those changes are appropriate and are very efficiently preventing some fatigue. Not all though - there are definitely too much lock to pick in that game.
It can be pretty, it's often pretty scary, it's always heavy on the mood like any self respecting zombie game should be. Actually AFAICT, it's just the best zombie game out there. It conveys that feel of despair that's the trademark of the genre far better than any other games with the possible exception of Dead Islan whose first Chapter, played alone and without all the "damage" displays, could be super oppressive as well (same team, no surprise). Also the infected are really, really ugly, and you kill them in one thousdand very, very bloody ways. It's one of the very few game I'd be really careful not to show in front of my 8 yo son. I know he could easily nightmare on this.
If you play alone, it's not easy on the mood, you have to like it.

A great successor to the Dead Island series of games, by Techland, Dying Light is a wonderful forray into open-world zombie killing/survival.  The game's singleplayer/co-op campaign deals with the events unfolding in Haram, where a zombie infection spreads like wildfire.  While the premise isn't particularly unique and the plot twists don't really make up for a lack of good characterization or meaty decision-making, the campaign when combined with other multiplayer modes adds good value to this title.  Melee feels good and the weapons are also effectively rendered.  Parkour adds a new dimension when traversing the city and the variety of traps/modifications and upgrades that you can pursue are significant and add color/flavor to the game's world.  While it is true that the game can feel a bit rote at times and the constantly breaking weapons take some of the fun out of crafting high level implements/tools of mayhem, Dying Light is still a worthy title to pick up on a steam sale.

Not knowing what to expect, i was rather surprised by this game. The graphics are decent, the music and sound is good and the voice acting is very well done. It felt like playing an adventure game the first 10 minutes, because it has these elements of putting things in your inventory and using/combining them with other objects to make progress in the game and advance the story. However, soon enough you run into these 'hidden object' games, which i don't see the point of. You're presented with a list of objects and you have to find them, when you complete this task, you get a new object in your inventory you need to get further along the game. There are also puzzles to be found, you know the kind, activate all lights by turning the dails, arrange this or that without crossing other bits, ... After playing it for an hour or so, it started to feel more like a very light version of Nintendo's Professor Layton series (i say 'light' because it's not as good).
The story is very very predictable and so are the actions you have to take to advance. They are not hard as in real adventure games, which could have you scratch your head for days (back in time, when there was no internet yet and you couldn't look up the solution).
What is left is a very well made and executed game that is rather simple and so falls more in the casual gaming field (at least that is how feel about it). I was not bored by it, though it was easy to complete and was short, buy it only if on sale.

So I'm going to start by saying that this is the only review I've ever written on steam, and will continue to be the only review I write on steam. Forever.  I hate writing reviews or anything really so you know this is something special.
I've been aimlessly watching tutorials and fooling around with different modifiers and simulations for over a year now. I've easily logged hundreds of hours in Blender and I'll tell you something. It's worth all of the frustration over unsaved work and all of the crashing. (well, if this kind of junk interests you)
So here's some of my advice:
-There are plenty of tutorials and guides to look at online. (Andrew Price will save you)
-PAUSE THE FRIGGIN VIDEOS, THEY ARENT ALL MEANT TO BE FOLLOWED IN REAL TIME.
-If you really want to get into this kind of software, a few hours of videos and a weekend is not going to do it.
- I don't recommend trying to learn everything. Start with modeling before you get into texuring and so on.
-Key binds are nice but don't stress about memorizing all of them, you'll remember the ones that you actually use as you learn to use Blender
-Photorealism is very difficult to achieve so if your renders don't look very photorealistic after the first year, don't worry. It will get there, I promise.
-abandoning projects is OK, if you're teaching yourself it's not like you have to show anybody that you're making progress. As long as you are making progress, usually you are :)
-Final renders are for overnight please. As obvious as this may seem to some, it is a necessary comment.
-Get inspired. You probably already are inspired if you made it this far, but look up demo reels and other peoples' work. Other than showing you what blender can do, it can give you ideas.
-Spend more than a two hour sitting working with blender. Believe it or not, but spending ten minutes in blender a day after watching a speedy five-minute walkthrough won't help you get better.
-Don't get caught up in complex scenes when starting, a glass cube on a checkered surface is pretty much all that you'll be able to do on day 1.
-Switch to cycles engine, it's what everyone does. (Andrew Price explains why cycles is amazing in quite a few of his videos)
-Don't waste your money on tutorial packs until you're already into using Blender at least a little bit.
Not all of these are musts, and some of them might be a little misleading, but hey it's worth a shot. I guess you should take my words as seriously as other users find it useful.

Braid is a traditional 2D side scrolling platform game that feels very familiar. You enter different levels, hop on most enemies to defeat them, find keys, open doors and climb ladders. It feels very familiar. There is a jump button, up lets you go in doors or climb ladders, and a button for the big twist.
The big twist is time manipulation, you can reverse time or fast forward it once you have rewound it. This way, when you die, you rewind time to when you didn't die. You rewind time to help you solve puzzles too.
Such as, you will get a key, open a door and find another door, well you can rewind time to where you still had the key. When time is restarted, you will have the key, but the first door will be open. A lot of puzzles are like that in the game, whether its dropping 5 ceiling fixtures onto a boss's head when you need to rewind time to reset the fixtures or grabbing a key in a pit and rewinding time to when you didn't fall in the pit (but still keep the key).
The game feels mellow and has a unique art style that makes it feel like a story book. There are things before the levels that you can walk by and read the rich back story to the game.
While it is amazingly good, challenging and thought provoking. It feels like other free games found on the Internet. This game is just the best of them all, its a nice change of pace from everything that is 3D in the world.
To be honest this game is more challenging than fun. It is a side scrolling platform puzzle game. Like Mario.... but with a tragic story. Like an unhappy Mario game based on puzzles that require you to rewind time, speed it up, slow it down. All that fun stuff. The only catch is that the difficulty curve goes up a giant hill. It is not fun and it gets challenging too quickly all while keeping a sad tone and a painted art style. Skip this game and forget how many people love it because its one of the first indie games to get praise. Go pick up something fun instead.

Note: I haven't played any of the other saints row games, this is my first.
This is without a doubt one of the most fun, entertaining , exciting, hilarious games i have ever in my life. It takes GTA style(or saints row) gameplay, completely turns it upside down and introduces insane super powers such as running 200 miles per hour, jumping a 1000 feet, sprinting up buildings, gliding like a flying squirrel, telekenesis, throwing fireballs that can explode entire city intersections, and tons more. This type of gameplay is really a no brainer , and made me wonder why this type isn't present in more games. It's just too fun to describe. Not only is this  game fun beyond belief, but the characters, story, and dialogue  are all top notch. Saints Row IV is rich with satire , referencing numerous films and videogames, and it does so in a way that the game doesn't outright explain it's references, it insteads presents it in a way that if you've seen it/ or watched it, then you'll "get it".
I've read some people say that exploring the sandbox environment is boring. It's true that the city is kind of boring and nothing really stands out, but that is so besides the point for me. The fun was in the fact that i could run down the street going 200 miles per hour, knocking over any thing in my path, while listening to the radio(something that is lacking in GTA games, cause you need to be in a car for music), sprinting and jumping over giant buildings, then flying like a mad man. The mechanics of the game never got old for me. Sometimes i found myself just running around doing whatever just for the fun of it, No super hero game to date has been able to capture this kind of freedom.
I normally list pros and cons, but the pros of this game are so many that ill just stick with the cons and try to explain it a bit.
- Side activities outside the main/side questlines can become repetitive. BUT, they are totally optional, the game doesn't force you to do these things, and i had no problem experiencing the game/super powers/story to the fullest by only dabbing in a few side activities.
- anything to do with cars is pointless, wether its buying, upgrading, anything. BUT again, its totally optional. I've read peopel complaining about the fact that the game gives you your super powers early on. I for one have no problem with this. The cars are available if you want to do stuff with them, but why would you, when you have super powers? Again its something that is totally pointless to complain about. It goes to show you that people will complain about anything. Im sure if the devs gave you the powers later in the game then some gamers would just complain that it should have been available sooner in the game.
_ I wish more radio stations were available, I still love the fact that you could get out of your car and still listen to music though
- Finding clusters to upgrade your powers felt like grinding after awhile. This is prolly my only legit complaint. But even so it doesn't take long to get the amount you need to get the desired upgrades, and it was still kind of fun obtaining them.
I Love this game. It was a hell of an experience that i won't forget anytime soon. I could rant/rave about Saints Row IV all day long, but ill end it here. Do i Recommend this game? You bet your♥♥♥♥♥I do

There aren't many negative things to say about Blender. It is, I think, the best and easiest to use... and it is free. The interface, after a few tutorials, is very easy to understand. I have only been using this software for about 2 months now and have already seen exponential progress in my creations... Granted, I am doing all of them with guided tutorials, but that's how I think someone of my level of skill (none when I started) should start.
I am starting to experiment and make my own stuff. When I started out with the default cube scene, I added an armature to it. I realize now how funny it was that I did that, but back then, it was the first button I saw and I had no idea what anything did. Now I'm making alien spaceships, audio vizualizers, and caves. All of this art for FREE.
Sure, Blender may not be the perfect software, but it is completly customizable. You can change the color or the size of things, you can evenmake video games with it if you want. (That's my eventual plan). Blender is amazing, but it's community is also amazing. I've never met any other community so willing to help and eager to share their creations and how they made it. There are thousands of tutorials out there for things I never thought was possible with a free software.  Now I have the ability to make my own amazing art to share with others.
By now... I'm sure you're wondering why the bad review. After all this praise, how could there be anything negative? I recently learned (the hard way) that Blender takes up a LOT of RAM. Steam (conveniently) also takes up a lot of RAM. If you have Steam AND Blender open at the same time Blender will crash and you will lose any work that you do not save, and believe me... You will forget to save. You will get sucked in and apply the subdivision surface modifier before you save and scream when you lose your work.  It also helps to have something to play while rendering and, unfortunetly, Steam only allows you to play one thing at a time.
So, to conclude this ramble, I recommend you download this software. If for no other reason, it is fun to play with when you are bored. It is amazing to look at the things other people come up with and create from a single cube. It is extremely satisfying when you make your first artwork. I do recommend people continue to post their artwork on steam. It is good inspiration for those of us who need it. I absolutely recommend this software, I just think people should download it from
instead of Steam.
Also, for those who are just starting out, I recommend you find Tutor4u and/or browse the tutorials they have on
. BlenderGuru is also really great, but his stuff is very difficult to understand as a beginner.

Each iteration of Tropico keeps getting better and this is no exception. Some highlights:
* HUGE improvements in traits. Instead of having to pick both "positive" and "negative" traits, you can now pick whichever ones you want. Previously "negative" traits involve trade-offs with potential for big overall payoffs. Leveling traits to enhance their effects makes a big difference too. This helps a lot in scenarios where you need to accomplish specific goals.
* Better supply chains for industry. The concrete plant in particular is a nice, cheap way to get industry started without pre-requisite buildings to supply it.
* Importing resources allows you to have industry without any mining, logging, or farming. It also makes a large population without tons of farming simpler.
* Richer, more complex foreign affairs that have a much larger effect on your export prices on various goods.
* The in-game missions provide a lot more opportunities for bonus effects.
That said, I feel like the game has lost a little of its tongue-in-cheek charm towards banana republic regimes. I still crack up at the over-enthusiastic way that the original in-game voice would say "right away, Presidente" about every command or edict you issues, be it doubling food consumption or executing someone's entire family. This iteration feels like it's trying a little too hard to be obviously sarcastic and relies a little too heavily on awful, generic stereotypes.

Before I bought this game I had one overpowering thought: Dead Island was the most boring and unsatisfying zombie game I have EVER played.  Co-op was bland and rarely worked. Weapons that broke after 2 hits.  The same boring few enemies, including those big guys you couldn't hit.  Everywhere looked the same, getting lost was guaranteed and intensely frustrating. Dead Island is possibly the worst Co-op game I have played.
Why am I talking about Dead Island? On first appearances, Dying Light looks like another Dead Island. I sat on the fence for a while before buying this game.  I'm glad I did try it.  It's nothing like Dead Island.
The weapons are varied and fun, the ability to climb and move around the scenery pretty much everywhere is well thought out and implemented.  Co-op works straight away with no fuss and has some good features.  Set a waypoint on the map and you can race the other players in your session there.  You don't have to, but the winner get a bit of extra XP (and bragging rights).  It's a nice feature that makes things that bit more entertaining.
Your weapons don't instantly break either. Enemies are interesting and varied. You rarely feel safe. See what I mean by "It's nothing like Dead Island"?
The skill trees are full of both useful and entertaining options. I felt myself looking forward to each new skill, there was always something to aim for.  (insert nothing like dead island again) The variety of night and day cycles was a great choice by the developers. Night time is not nice, but the rewards are sometimes worth the risks.

I'm recommending "9 Clues: The Secret of Serpent Creek," but not at the current list price.  It's a decent Artifex Mundi casual adventure Hidden Object Game (HOG) that's got acceptable graphics and voice acting for its genre.  But, the story is very simplistic and the HOGs, themselves, very simple to do.  The worst thing I can come up with to complain about is that the Detective Mode scenes are just silly.  They're sort of a reverse HOG:  you find things that look odd in a scene and it fills in the name down below.  The silly part is that the main character then uses those objects to come up with what happened in the scene.  And, she's just pulling that stuff out of her posterior dorsal when she does.  The sole reason I don't recommend the game at its current list price is its length:  it took me 3.3 hours to finish the whole thing with 100% Achievements.  If you can find the game on sale for about $3, go for it.  Otherwise, it's just not worth it.

A masterclass in strategy and punishing difficulty rehashed, gutted, and dumbed down into a mobile game. This is a sci-fi version of "Breach And Clear".
Stripped back to a single XCom HQ, with no risk of alien retaliation, and limited UFO detections each month, you speed up time waiting for alien activity any where on the planet (which consists of only 8 nations) which is enevitbaly an urban 'abduction' battle or, much less frequently, UFO crash sites.
Highly repetative gameplay sees your soldiers move from cover to cover, jarringly interupted by cut scenes each and every time you lift the 'fog of war' and spot an alien. These cut scenes also provide the alien side with free movement, preventing your soldiers from catching the enemy at a disadvantage.
Action Points are stripped down to two for every sodlier: They may either move one radius (blue squares), with the option of firing or using equipment, or "dash" two radii (orange squares) with no chance to fire. As far as I can tell the movement radii are identical for all soldiers, regardless of rank or ability. Accuracy (or % to hit) is fixed regardless of movement, with stance and aimed shots excluded from this game.

Relic Entertainment works with Games Workshop to produce an epic real time strategy game that pushed the boundaries of the genre. Dawn of War offers economics, base building, military tactics, and unit management.
Dawn of War, the first installment on an incredible Warhammer 40,000 saga. The game is based on the planet Tarturus where Ork forces are out of control ravaging the planet and destroying Imperial Guard moral; but, how are they winning so easily? Of course the forces of Chaos are behind the whole war. Dawn of War is the story of Gabrial Angelos and Isador Akios and how they work together to figure out the whole reason behind the presence of Chaos on the imperial garrison at Tarturus.
The campaign offers an epic tale into the 40k lore with amazing twists and turns around every mission. Coupled with the amazing combat system, base management, and resource management this game really packs a punch. The campaign is divided into eleven missions which put you to the test fighting against the Orc Horde and the Chaos Might. As you progress through the campaign you work with the Eldar to defeat a common foe, but as the game dictates the Enemy of your Enemy is not always your friend. The game pits teams together, but at the same time continually draws them apart.
This game was one of the first to successfully introduce rapid base expansion by requiring players to capture strategic points, which give the player a trickle of endless resources over time. The fast paced gameplay coupled with the macro and micro unit management really made this game a force to be reckoned with. Although the unit population seems rather low (20 personal – 10 vehicle) because the units are based in squads the real unit count is much higher. The battles seem more like full scale wars with you gripping to manage all your units at once. The best feature of this game (and all the Dawn of War games) is that each team is completely different. They have different units, different buildings, upgrades, tactics, resource types, hero units, and strategies. For example the Orc play completely different from the Eldar while both the Eldar and Orcs play completely different from the Space Marines and Chaos Marines. The only two similar teams are the Space Marines and Chaos marines which offer a good learners curve to Dawn of War by giving providing a basic approach to strategy: build barracks, build turrets for defense, use main base to upgrade to new “age” to receive better buildings, build power plants to get power, and upgrade units within armory, etc.
There are four teams: Space Marines, Eldar, Orcs, and Chaos Marines. Each team poses different tactics/strategic elements which make you play them differently. The Orcs are based more around unit massing and rapid base expansion. While the Eldar are more about unit specialization and micro base management. The Space Marines and Chaos Marines are essentially the same team set, and fit between tactics of the Orcs and Eldar. Each of the teams units have upgradeable attributes which customize them for specific purposes: weapons, additional squad members, and squad leader units. Each team has special commander units which can be used as heroes buffing the team and supporting military units.
All and all Dawn of War is a must get game. If you can play older games without constantly yearning for the graphics of the modern day games then you’ll enjoy this game. The gameplay is not outdated, but rather refreshing. As it seems most strategy game developers have diverted from base building, resource management, and mass scale war to simple micromanagement tactic games. I loved this game and all the installments so much I repurchased them all on steam. Despite that I still have all the discs, in functional condition, right next to me.
Pros:
+Economic, Base building, and macro unit management
+Fantastic story and campaign (which is very rare in a strategy game)
+Amazing teams which each play completely differently.
+Fast paced gameplay which requires expansion to acquire resource nodes (but those nodes do not run out like in most games)
+Unit customization allows you to create squads for specific tasks
+Fantastic computer AI that puts you to your wits
Cons:
-Cannot play this game while having another monitor running (if you have two monitors the game will launch but every time you move the mouse to the edge of the screen where your monitor extends the mouse exits the game as if you are playing in Windowed mode).
-Lots of unbalances (don’t worry they fix all of these in the later installments)

One of if not the best indie game I've played, 9/10. Think rogue-like game where you control the crew of a spaceship. You can move them around, repairing or boosting systems. You also control power distribution, and can boost shields, weapons, or hyperdrive (if you need to flee quicker). You can also buy various upgrades for both your crew, your ship and the weapons. All these things allow for a suprising amount of customisability despite each playthrough being quite short.
Pros -
Indie game means low price, which it's more than worth
Interesting mechanic of controlling the crew rather than the ship directly - if you get boarded either send you crew to fight or vent that room to space
Lot of customisability
Short(ish) playthroughs mean its handy as a pick-up-and-play
Cons - There isn't THAT many random events, enough to have 3/4 unique playthroughs but after than the odd one will be familiar - still has more replayability than a lot of games
Endgame is ridiculous, expect to have to play through half a dozen times just to reach the final boss, just to get annihilated by them.

On a more serious note, I may have clocked in more than 50+ hours in Blender before it came to steam. Braid is a time-twisting platformer. But, it's more of a puzzle solver. You play a lil dude who has the ability to stop, speed up, slow down and rewind time to bend the world to it's will.
I've heard from a lot of people that they find Braid pretencious. For those people, I'd ask them to complete the game. It is quite complicated at times, but gives you some really quite remarkable closure at the end.
One of the criticisms I have for the game is that the story doesn't "fit" together until you have fully completed the game. The fault here, though, is that people get so annoyed at the lack of a coherent storyline, confused as to what's going on, that they give up before it's over, and never appreciate the full story. Which is a real shame.
If you like puzzle platformers, check this one out. Give it time and complete the game. If you buy it and give up before it's finished, you'll be disappointed. If, however, you finish the game, I think you'll be impressed. I was.

That's not me saying it's all bad, unfortunately the good things only ever impress you the first few hours of the game and then you start seeing all of the flaws and oh boy, are there a lot of those.

Nothing feels quite as acomplishing than learning how to create dishes and learn how to plan your strategy without even realising you are getting getter.

Empathising on what I said earlier, the gameplay and sound rather go together, as you're copping tomatoes and sizziling burgers it feels natural and pleasing to the ears. The music is also awesome as when time is running out it speeds up, creating a sense of urgency and a heads up to get♥♥♥♥♥♥done.
MULTIPLAYER - 10/10 WHERE'S THE LAMB SAUCE?!
I played this whole game with one other person and we had a blast, she really enjoyed being able to play as a team in a light-hearted game environment, we laughed a whole damn lot and high fived everytime we pursused that 3 star rating on each stage. If you don't have anyone to play with go make a friend and force them to play this game and then instantly lose friendship over hot soup. The core of the game basically says work together or die together, it's where the fun lies, communicating with team mates and helping each other with information.
VERDICT - 10/10 BUY THIS GAME

Xcom is widely known to be an exceptional game.
I would agree absolutely with that general concensus that this is a really decent tactical strategy game.  I can almost see what this is based on and where it has come from.  This version too exhibits some really nice additions which allows me to say with absolute confidence that technology made this game better.  In saying that there are issues with this game's quality and its design, and irronically Firaxis are getting no better at making games that are flawless... and that is worth saying as these are integral parts of the game I can  see that don't work/don't give enough feedback/ or just are buggy as hell, and it doesn't feel like it will get fixed at all.
The beauty of Xcom Enemy Unknown is that is has so many sides to it.  It is in everyway, like Divinity : Dragon Commander, where you manage your ship, build stuff, get reserach, monitor stuff, build more stuff  in between tactical battle mode.  This design is brilliant can offer so much depth I think, and Dragon Commander went a step further in many cases.  I will add that Xcom's implementation of that is no different and allows you to do all sorts, though from what I can see, if you dont get this stuff by a certain time in the game, the game seems to suffocate your operation... not sure about that exactly,  but it felt like I 'nearly' did and it cost me at some point throughout the game.  Whats more, as Dragon Commander's Political exploits are generally not required in your 10th game, alot of the stuff on here is not time draining and does NOT keep you from getting into what XCom is all about.  Combat.
Combat is decent and has reasonable depth and certainly does not get overloaded with stuff.  Its seamless, nice to do and leaves you little to worry about in your decisions.  improvements of weapons are worth it, improvement of the skills of each soldier is worth it , and when you get to a stage in the game where some of you soldiers get 'extra skillls'?  It's definately worth it.  However when its late game and your waiting to 'get paid', battle mode does feel like a chore sometimes, it restricts progress.
Each of the classes to some extent feel like they are worth using, though the best ones at the start feel weak at the end, and the weak classes at the start feel OP at the end.
What adds to this is the camera system, when an order is made, the camera follows your soldier, or some cinematic view is taken.  This is not something I would comment as being essential, but as it doesn't break anything and it looks good, gives  the game a nicer feel, it defeintely is good overall and gives the game a nice sheen.
Now what I don't like about Xcom: Firaxis, have had a few gmes I have played with certain bugs and broken functionality, Xcom is no different.  As amazing as Xcom looks, and runs, Firaxis clearly didn't get the engine right.. There is a serious issue with the selection of parts of the map that you are not looking at ... for example, I can be looking at the interior of a ship and then click inside to move, and the system will think I the roof tile (above)or lower floor(below), potentially screwing up tactics(yes which is the difference between something going horribly wrong!)and the game (Diablo Hardcore characters and poor connection come to mind, and yes you can play hardcore on this - no saves!). I guess there is a cure, if you are pretentous enough to challenge that assertion, as you will need to look carefully where the point is and where the path fidning trail is.  This generally means, you have to zoom out, rotate the view blah blah... all in all its a bit of BS.. waste of time and does takes from the game. This should not happen if you are not zoomed to another 'layer' in my oppinion, and I think that is just logical.  I think if Firaxis thought about this issue, then they could have included an undo move button function, but they didn't... There are other issues with seeing the range of your units and what they can attack as it is not clear at all what you can attack and what you can until you move that unit...
Also as far as i can see, you cannot pick your squad, i.e. if I want to train up a bunch of noob soldiers instead of using vets , then I can't, it's simple... Well, I could of course make sure (the vets) all take mortal wounds last match so they are off in the infirmary nursing wounds, but nothing more from looks of it.  Then in addition to that, when they are removed from the squad without wounds, the equipment stays on the soldier... Sometimes those soldiers dont show up in the team for the next mission, so you have 1 soldier with no gear (perhaps returning from the infirmary)and another one in the barracks that you have to track down and strip of their gear, and you CAN'T switch them... makes for boring cheese and bad design if you ask me... and yes, some equiptment mid game is damn expensive, so it is important that this works!
Science is a let down, like supcom2, once you researched everything, you have wasted money on labs and scientists are in-effect worthless, it is very dis-empowering, and as much as your squad is powerful enough and the rest is justifiably left up to you to be a good strategist, it still makes for something of an empty concept... Civ and Alpha Centurai had post science qualifications.. I think they could have added those in to make an intersting endgame of sorts, making science a worth while endeavour.
The story was alright I guess and the game flows much like Unreal 3, so its not complicated, but its good, and the art design definately complements that with the idea of who the alien race really is and where your going.
There are some bad parts to this game , and as many people will rave blindly with the 'horde', I feel its nesscessary to point out Xcom is NOT perfect.  However, as a game, I spent 50+ hours  on this and I could play it again.  It was generally fun to play, so I would say most of the hype is infact justified.
I will add, that I would definately consider gettin Xcom 2 at near full price as I liked this one so much.

I'm not the sort to prejudice games over things like their being hidden object puzzlers; and the Artifex Mundi games are by far the best examples of the genre. Nonetheless A.M. has followed the method of if it isn't broke don't fix it, meaning they reuse their puzzles with cosmetic variations from one game to another. This has the unfortunate result that if you've played one of their games you've played them all.
That's O.K. if you think of the games as more visual novels with bonus puzzle content. Granted the writing isn't amazing; but it isn't bad either. I know I've yet to play an A.M. game I could make myself stop playing before the end. That's, on average, over 3 hours in one sitting. And, most of their games include a bonus chapter that extends gameplay another hour.
They do manage to do this without unnecessarily padding game length that overstays its welcome. I know that doesn't sound like much in an industry with triple AAA titles that boast hundred of hours of gameplay. But, for cheap casual games this is an achievement.
My recommendation, because of the "if you've played one you've played them all" problem, is pare your selections down to their better games. That would be Enigmatis 2 (but not the mediocre Enigmatis: the Ghosts of Maple Creek) as a top pick, Grim Legends 1 & 2 if you liked that, and the Nightmares from the Deep trilogy if you just can't get enough of these games.

This might upset some who are saying "Quake is dead."  Good.  Go and play something else, there are plenty of games to choose from.  But why would you give this brilliant game a thumbs down, you TRAITORS?  Just to express your disapproval of the changes that make it easier for new players to pick up?  You really don't deserve this game so I'm glad you've left.
And now for the positives.  ;-)
The entire series of Quake is awesome.  And so was Doom before it.  In fact once upon a time, the ONLY networked FPS shooter available was Doom.  It was id Software that kicked off the whole FPS scene, and every iteration of Quake that's been released has been excellent.  Not always better than the last, but always excellent.
Including this version.  So why give it a thumbs down?  Spite, that's why.  Bad show fellers.
Since Quake Live, we've seen constant tweaks and changes to make it as much fun as possible to as many people as possible.  Yes I understand some people might feel miffed if they've put lots of hours in as many of us have, to become good with a certain style of play and game mechanics, but nothing can stay the same if it's to pull in more players and keep the game alive.  As some have said, the game can be unforgiving to newbies.
And talking of game mechanics, if you upgrade a for a few quid a month to Pro, you can run your own servers on the QL network and edit all the settings to suit yourself, including turning off loadouts.  I hardly ever play on ranked servers and instead choose to play CTF with tweaked air control and other mechanics that are reminiscent of OSP.  Faster and more fun, and there are tons of gamers willing to play.  And no loadouts.
To me, logically, that sort of says the people who are complaining about QL game mechanics are those who aren't even real supporters of the game.  Because if they were, they'd have Pro accounts, and run servers with what *they* think of as "traditional" server mechanics.  Then if people liked them, they'd join.  You can't have your Quake and eat it guys.  (Sorry for the pun, but you know, dad jokes and all...)
tldr;
Quake Live is awesome.  Fast and awesome.  With the best bangy-gun-feeling (R) and shooty-mechanics (tm) of any FPS you'll play.  Don't let your life go by without playing one of the funnest games ever.

I can honestly recommend this 100%. I have used blender for about 4 years now, and I was happy when it came to Steam. That means it's community is growing rapidly. Anyway, on to the review part (I will break this up into features).
100% FREE FOREVER
Blender is free completely, always has been and always will be. That is what the team has said. You will not have to ever pay a single penny. No catch. Simple as that. You can donate if you want to but it is never mandatory. There is also merchandise you can buy but again, not mandatory.
3D MODELING
Blender's 3D modeling is very easy once you get used to it. Everything in Blender just takes a little time to get used to. The 3D modeling is powerful and precise. Not much more I can say on that, it is just awesome.
ANIMATION
Again, once you get used to it, animating is very easy and powerful. Now don't let the word "easy" trick you into thinking it limits your freedom. Animation is quite awesome. You can set bones to anything. If you want a skeleton that can twist and turn like a body, you just need to have verticies where the bone joint is so the model has somewhere to bend. If it is a single face, nothing can deform that way.
MATERIALS/TEXTURING/RENDERING
Blender has a great system for adding textures and creating materials. Whether it's wood, metal, grass, glass, lava or water, you can make any kind of metarial. You can use the node editor to make 100 times more complicated effects.
You can make cartooney looks, sci-fi looks, even photorealistic looks. Everything in that video on the homepage is made with blender, all of it. You wouldn't think some of that was animated.
GAME ENGINE
This is the only single part of Blender I don't fully recommend. It just seems a little under developed at the moment. It is a great and powerful game engine, however there is alot to be improved. I am sure it will get better over time for Blender is still updating.
GUI
The entire inteface is completley editable. You can change the color of buttons, background, axis, windows and more. You can change the location of many parts. Also aweosme.
All in all, I recommend Blender all the way.

Braid is a nice, short, enjoyable game to put it simply. It's a 2D platforming puzzler set in a gorgeous painterly world with one of the best soundtracks in modern gaming. The gameplay involves manipulating time to solve clever puzzles that earn you jigsaw pieces to a painting that hints at further back-story and helps open the path to the final chapter… which is actually the first chapter in the story. It's refreshingly forgiving in that you can never die and need only rewind time to do something just right; this focuses your attention on trying to complete a challenge rather than needing to re-play entire areas or continuously try to make the same jump over and over again. I deeply appreciate that.
The ending sequence to a story that is told through hind-sight and recall is a level of brilliance that made all the time spent playing it worth every second.
