To state it simply as I can, there is no way that I can do enough to recommend
as highly as it deserves.  In the Kentucky Derby of the rather numerous games (a few of which have or are solid enough to merit at least some serious note) in this generally broad set of the Post-Apocalyptic/Survival genre of the current/modern PC scene,
is a Thoroughbred Champion of the most uncomplicated sort.
The thundering hooves of the race set the pace out of the gate, nearly beating a tattoo on your ribs from within the moment you find yourself thawed and unceremoniously deposited into a world that appears to not only have been blasted and scarred by the now typical arsenal of Post-Apocalyptica, but also one haunted by Werewolf-like monsters -among a number of others-  that are both imminently fatal, but also understated in a way that for my own part recalls the same sort of creeping, crawling, truly psychological horror upon my initial encounters with some of Lovecraft's more authentically gripping horrors.
With a pedigree of the caliber that
boasts for itself in my ever so discerning gaming tastes, the more atypical or "monstrous and supernatural" of the associations piercing my own memory and stretching all the way back to 1931 and the horror that rose from Y'ha-nthlei to consume and squat over Innsmouth as the Dagon's Deep Ones.  The second major thread is likely more easily expected and certainly open to being related to by a (vastly) wider audience in the sense of the overall and yet still growing popularity of the genre, this association springs forward over (the next two and three) centuries, bathed in the near incandescence of the white washed mediocrity of the just shy of unending faux 1950s Apple Pie-Americana and all consuming oceans of nuclear fire and equally inescapable Fallout.
In contrast to the almost stark bleakness that Lovecraft instilled in me at times - without being overtly apocalyptic; whereas Fallout inspired and from time to time continues to inspire the notion that humanity might well resist and rise again on the dark side of whatever Great Catastrophe it happens to be this time.  And it is certainly a blend of these personal, half-imagined (and again, doubly personalized) inspirations and senses of direction for my gaming imagination that are invoked upon finding my way out into
wide-open Michigan, a great American state that it would seem will take a little more than a single puny Apocalypse to wipe off the map altogether.
I imagine that aside from being a logical decision for a one-man marching band, along with/and cost-effective from the angle of overhead and production costs, the old-school vibe and streamlined
go a great ways in the direction of encouraging the individual player to engage the game in a way that other, more modern examples do not and cannot allow for.  Specifically, there aren't so many details, so many aspects of the experience predetermined by hard-coded and visualized default automatically and inescapably included in the Scavenging experience from the mouse click on.
The Crafting System is a standout aspect of the Gameplay Mechanics for
, which speaks to a bit of that aforementioned logic - it being pretty pointless to spend an entire game scavenging for junk that doesn't, or can't be combined with something to do or become anything useful.  The type and variety of that junk you'll be so happily scavenging is at a fair balance at the moment - though more melee and/or ranged (re: improvised DMRs/battle rifles) weapons of any stripe and variety, as well as pretty much any new items at all will always make me happy.  The combat system is similarly uncomplicated and crisp, though perhaps taking a game session or two for many of the more fast-paced FPS-twitchy gamers of the here and now.
It's these invitations to the individual imagination that - along with the perfectly applied Game Mechanics- are the most easy and obvious examples of the true genius you can find here.  Or, to restate it again in final summary, there's so much about
that will allow the gamer to become as immersed in and rewarded by their experience as the breadth, depth and staying power of their imagination will allow.

Following Saints Row the Third is the fourth game that goes even beyond boundaries of what SRIII offered. I don't want to spoil too much but after a parody of Apocalypse Now follows a parody of Armagedon with Aerosmith's "Don't want to miss a thing" and a Alien Invasion by the most sophisticated Alien either, he even quotes Shakespear and MacBeth, being voiced by J. B. Blanc (who played Dr. Barry Goodman on Breaking Bad and is otherwise known from a lot of games and animes like Naruto, World or Warcraft or as the voice of Bane in Arkham Origins)
The big criticism this game has seen was the fact that the side quests are always the same mini games: jump up a tower, destroy everything in a tank, run a track like sonic or load up a virus by killing a ton of enemies and while it's true that this gets repetitive after a while, i have to saw with all the superpowers and crazy weapons at your desposal it doesn't get boring, you can always bring a new gun weapon and experience a fight new.
The main story missions truly shine as they are a parody of various games. Stealth is made look like a joke in a parody of Metal Gear Solid and Splinter Cell, later you encounter "Saints of Rage". You ride a motorcycle to cyberspace, get into a text adventure where you have to find your way through multiple choice answers and do some quick time events.
The Voice acting is again awesome with Keith David acting as a politican and in one of his last big projects the late great Rowdy Roddy Piper plays himself, having Keith David here too of course leads to a recreation of the classic movie The Live.
The weapons and superpowers you have, you are a super hero in this game with extreme powers, you can shoot fireballs, hover cars in the air only to shoot them at opponents or run faster than light speed. While that makes cars obsolete you can still use cars and tune them in the rim store shop.
The Music is alos great again with various radio stations and a ton of licenced songs, like in SR3 you can make your own mixtape but you can't import your own music.
I played it several times now, in co-op it's even better and a ton of fun. I can only recommend it.

Let's just get one thing clear up front. No. It is not as good as the original Company of Heroes.
Why?
It's the little things. To put it simply, where COH1 felt like an RTS equivalent of a classic war movie, COH2 feels gamey, seeming to cater exclusively to multiplayer. I've watched submachinegunners firing entire clips at point blank range into artillery crews who just stand there, not dying for what feels like an eternity. Where in COH1 you could build sandbag walls and tank traps and barbed wire that seemed to fit seemlessly into their surroundings, player structures in COH2 stand out like a sore thumb. Sure it's a little more streamlined to have a fixed structure you place that serves its purpose, but it just doesn't feel as immersive as something that looks like something you'd actually see on the battlefield. I could go on about how increadibly long it takes to kill a tank while other units can be wiped out by one mortar round but I'll stop myself.
The campaign is reasonably fun but feels overly political. I mean, I'm pretty anti-communist myself but a lot of the attrocities depicted in the campaign are just depicted in a way that makes the bad communist commissar look more like a cartoon villain than a genuinely evil person. It's all just so ridiculous that it's hard to actually care when something awful happens.
COH2 isn't, for all this, a bad game by any means. It's still my favorite basic model for an RTS and in many ways it does improve on COH1. The graphics are better. The sound is better, particularly when your camera is far from the action and the sounds of your units fighting on different parts of the map mesh together to create an ambient battlefield sound that is immesely fun to listen to. COH2 also features a fun mission mode which can be a nice break from the simple, straightforward skirmish.
In the end this game just barely warrents a 3/5 from me. It's a definite step down from COH1 for the franchise but it's still a solid game that, were it not for the legacy of its predecessor would be truly amazing.

Summary: One of the top 10 games in my entire library (of over 2,000 games). This is a TRUE co-operative experience of a kind that's rarely seen. Like another great example, "Lovers in a Dangerous Spacetime", this game has perfectly captured the essence of co-operative play, and player co-ordination through strong communication. Unlike most "co-op" games, trying to go it alone, or trying to "be the best guy" doesn't fly here. You and up to 3 teammates will rush about to gather, prepare, cook and serve delicious food in a multitude of exciting and often dangerous environments. This may well be the best truly co-operative gaming experience available to date.
Pros:
+ Designed around co-operative play
+ Co-op Campaign
+ The "lone wolf" mentality is rightly the worst choice, as should be the case in a good co-op experience
+ Quick to learn
+ Encourages participation from gamers of a variety of skill levels
+ Demands strong communication between players
+ The screen is tidy, and everything sized just right to lend to visual clarity
+ Up to 4 players can play at once
+ Couch co-op works well with Steam link working great, and the game has excellent controller support
Cons:
- Local co-op only. This may turn away some players, but I prefer local co-op so this didn't bother me.
- Nothing else, really. I want more of it, but that's just because I want the fun to continue forever!

This is the first Telltale game I played and it will probably stay the only one.
This kind of "game" is more like an interactive movie and I am not a big fan of that, besides that the theme of the other games don't really interests me, like Borderlands and Walking Dead. But I am a huge GoT fan, so I wanted to try at least that one out. I don't regret to have played it but I won't change my mind to that kind of "game" either.
To be fair the game has a respectable length, the synchronization of the characters is great. To speak of the characters, they are mostly invented by Telltale, only a few characters of the show also appears in some scenes and of course they are spoken by the respective actor. In the center of the story is house Forrester, vassals of the Starks. And Telltale took that too literal. You can assign almost every member of House Forrester to a member of House Stark. I guess you can say the story of the game is more like a parallel story to the show. If you can overlook that you have mostly characters which you carry for.
Also the music is great, now you may say of course it is because it's GoT, but Telltale made also their own music and they really don't have to be ashamed for that. Specifically Talia's Song at the end of Episode 2 is so beautiful.
Now the points I didn't liked: Like the other Telltale games it uses a cel shading look. Either you like it or not, I don't. But I can live with it. The game only runs with 40 fps, at least with my pc. While the character animations are mostly really good, special effects are not. Like I said before, this is more an interactive movie so gameplay is almost not existent.
But the biggest problems are the called story decisions. Because usually they have no effect at the big picture of the story. The story continues like Telltale wants not how you want it. They usually effect little things and mostly the decisions have a pattern: Do that to please person A (or yourself) and displease person B or the otherway.
Now you can decide if this game is for you. To make it simple I'd say I can recommend this game to fans of Telltale and/or GoT, otherwise skip it.

Boy i really wanted to give this a thumbs down, write a crappy, rage fueled review, and call it a day. But i withheld my anger and took time to reflect on my experience with the game. I have to say, this might be a buy for most people! "MOST" is the key word here.
This is basically alien invasion simulator. You manage everything in the Xcom division, from construction, research, troop managment, basic world politics, and missions by way of turn based mechanics. And this game is brutal, as it kind of should be. Super advanced aliens raiding a planet inhabited by a species who can barely understand space travel? Yea, they will probably have other kinds of weaponary to melt our faces off.
This game is deep! Deeper than anything i've played in a long time. Field tactics are very important to successful missions. So many kinds of research, almost too many, and if you try to do everything, you'll fail. Figuring out if researching weapons, armor, or the alien species is more important is tough, but there is no wrong path. Everything from construction, research, healing wounded soldiers take multiple days, even weeks to complete. In that time, you could be given a crucial mission, or a country is in danger forcing hard decisions, making everything you do extremly meaningful. There is always a sense of danger looming over everything, and its enthralling.
However, this is not for everyone. This game adds one more layer of excitement, You can completely fail and be forced to start all over again. Those hard choices i mentioned earlier, sometimes 3 nations be attacked at once, and you can only save one, the other 2 will have their panic level increased. If it get too much for that country, they pull funding from your organization. If too many pull away from you, its game over, It doesn't matter how much time you've invested into your save. Fortunately for me, i only lost about 5 hours just recently. If that is something you hate, avoid this game like the plague.
Everything else however is pretty great, the great stories i've put together in my head based on what happened in game, are pretty memorable, heroic, and down right Face palming. I've renamed and customized my soldiers after my friends, which pushes me even harder to fight smarter and keep them alive. Also leaves you stricken with guilt watching them die.
Do i recomend it? yes, but only if you have any passive interest in turn based stratagy. Also if you're willing to accept that you're going to screw up multiple times as a new player, and suffer the harsh consequences of your failures, maybe even starting over from scratch.
Now im going to set this game aside for a week or 2 and maybe come back, who knows....

I can't ever remember liking and being so frustrated with same game.   I feel the game should be played in ironman mode because playing the same map over and over until you luck into winning combo seems pointless.   That being said,  I think that there is a diffuculty setting missing in this game.   Normal feel extremely easy.   In my 1st playthrough, knowing nothing about the game,  I just breezed through the content.   So I decided to jump up to classic...It's a lot lot harder but sometimes exciting because it puts you on edge because things become important.   But I still feel that there should be a difficulty between the two.
My main frustation from this game comes from losing people from quirks in the map.   I would say about 50 percent of all my deaths come from some invisible thing that I couldn't anticipate.  For example,  I'm on top middle of the roof and the AI, from the ground, shoots through the side of the building then through the top of the roof to kill my best soldier.   It wouldn't make me so angry if there was some consistency to these type of shots but you just never know if a solid wall is really a solid wall.  To make matters worse,  sometimes the opposite happens.   You move into postion to what is clearly an open shot only to find once you have expended your action that computer has deemed it impossible.   Of course,  the alien with one hp,  kills someone in  your squad next turn.    Sometimes entire campaigns hang in the balance of these random map quirks,  especially when you lose said soldier early on a difficult map or your entire squad starts to panick.
With that being said,  I really like the rest of the game.   The tactical gameplay and character building are extremely fun and addicting.   There are tons of different paths through xcom headquarters which also adds extra depth.  The only thing i would ask for would be some light or color in the game.   I'm sure they probably did it for some type of dark alien atmosphere but I find it a little depressing after hours of gamepley.  Maybe just add a view sunny maps or maps with sun rays poking through.
So I reluctantly give this game a thumbs up because it kept me engaged and entertained for over 100 hours.   But I don't know if I can play it again because quirks are so frustrating in the end..

PSA:  You can't render fire in Cycles Render on your GPU, you HAVE to use your CPU as of 2.76b.
*For the Newer 3D modlers:* Welcome to the world of 3D modeling!  If you have used another program (such as Wings 3D) or might find blender confusing at first, but as someone who moved from Wings3D to Blender I can tell you it is worth it 100%.  Blender is a great program.  What is that you say?  Never 3D modeled before and you are looking to get into it?  Don't be afraid!  Blender is a complex program at first, but it's power more than makes up for it.  Getting into blender as your first 3D modeling software means you are immediately working with profressional grade software.  Blender isn't easy to learn or get into, but youtube has some great tutorials that will help you greatly.  With a little time and effort you will begin modeling and creating in no time!
*For the 3d modelers, animators, 3d sculpters and video editors:* I have used Blender before off of steam and I greatly enjoy having it on steam.  Blender does Animation, 3D modeling, 3D scupting AND Video editing.  It's an awesome program with a variety of uses and I highly recommend it.  Youtube is a great place to get tutorials to get you up to speed on the software's controls.
*For the Gamers and others who have stumbled upon the Blender store page:* If you are at all interested in creating digital art (such as models, animation, or even just editing some cool clips of some n00bs getting pwnd) then Blender is great to have!  It's a VERY powerful program and if you follow along with some tutorials it's actually fairly easy to use once you have the very basics down.  Also, don't be worried about the tedium of messing with individual points in a mesh, I SWARE to you that is my favorite part of modeling.  There is a calming feeling that makes me completely at peace and I have only found it in two things: Music and messin' with Verts.  Trust me, 3D modeling is something you should at least look into if you are a creative person.  Blender is free and professional grade, there is no better program for you to start with out there!
Note related to Video Editors: I advise you look up a quick tutorial in order to get you started with editing in Blender, however, just so you are not completely confused: Blender starts out in 3D modeling mode.  Up in the upper left you should see a little i then File, Render, Window, and Help.  To the RIGHT of these there should eb a thing that says "Default" and looks a bit different.  Click on the icon to its immediate left and it should open up a drop down menu from which you can select "Video Editing."  This will load a preset config for UI.  I highly advise you change the Graph editor widnow (the one in the top left; above the timeline) to "Properties" via the icon in the lower left hand corner.  Then, change the FPS to 30 or whichever FPS your files were recorded at.
For the VFX guys:
Well... Blender just gets better and better the more time I sink into it.  The VFX side of blender is a tad bit scary at first (For people new to VFX anywho), but it is really powerful.  The more I use the node editor the more I fall in love with it.  It's very easy and simple once you get to know how it works.  With easy FX such as Quick Smoke, you can start to make really cool stuff almost immediately.  However, if you are at all new to VFX in a program like blender you will HAVE to watch some youtube tutorials.  VFX in blender isn't something you can just pick up immediately when you have no experience.  Watch youtube tutorials and DON'T GET FRUSTRATED.  Blender has a way of making things not work for a logical reason.  The problem is you don't often know what this logical reason is.  Don't overwork yourself.  Give some VFX projects a break when you are hitting a stone wall.  Post on the forums (Steam or otherwise), watch youtube tutorials, and DON'T GET FRUSTRATED.
tl;dr
Great program.  Capable of a variety of things. (Animation, 3D modeling, VFX, and Video Editing)  Complex for new users.  Recommend Youtube for tutorials.

A puzzle game disguised as an action packed cooking game! One must save the onion kingdom by cooking adequate amounts of food for the all-destroying spaghetti monster, but first, one travels through the galaxy to be trained in the fine art of cooking.

-tons of variety in the map and recipes
-everyone working towards the same goal, which I find surprisingly little in the market
-short and sweet levels
-nice and easy graphics
CONS:
-singleplayer not fleshed out, just one player controlling two characters.
-music selection fairly small, you kind of tune it out because it is an intense game but it still gets to you a little.
-split control on the keyboard is fairly awkward, player on the left must place one hand on top of the other since you are using WASD and shift alt and ctrl. Almost guaranteed handcramps.

Wow! One of the best games I have ever played. I love zombie themed games and this is basically FarCry 3 with Zombies (seriously I'm convinced the devs from Dying Light used the same engine as there were features that I've absolutely seen in both games). An absolute must play. 10/10
Pros
- Story and cutscene animations are excellent
- Gorgeous (or should I say disgusting?) artwork really helps with the vibe
- The Parkour is some of the most fun part of the game
- Weapons are fantastic
- RPG elements unlock new features at a good pace
- Game world is huge with lots of in-game content that will let you keep playing long after the main storyline is over
- The night missions help you never feel quite safe even when your character is overpowered
- The Following episode adds the buggy. Running over zombies is more fun than I would like to admit.
- The game is not overly frightening but the engine can randomly produce some decent jump scares
Cons
- The later The Following episode had a number of "soft" ledges where the character would miss grabbing on to something that the skin made look grabbable. This led to quite a few annoying deaths during high climbs.
- The Bozak's horde extra missions had a great idea but the save system annoyed me to the point that I decided not to finish them.
- Eventually your character becomes so overpowered that killing zombies can become almost a nuisance
- Besides adding missions, once a safe zone is unlocked it didn't have much more to offer than a safe place to sleep and/or sell stuff. I felt this was a missed opportunity as I would have loved to see some base building or defense elements included in the game.

This game is a masterpiece of co-op play! The controls are simple and require seconds to master, while level design and a need for cooperation add complexity and depth to the game. The game-play is simple enough: take ingredients over to the chopping board, take chopped ingredients to the pan/fryer/pot, plate the dish and serve. This sort of cooking management game has been done many times, but never with this finesse and attention to detail. Each level brings something new to the table and forces players to communicate, strategize, and improvise on the spot, while maintaining a constant delivery speed to rack up points. This game is challenging and fun and will offer extended replay value with up to 4 players.

There are two types of HOGs. Strictly HOGs and ones with puzzles added in. This is one that also has puzzles. They aren't difficult puzzles though, and definately won't trip you up much if you're not much of a puzzle solver. I beat this game in about 6 hours, but went back and played it again for the achievements.
I've played alot of HOGs and am very fond of them, and I can say that this one isn't bad. The artwork of the scenes themselves are good, even if the characters look a bit strange. The story flows nicely, which I find doesn't usually happen in these types of games. There were no lose ends, all the charaters had useful parts, and it didn't leave you wondering about anything (except for the parts that were meant too). They also gave you information in a coherent way. No finding dry documents in a flooded sewer for no reason, or exploring some random strangers house for clues. It was cohesive. It also had an unusual twist on the object hunt scenes by having "detective scenes". These won't be for everyone, but I enjoyed them.
Only things I can point out as cons are the back and forth between scenes. Lots of clicking all the way across the maps to find one object, then go all the way, use it, go 5-6 scenes to another part, ect... You only really finished with two out of about 15 areas. The only other issue was repeat and unusual objects. I think I needed to find a stamp or cigar in 90% of the scenes. A few of the scenes also had objects that were culturally obscure. Like African symbols. I only knew them bc I watch the Discovery Channel. I don't know how other people would find them without the hint system. It just seemed odd to have those kind of things in a game like this.
Overall this was a nice, casual game. Not too difficult, not too long (unlike this review), flowed nicely, and had a bit of humor and sarcasim to boot. I'd definately recommend this to HOG fans.

If you ever wanted a nice, easy, and stylish noir adventure in the form of a hidden object puzzle that won’t take longer than an average movie, then 9 Clues is your title.
9 Clues: The Secret of Serpent Creek is all about style. The 1950s noir detective story motif and the incredibly talented scene compositions– which feature slanted shots and lots of wide angle close ups– create a powerful atmosphere. Too bad the same cannot be said about the over the top characters and the horrible voice acting (not counting the protagonist, whose performance saves a few scenes).
Despite the 2013 release date the low resolution graphics and some design flaws make it feel like as if the game was made around 2007, especially in the normal puzzle segments. It’s not like as if the game isn’t trying: it introduces a new HOP type called Detective Mode, a welcomed addition, and also an integral part of the story. But even that can’t help the largest problem, the length. Even the most casual player should be able to finish it well under three hours, making 9 Clues nothing more than a nice one-afternoon entertainment for a low price.

I can't ever remember liking and being so frustrated with same game.   I feel the game should be played in ironman mode because playing the same map over and over until you luck into winning combo seems pointless.   That being said,  I think that there is a diffuculty setting missing in this game.   Normal feel extremely easy.   In my 1st playthrough, knowing nothing about the game,  I just breezed through the content.   So I decided to jump up to classic...It's a lot lot harder but sometimes exciting because it puts you on edge because things become important.   But I still feel that there should be a difficulty between the two.
My main frustation from this game comes from losing people from quirks in the map.   I would say about 50 percent of all my deaths come from some invisible thing that I couldn't anticipate.  For example,  I'm on top middle of the roof and the AI, from the ground, shoots through the side of the building then through the top of the roof to kill my best soldier.   It wouldn't make me so angry if there was some consistency to these type of shots but you just never know if a solid wall is really a solid wall.  To make matters worse,  sometimes the opposite happens.   You move into postion to what is clearly an open shot only to find once you have expended your action that computer has deemed it impossible.   Of course,  the alien with one hp,  kills someone in  your squad next turn.    Sometimes entire campaigns hang in the balance of these random map quirks,  especially when you lose said soldier early on a difficult map or your entire squad starts to panick.
With that being said,  I really like the rest of the game.   The tactical gameplay and character building are extremely fun and addicting.   There are tons of different paths through xcom headquarters which also adds extra depth.  The only thing i would ask for would be some light or color in the game.   I'm sure they probably did it for some type of dark alien atmosphere but I find it a little depressing after hours of gamepley.  Maybe just add a view sunny maps or maps with sun rays poking through.
So I reluctantly give this game a thumbs up because it kept me engaged and entertained for over 100 hours.   But I don't know if I can play it again because quirks are so frustrating in the end..

Ok, to start out I want to say I love this game and any criticisms is because I want it to be better ok? Good! So in Neo Scavenger you are basically given one of two goals: A-Survive Or B-Story based playthroughs. to tell you the average life expectancy of any character is really not a for sure answer just because of the learning curve, this game takes micro-managing to quite a substantial level and unless you keep up with it you're gonna bleed out of your eyes and you won't notice because you didn't read the red text! Another great thing about this game is the combat system, rather than having a "Health Bar" it has more of a..."How much♥♥♥♥♥♥can you Eat Before you die" bar, now what I mean by this is you can take hits to the face with a Crowbar and still have a chance of survival, even though at that point you'd probably be "earing♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; thus the name! Genius! There is of course the as always Eating, Drinking, sleeping bars, but this game is kind of speacial due to it's tempature and pain bars, tempature is pretty self-explanatory so I'm going to stick to the "Pain" bar. It basically shows how badly your player is feeling so for example if he fell down he'd probably have a bum knee and that produces a bruise and minor pain, but if some dude rushes you with a cleaver and starts hacking into your stomach with it, he's gonna feel a little differently, And to wrap it up let's talk about the less than wanted things of about the game. Because of it's damage system and the random number generators you can sometimes get killed pretty ridiculously, for example I was killed once with a stick because he hit me in the head hard enough...Now while I like the damage system beacuse of it's complexity, that has to be fixed and I believe they are working on bugs like that, secondly the random number generator can be a real♥♥♥♥♥sometimes and even when you are supposed to be getting loot because you have a full loot chance bar you get nothing, I believe the developer is also looking into this. I really love this game and even though there are some rough patches I really hope the devolper can sand them down and hopefully bring this game to full potential! (Modding is involved in the game I did not cover it though because Steam doesn't have a Mod Page for it. Oh and by the way sorry for how long it is, there's just so much greatness in the game that giving it half a sentance didn't sit well with me.)

Before the recent drops update, you had to level up to get new items (Commanders, Intel, et cetera), this was alright, in the sense that the items weren't even that bad. The new system changed that. The 'points' system rewards you with a "random" drop (again, Commanders and so forth) after collecting a score of 6000 by playing games. I quoted "random" as everytime I have recieved a drop it has always contained points. 500 to be exact. To get a random £5 skin pack, I'd need 22500 points. To get 22500 points I'd have to get 45 drops. To get the 6000 score to get 1 drop, I need to play either 3-4 games, as playing a game (to the end) rewards 1500 and winning an additional 500. An average game lasts around 30-40 minutes. So, just to get ONE £5 I'd have to play 180 games. If each game averaged at 35 minutes, thats 6,300 minutes. 105 hours. 4.375 days straight. FOUR DAYS. It's stupid as the average wage in the UK is £72 per day. THATS £288 YOU COULD SPEND ON FOOD AND HAVE LEFT FOR CoH INSTEAD OF PLAYING THIS FOR 4♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ING DAYS.

Pros

There are many different recources: There are many different recources, stratigic recources(things you will need for military and construction) such as Horses, Iron, and Uranium. And map editor
Cons
Every game is the same
In my experaince, every single game I just end up doing the same thing. no matter who I play as, what aprouch I take, and what map. The game get extremely repetative. The eras do not seem different, exept for the new units and buildings, which never change the experaince.
The game does not change troughout the eras
You would think that as time passed, the game would change. Unfortunitly, that is not the case. Comparing the game from the classicle era to the modern era, not much has changed. The deplomacy has not changed, the millitary stratagy has not changed, etc.
War
The war is this game is horrible for me. Basicly, the more powerful unit wins in a fight. I am not asking for something very intense and detailed like Total War, but just more than, the most powerful unit wins. Also, when you do go to war, all of your allainces are ruined. If you declare war everyone hates you. Even if you dont declare war every one hates you. For example: Once Greece declared war on me. I defeated their army, pushed them out of my land and took Sparta. I began fighting the Greeks second army near Athens. Suddenly, England(not allied with Greece) yelled at me for being a savage. Why? I defeated the second Greek army and tried to make peace. Alexander said no, so I began besieging Athens. Then Brazil(one of MY allies) denounced me. After I took Athens me and Greece made peace, I gave back Sparta and Athens, I had no use for holding them. Then whole f*cking world starting donouncing me.
The deplomacy is lacking
I am comparing this to a game I really like, the Total War series. Other the alliances and trade deals, you cant do much with other countries. In TW you can do a little more, such as forming confederacies and having vassels. Cities can rebel and such in TW. In civ, you can trade and form alliences. Nitpicks
The world is not round until a certian point in the gam
cities cant succeed
Mechs and xcom squads are way to overpowered
Conclusion
Over all the game is good for a time or you play with friends. If you want something that shows the growth of a civilization over thousands of years, yes I would recommend this. But If you want a diplomatic/millitary stratagy, I would recommend a game from the Total War series.

An excellent game and in a way it feels like an entire season of episodes of the Game of Thrones series. It plays like an interactive movie.....a long movie (in a good way).
Some players seem to have issues with the fact that you cannot control everything with the choices that you are given. The best way to see it is that there is a plot that unfolds and how various aspects of that plot take place are decided by the player just like the plot of the Dead marching south cannot be changed in the Game of Thrones movie series, but the relative positions of power between Houses can be changed. Personally I do not see the issue with that....it is exactly like Game of Thrones and real life where you cannot control everything. Some things you can influence, other things you cannot influence. This is Game of Thrones and not Fluffy Pink Unicorn land where nothing bad ever happens.
The story is great and that is what matters the most. It should be played once I would say without trying to back paddle on the choices you have made. The frustration that some experience is when those players try to influence events that they cannot. Play it like every decision really matters. It is Game of Thrones after all. Don't try to min/max, load and retry again. Those who play in the real Game of Thrones only get to play once. Do it wisely and leave the carebear mentality somewhere else.
There is also a second season coming up. Some might be upset about various 'unfortunate' events that happen during the first season, but victory only truly means something in the face of having previously experienced various defeats. Those who only win or only lose cannot place matters in perspective. I really like the plot and along the way you encounter various famous characters from the Game of Thrones series. For Game of Thrones fans, this game is absolutely wonderful.

It may sound weird to some, but
is actually the first
I've ever played. And to make it immediately clear: I liked it a lot! It's stylish, cleverly designed and it has an original story.
was developed by Tap It Games and published by the well-known Artifex Mundi in July 2013. Some research out of my newly-found interest in this genre, has learned me that Artifex Mundi is perhaps THE prime publisher of this kind of games, and after playing a second one of their games, I can safely confirm that they stand for quality and sheer gaming pleasure.
could be defined as an adventure-light, or casual adventure game, with a touch of horror added to it. The story is quite original and entertaining and certainly proved interesting enough to keep my interest right through to the final stages. I won't spoil it here, suffice it only to tell that it is also suited for teenagers and maybe even younger children, since there is no offensive context in any way. There are also a whole bunch of helping-tools, perfectly adaptable to everyone's needs with three difficulty levels. Exactly as how it should be done in this kind of games, imo.
The actual gameplay is very much point-and-click orientated, with static screens following upon each other. Most of the times there are objects to be found to advance to the next screen, to solve a puzzle, or to be combined with each other. Thanks to the very intuitive inventory, all this can be done in a smooth manner, and thanks to the map (with fast-travel system incorporated), the amount of backtracking is limited. The shining point of the game are the famous "Hidden Object" scenes, where one has to click several named objects in order to find one story-related object. As easy as this may sound, it proved quite a lot of fun, and even challenge to a non-native English speaker as me. I made a sport out of it not to consult any dictionay, and I've certainly learned a whole bunch a new English word just by playing this game ;-). Apart from the Hidden Object-screens, there are also quite some well-designed puzzles, more of a challenge but still very well designed and easily solved with some thinking.
Since gameplay is limited to pointing, clicking and thinking, graphics and sound are very important to me in this kind of adventure (light). And in these departments
certainly delivers. The scenes are vividly painted, with bright coulours if needed and lots of visual clues. Sound-wise, there's not much to complain about: voice-acting is fine, only the music could have delivered more of a punch.
All in all, this was a very fine first encounter for me wtih this genre, and with the quality-products Artifex Mundi delivers. Don't hesitate if you like this kind of games, and do give it a try when you're curious about them. It's not expensive, and as icing on the cake: it comes with Trading Cards and a set of Steam Achievements that can be made into a perfect game without too much hassle.

Worthwhile - if you know what you're letting yourself in for.
This is a sim with many problems. The graphics are about as badly optimised as most of these sims, so it can get quite chuggy even with its relatively simple graphics; saving is very wobbly indeed and has a habit of wiping one's setups; the extremely repetitive background music can't be switched off without also muting the show soundtrack; user-configured racks don't have a simultaneous ignition option, and so on.
But what works works fairly well, and there are some good ideas there. I like the fact that it shows an audio waveform to help line up the effects (though a slow option and step keys would be useful), and allows you to line up airbursts both by launch time and by detonation time. The graphics are rudimentary but look quite pretty within their limitations.
It's not perfect. In many ways it's barefly functional. It's certainly not worth full price. And the devs seem to have abandoned it, so there's a big caveat emptor hanging over it. But I've had some fun with it, and if you catch it on sale you might too.

NOTE: Do not play this game unless you have finished watching season 4 of Game of Thrones. It has a few big spoilers in it for the series. Things in Season 4 will come up occasionally in the game.
Game of Thrones (GoT) was possibly my favorite Telltale game. I say "was," though. Then I got to the last two episodes and some of my love faded. If you are a GoT fan, and like the Telltale games like The Walking Dead, A Wolf Among Us, and Tales from the Borderlands, then this is definitely a game worth checking out. Telltale seems to have a knack for mimicking different franchises, and they've had a lot of success. This game did a lot of GoT stuff so, so right. The lore, the voice acting, the violence, the intrigue, the treachery, and even some fun, surprise character deaths. I was enthralled with this game. Something at the beginning of episode 2 had me cheering for a certain character and panicking, trying to survive, and it was a really fun moment and led to neat developments for the rest of the season. It's incredibly rare I experience that sort of thing in games.
However, despite being a big fan of GoT, and fully embracing the killing of characters throughout, I felt like the Telltale game was very dissatisfying in that regard beginning with episode 5 onward. I won't spoil who dies, of course, but in the actual show, a character dying is either a big shock, a bit sad, or even loved (if you hated the character). However, I've always felt like it was the right decision, even minutes after seeing it. It's almost always glorious writing. It makes the events play out even better and in my opinion, making the show interesting and exciting, and protecting the characters who make the show as entertaining as it is. There's that worry someone might die, so you root for them more, but the show is pretty fair in that regard. Some might disagree with me, but it seems just.
With the Telltale GoT game, however, in my opinion, they got a murder boner for episode 5 onward. Certainly, characters need to die for the plot, and to make things interesting with it being near the end of the season, but it just felt, to me, like Telltale was trying to copy GoT's kill-important-characters ideology at its most basic concept: just killing characters. Very few of the deaths from season 5 onward felt like they would do wonderful things for the storyline. How do I say this? In the show...it's like they're dying for the greater good of the plot. In the last couple of episodes of the
, however, it just felt like they were trying to hit a character death quota. There was no beauty or narrative glory in these killings, and if they're killing characters I like, then they'd damn well better be doing it for the right reasons.
Anyway, aside from that, I had a marvelous time with the game. Most of the plot and the setting was wonderful, I felt like I was watching a long, interactive season of GoT, and got to interact occasionally with a few characters from the show. This is a good game, marred by a required death quota without doing so for the easily perceived improvement of the story.

Ok, to start out I want to say I love this game and any criticisms is because I want it to be better ok? Good! So in Neo Scavenger you are basically given one of two goals: A-Survive Or B-Story based playthroughs. to tell you the average life expectancy of any character is really not a for sure answer just because of the learning curve, this game takes micro-managing to quite a substantial level and unless you keep up with it you're gonna bleed out of your eyes and you won't notice because you didn't read the red text! Another great thing about this game is the combat system, rather than having a "Health Bar" it has more of a..."How much♥♥♥♥♥♥can you Eat Before you die" bar, now what I mean by this is you can take hits to the face with a Crowbar and still have a chance of survival, even though at that point you'd probably be "earing♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; thus the name! Genius! There is of course the as always Eating, Drinking, sleeping bars, but this game is kind of speacial due to it's tempature and pain bars, tempature is pretty self-explanatory so I'm going to stick to the "Pain" bar. It basically shows how badly your player is feeling so for example if he fell down he'd probably have a bum knee and that produces a bruise and minor pain, but if some dude rushes you with a cleaver and starts hacking into your stomach with it, he's gonna feel a little differently, And to wrap it up let's talk about the less than wanted things of about the game. Because of it's damage system and the random number generators you can sometimes get killed pretty ridiculously, for example I was killed once with a stick because he hit me in the head hard enough...Now while I like the damage system beacuse of it's complexity, that has to be fixed and I believe they are working on bugs like that, secondly the random number generator can be a real♥♥♥♥♥sometimes and even when you are supposed to be getting loot because you have a full loot chance bar you get nothing, I believe the developer is also looking into this. I really love this game and even though there are some rough patches I really hope the devolper can sand them down and hopefully bring this game to full potential! (Modding is involved in the game I did not cover it though because Steam doesn't have a Mod Page for it. COH was my favorite RTS of all time. I really like the historical aspect of the game. The top positive reviewer of this game points out that COH2 is a lot more balanced and artillery is less effective and armour units require more support. Judged purely as an RTS, it has better balancing of forces, but that ruined the game for me. Having played a lot of the Eastern Front mod, this new game was a huge downgrade. No mobs of poorly trained Russian infantry, no elite German troops that cut through them. I really like how Eastern front and the original COH gave each side their historical advantages. Germans had units that could crush anything on the map, but were expensive and few in number. Early Russian units were cheap, plentiful, and expendable. I have no love for a WWII RTS where all sides are equal. They don't have to be equal to use their unique advantages to overpower the other. Infantry is almost on the same level as armour on this game, what is up with that?!?

This game looks like a lot of fun and has a lot of potential, but unless you have four people, I wouldn't recommend it. I played with one other person, and although it was fun at first, we quickly felt like we couldn't get ahead of the orders. The game is setup as such that orders start coming and you have to complete as many as possible in four minutes. The orders just stack up and up, and no matter what, you feel like you aren't doing well because it isn't about completing the orders, it is about completing a certain number of orders within the time limit.
Then I tried playing the game in single player. Wow, even more dissatisfying. I really wish there were other game modes that let you play for as long as you could keep up with the orders, and the frequency was based on how many players you had. Also, the game really struggles without online multiplayer for people that don't have three other friends around all the time to play. I have friends I would love to play this with across the country, but not many people locally.
TL;DR If you have a group of local friends to do 4 player co-op, you'll love it. Anything less and you'll be disappointed with the gameplay.

This game does an excellent job of combining roguelike elements (map randomization, loot randomization, permadeath) with a post-apocalyptic environment.  As a parent of two children, it's rare when I spend 24 hours (at the time of writing this review) on a single game.
Although I am still working my way through the narrative, I am finding it very interesting and it reminds me of my early days of computing where the story is told using text with minimal pictures, allowing you to form your own image of what's going on.  I didn't realize I had missed that until I played this game.  It's great.
In other games (Elder Scrolls, Terraria) I have not been a huge fan of crafting, but I'm finding that in this game I really enjoy it.  I've found most of the basic recipes, but I have a feeling some more will appear as I progress through the narrative.  This game has changed my opinion of crafting in games and got me looking into others (Project Zomboid, for example).
As this game is still in beta, I think some user interface improvements would be helpful going forward.  Some examples include the ability to easily combine stacks of items such as pills, without removing them from the pill bottles, and the ability to consume stacks of items such as berries (rather than eating one at a time).  Recipes could be streamlined as well if there were a way to chain them together.  For example, harvest meat, create fire, cook/cure meat.  Or create fire, sterilize water.  These are minor annoyances and don't detract from the enjoyment of the game, but could greatly streamline things.
Overall, I really like this game.  As someone who didn't care for rogue likes or crafting games in the past, this game has really opened my eyes.  I don't know how to explain other than I play the game just for the fun of the game.  Rather than playing to progress the story as in a traditional RPG.  Many times, I don't even pursue the story; I just scavenge and try to get the best equipment and camping gear possible.  Lastly, I'm also excited to see what the recently implemented modding ability will bring.

Just like the other 885,363 PC gamers out there, a few weeks ago I picked up a copy of the Humble THQ Bundle. Not only was it a great deal for some games, it was also a way to help a company in need.  Now everyone can argue the ‘Hows’ and ‘Whys’ of THQ’s current situation, but at the end of the day gamers aren’t overly interested in their products.  And its hurting them more than it has in years.  But this isn’t an financial overview of the current fiscal situation of THQ.
This is a Bargain Bin Breakdown, and the game is Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War.  And you may have figured out prior to the break that I’ve never played anything Warhammer 40,000 before.  So its another unbiased review that falls completely on the games merit!  I love it when that happens.  However, with schedules tightening and life being life, I’m not always able to play an entire game.  Its actually a difficult choice on what to play when and for how long.  And having nine new games added to my Steam games list only makes it more of a challenge.  Do you realize I’ve had L.A. Noire for months and have yet to play it?!
But I’m rambling again…
My plan with Dawn of War was to play at least 3 missions of the main campaign then a skirmish as the enemy faction.  This, in theory, would give me enough to rate the games mechanics, story, and balance.  After which point I could continue to play, if the game had captured my interest, or begin writing my review.  Everything started well.  I played the tutorial so I could see which type of RTS this was.  Then I started the first mission.
I was impressed at how well they tell the story with the opening sequences.  Even if I wasn’t really following what was going on with the story, the way in which it was given was very well done.  Unfortunately, to me its just another Orc vs Human story that I can’t find interest in.
And unfortunately I've never had any interest into the types of worlds where Orcs are present.  I am a fan of Science Fiction, but Fantasy hasn't ever done it for me.  Orcs, Elves, Humans, Middle Earth, whatever or where ever it is, hasn't been my thing.  I've played the WarCraft games, I’ve seen the Lord of the Rings movies, I attempted to read a few different stories in the past.  But none of it really sparks much interest in me.  So the real challenge with games of this genre is to excite me in other ways.  Which has happened, but is a rare occurrence.
I can’t find any of the Orcs terrifying, or anything other than plain stupid, and in this game its no different, they just look goofy.  Sure the graphics are dated, but not so bad, and I kinda enjoyed them since they reminded me of Star Wars Galaxies.  But the models themselves, and the designs that were chosen.  A part of my lack of interest in the fantasy worlds fall under technology.  The worlds always look very similar to the Middle Ages, but then there will be some sort of advanced technology that just doesn't fit.
The Humans are actually fine in this regard since everything of theirs looks and matches the advance space faring race type.  However the Ocrs look like a lesser advanced race, until they bust out the battle units.  And I just can’t accept being so far advanced on one side and looking a few centuries behind on the other.
But story and setting or not I can still play a game.  So I brushed aside my opinions of the story and played on, enjoying the games itself.  And the mechanics are amazing.  The first mission did a great job of holding my hand and guiding me through the process of playing.  Sure, I had learned a bit from the tutorial, but had quit that about halfway in.  It didn’t take long to finish the mission, and even take a moment to realize that I have genuinely enjoyed playing the game.
Then came the second mission.  And while I did enjoy myself for most of it, my enjoyment started to ween.  There came a point in the mission where my troops, just a couple of infantry squads, felt so overpowered.  There wasn’t anything they could’t take out in a matter of seconds.  I expected it to be on the easier side this early in the game, but this was ridiculous.  The hand holding was still there, which wasn’t a big deal, just not really necessary.
In between he missions are more story pieces.  And I’m not sure what to call them, since they’re not FMV or cinematic’s   They are scripted sequences that take place on the map itself.  Often before you take over control of the game and start the mission.  It was really well done, and probably my favorite thing out of this game.
I did also love the dead units not disappearing from the battlefield.  There’s just something about watching your enemies slain pile up.  It really brings to light just how many souls you’ve taken in your quest for vengeance.
Onto the third mission, this is where everything changed.  This is where the game got real.
It starts with a pre-built base and units guarding checkpoints.  It starts with you coming under attack.  And the attacks don’t waver.  Now I will offer the chance that I was completely missing some important factoid that makes the mission easier.  But I did try it three separate times.  Each time I was unable to build up or maintain a defense force while also building an attack force.  And after awhile the tanks rolled in, and I hadn’t a chance.
That’s when a friend informed me of a Mech unit that was located on the map.  So on the fourth attempt I managed to hold my ground long enough to seek out this unit.  I found it and unlocked the ability to build more of them.  And with these new units I swept through the lands slaughtering all that came in my path.  And completed the mission.
But here is the problem.  While on previous missions my infantry units mowed through people and buildings like they were all made of paper, now the enemy has tanks and is mowing through me in the same fashion.  Until I get these Mech units, and it sways back into my favor.  I don’t like this.  This doesn’t feel like balance.  It feels like the scales are swaying back and forth.  One side always has an advantage over the other, its just the who that changes.
So I tried a Skirmish, just to see.  A standard 8 team Free For All, where I played as the same faction that I was in the campaign.  It was pretty uneventful, I may have had it on too easy of a difficulty.  But I managed to build a base and maintain my defenses from a few attacks, and then build up my attack force.  Then I sent them out to battle, and they walked right through the enemy like paper…
Now, when I play a mission I tend to have double the needed units to succeed, sometimes triple.  I love nothing more than having units in the triple digits.  Dawn of War, like most others of its RTS type, has a population limit.  Sometimes I can work with this, but I always feel like its not enough.
But don’t think I’m going to trash this game because of the apparent major change in the difficulty curve from mission two to mission three.  Or because the balance feels to be in constant shift.  Because of what I did play of this game I did enjoy.  A lot of this game I thought was great and pretty ground breaking for its time.  I just can’t create any connection with the characters, units, or setting.
But I have no plans to uninstalling or forgetting about Dawn of War, I will keep it there, ready for when I’m ready to come back to it.  But most of all this time spent has shown me where Company of Heroes really came from.  Which seeing as I’ve been obsessed with that game is a great way to open my eyes to its evolution.  Things that I don’t like, or don’t feel like they work in Dawn of War are not present in Company of Heroes.  While other things are expanded on and evolved into better thing

With a bit of spare time I found myself browsing through my steam library. I saw the Telltale game I'd got probably in some humblebundle way back when and as a fan of the Game of Thrones TV series I decided to give it a go.
The storyline is immersive and I find the game best treated as interactive spin-off of the main series. It ties to the events running in the main show and is disconnected enough from it to not know the fate of the playable characters which I am, more or less, in control of.
I am 4 episodes into the game and so far am enjoying it and am eager to carry on. However, unless it's just me being absolutely terrible at the game, I can't help but feel every decision I make is wrong. It feels literally impossible to get something "right". Maybe that is the beauty of this game though. It captures the very essence of Westeros/Essos, everything comes at a price. For every ally there is a new enemy made. For every person you help, you let someone else down.
There have been situations where I've said things in the game and the character goes spouting off about things I did not intend them to say, or say the same things with a completely different intonation to what I was expecting. I suppose that is always going to be an issue, it's like trying to have an incredibly delicate conversation with someone over text message, something will always be lost in translation. Quick time events feel engaging and the sense of achievement when you get it right is good. Snap decisions to be made which have huge impacts go a long way in making you feel more immersed.
My single biggest gripe is that ultimately nothing you do really seems to matter. All you can do is hope to survive through the story and get to the end. Perhaps there will be more branching of possible endings in the last couple of episodes as the workload for the game developers would decrease.
I'm looking forward to playing the last 2 episodes though in anticipation of what is to come, in a story-based game I suppose that is all you can really ask for.

       This is an interactive ''movie game'' you'll be using your controls during action scenes but not just for combatants. The cold hearted narrative and the literal gaming for power and survival and its subsequent blood shed and twists; the formula behind the books and the TV show. For fans, it is a dream to drive the plot at will - or at guts or dexterity.
The game will give you different consequences and some group tree so to speak. Between the forced illusion and real freedom, you surely feel connected but not always in control...  blatant scripts can undermine it but it is enjoyable regardless. I guess we either accept it or backlash to demand better efforts, what can you do.
      The character swaps from each other smoothly as the episode unfolds, just like the TV show. Characters and locations that are actually important on the franchise are present on the game, from the good Jon Snow to the cold Cersei Lannister and also my two favorite classic characters and actors- Emilia's Daenerys and Peter's Tyrion. The new characters, mostly from Forrester family are easy likeable, also for the voice acting reasons.
      George's universe blends references such as the
a book written by Lomas Longstrider the traveller owned by new playable character, Mira. You get to be around more active things such as the imprisonment of lord Tyrion and the Red Wedding event. When all that shows up interacting with new characters under your control, you get that insta-smile. When you die, its down to ''
" as it suits our doom just fine.
      Asher Forrester probably works as a theoretical main character for you if Gared Tuttle couldn't impress you, Asher's insertion and his friend Beskha energy probably will. They're so good and compatible that I already got mines, like the humble loyal handmaiden. Mira has the unlucky role to fight with words instead of swords on King's Landing. Such soul having to deal with Cersey is no small task - and it is quite the scene in-game. The way you can get in or out with Tyrion's evil sister and manipulate everyone from there (if you got the balls) is very pleasing for the likes of me. They're compatible, no silly gamey personas around the classics - they got identity by themselves.
Gared Tuttle, the first character you get to play with is not to be confused with Gared the ranger, the one who dies at TV GOT's episode ''Winter Is Coming'' at the hands of some White Walker. Things got swapped from
, and the name Gared feels just recycled.

Humans are weird and your interests may change when characters swaps. The nodes are amazing at providing a fluid workflow and flexibility, and have lots of room for experimentation.
Blender also has an outstandingly supportive community, with loads of tutorials for virtually any aspect regarding Blender on youtube, websites like
(containing a large, active coommunity), and

providing free and (sometimes) paid guides, jobs, and tech support.

-3D Camera Tracking
-Great 3D Tools including sculpting, direct vertice editing, and many shape modifiers.
-Great performance for even high poly models (Also includes optimization for rendering using Nvidia GPUs)
-Beautiful Cycles rendering engine for photo-realistic renders ( the old direct lighting engine was quite blegh )
-Bullet physics engine for soft bodies, rigid bodies, smoke, fire, water, and many realistic simulations.
-Built in game engine using python (I think) for scripting.
-You can also use a node system, but I wouldn't recommend it.
-A built in video editor, albeit basic.
I can't even begin to say all of them. Blender is amazingly full-fledged especially for being a free program. At first it had quite the learning curve. The old menus were all over the place. The new system on the other hand is wonderful and intuitive (but don't expect to jump right in, read a few guides first). Anything you can think to create, you can make it with Blender. This whole review doesn't even cover how much I love this program.

So, basically you have lost all your memory after waking up from Cryo Sleep, in an abandoned Cryo Facility in an extremely cold Michigan.
You then start looting stuff, most importantly clothes for warmth before the night falls and you freeze to death, then food, and then a weapon to have atleast small chances of winning a fight you might get into.
The game has a very good story line, not gonna spoil it.
What I like on this game the most, is that it's simple and complex at the same time.
That means it's mainly hex 'n' text based, you will not encounter any animations besides rain and snow (if you make it that far, that is.)
And you can simply just go around loot stuff and use them against people and for you.
But you can also do alot more, like for smallest examples, boil river / lake / marsh water to sterilize it instead of directly drinking it and risking infections and illnesses.
Or you could take a branch and sharpen it with a knife, or add sharp objects into it to make it a broad spear.
The combat also, pretty simple yet complex.
You CAN win a fight by simply repeatedly pushing the attack button, but you can also win a fight by playing much more tactically, luring people into traps, using the environment to your help etc, and win that fight even better without any injuries.
You can either follow the storyline, finding out who you are / were, or you can just do open world play and survive in the harsh environment.
It might look like a simple game at first, but I promise you that there's A WHOLE LOT MORE into this.
The crafting system is VERY deep, and you can craft QUITE alot, I'm playing it since a long time (before steam release) and still haven't had every single crafted item in the game.
It has a wiki with alot of hints and tips about everything in the game.
Also, for modders:
It has modding support, VERY easy at that.
To add just about anything, that is encounters, items, combat moves etc.. you just have to add some new lines into the .xml file, and the forum includes alot of documentation on how to do that.
I do recommend this game because it's simply awesome and has a very long and big replayability rate.
Also, did I mention the map gets randomized every time you play (besides the story hexes) ?

Overall, it's a great game to play with some friends. It is best experienced in co-op. While solo can become boring quite quickly. ★STORY★
This is another zombie game. Every possible angle of zombie slaying has already been explored by 10 games before it. That being said, Dying Light makes a good effort at an interesting story. You are a highly trained spec ops soldier. Your mission: to infultrate the quarentined zone, maintain your cover as 'just a civilian' while completing your main objective, which is to surpress any proof that there is no cure for the virus responsible for the zombie outbreak. Of course, as soon as you land in the drop zone everything goes to♥♥♥♥♥♥ You're immediately thrust into conflict between two rival factions that are viaing for power and the ever dwindling resources. There is nothing humane about humanity here.
★GAMEPLAY★
The game mechanics seem clumsy at first (I had a difficult time adjusting to them myself) but you'll quickly learn to master them before the sun sets on your first night in ground zero. Which is a good thing, because night time is truly intimidating. It's pitch dark at night and you will encounter special zombie types that are much, much stronger than your grade A run-of-the-mill walkers. When the sun goes down, you can easily find yourself swarmed and backed into a corner where death comes swiftly for your sweet, sweet brains.
It's a great time, but let's talk about where this game truly shines: CO-OP! Yes! Dying Light has fully featured co-op so that you and a buddy can play the entire game together (except for the beginning tutorial which takes about 45mins to complete before co-op is enabled). This is the best part of the game. It's easy to join, it's easy to host, it's easy to jump in and out of the game, and all the loot is individually rendered- meaning you don't have to share that♥♥♥♥♥♥with anyone!
There's a huge crafting system that allows you to create and modify your own weapons, bombs, drugs (buffs), medkits, and best of all FIRECRACKERS! Hell yeah! It's so satisfying tossing firecrackers to lure a bunch of zombies near a propane tank and watch it explode, sending zombies flying everywhere.
There's a talent system with some light RPG elements that allows you to customize your character the way you like to play. With three main trees to explore: Survival, Agility, and Power. You will earn experience by doing things related to each tree, like climbing earns you exp with Agility, Power is earned by smacking zombies in the head with a pipe, and Survival is earned by, well, surviving!
The parkour system is really well done. Like I said before, it's like Mirror's Edge mixed with Left4Dead. You can run, jump, and climb on just about everything. And the environment can be used to your advantage by pushing enemies into spikes, shoving them off a ledge, or catching them on fire.
★SOUND & MUSIC★
The sound effects are truly great, especially with headphones. Zombies can be heard off in the distance fighting, growling, and scratching their way through the city. Gun shots ring through the air so loudly you're guaranteed to attract a swarm of hungry, hungry hippos. The music is very ambiant in that it's effective in setting the current mood depending on what is going on without being distracting. It's a good mix.
★BUGS & BOTHERS★
There aren't much bugs to speak of. At least, none that stand out in my mind or stick out enough to list off the top of my head. The only bother here is that Dying Light was designed for a co-op experience, something it excels at, I might add. However, if you're playing the game solo, it can be a bit dull whacking zombies by yourself, running from waypoint to waypoint, etc...
It's a great game, and you should buy it if you got a group of buddies to play with, but in the interest of honesty, as soon as I lost my co-op buddies I lost interest in this game completely.

If you liked the "Dead Island" franchise you will definitely like Dying light.  You could consider this a next gen, triple A version of "Dead Island".  There were a lot of things that it did very well but I felt some of the design choices with the mechanics that I felt detracted from the experience.  Overall a very solid well polished game that also has a decent DLC as well.
The Good:
+Parkour/Freerunning:
In the main game, there are no vehicles to traverse the city so instead there is a parkour aspect to the gameplay.  This is done extremely well.  It takes a ltitle bit of time to get used to but once you master it traversing the open is actually quite enjoyable.  There's a lot of "Go from point A to point B" in the game, but the parkour aspect is done so well I really didn't mind it at all.
+Voice acting and Character Design:
The character design and voice acting is done very well.  Very close to games like Far Cry and The Last of Us.  While there aren't too many you can definitely see that each of them has their own personality.  Through cut scenes and interacting with them  deefintely see the subtle sense of despair from being trapped in a zombie infested city.
+Atmosphere and Environment
The Day and night aspect of this game was done very well.  At night mutated zombies that are incredibly strong and fast come out which even in the later stages in game when you have strong weapons are hard to kill.  If they see you they scream out attracting all zombies in the area.  This makes going out at a bit nerve-racking as if you're seen your only choice is to run (or die) otherwise they'll eat your face.  It gets easier later in the game but when you first start out theres definitely a lot of "<panic> <panic> <panic> Run Motherf***er"... "Oh Sh** F***ing run"... "<heart palpitations>".  The first night mission is definitely a treat, a whil
The Neutral:
Main Story Missions:
I really enjoyed the story missions so I wish there was more of them.  Fortunately there is a decent number of side missions which aren't too bad.  I had been warned before playing this game about the short story, so playing the side missions in between each story mission really helped to fill that gap.
The Bad:
-Platforming
This is probably the biggest issue I have with this game.  While the parkour aspect was spot on, platforming such climing towers or cliff sides can definitely be hit or miss.  When it misses, you normally end up falling to your daeth.  I would say half of my deaths were from falling.  When platforming, while going either ledge to ledge, or using the grappling hook, a decent percentage of the time the character would fail to grab the ledge.  This flaw is very apparent when trying to traverse rocks or cliffs.  In addition to this, there is a skill that allows you rebound/jump off a wall.  While it had its uses, it  proved to be more problematic than anything almost to the point where I wish I could unlearn that skill.  Imagine trying to jump up to a ledge but instead of grabbing the ledge you rebound /jump off the wall and fall to your death... smh.  While these are not game breaking it definitely detracts from the experience.
-Camera & combat mechanics
If you have motion sickness you will probably not want to play this game.  The slight  jaring and shaking of the camera when either swinging your weapon( or free running) can make even the most season FPS players feeling a bit disoriented.  I understand that yes it to make it more realistic, but in real lfe our brains compensate for that motion so we don't notice it.  Adding this mechanic to FPS games I feel kinda detracts from the experience.
In addition sometimes when attacking a normal zombie your attack will bounce off them and the camera will be jarred a bit like you've been stagger.  I found this mechanic actualy quite annoying as even with the strongest of weapons this seemed to happen randomly.  Again not game breaking but definitely enough that I most likely wouldn't play this again.
Summary:
All in all I really enjoyed this game.  While there were some aspects of the gameplay that detracted from the overall experience, there were a lot of things it did right.   I would say a solic 8/10
